5nZYvSLKhV.one_liner: Single encoder using separate LM heads for low and high masking ratios in a batch, distilling only the low ratio.
5nZYvSLKhV.problem: Encoder pretraining recipes inherit small-scale conventions, leaving encoders underoptimized, with no single model competitive on both classification and retrieval.
5nZYvSLKhV.method: Studies encoder pretraining at scale (models to 1.3B and tokens to 8.8T per reviews), finds low masking ratios help classification and high ones help retrieval, then assigns separate LM heads to low and high masking ratios within a batch and restricts distillation to the low ratio.
5nZYvSLKhV.key_idea: Mix masking ratios within a batch with decoupled LM heads, so low-ratio examples serve classification (with distillation) and high-ratio examples serve retrieval.
5nZYvSLKhV.evidence: Large-scale pretraining studies on saturation with tokens, masking ratio versus model size, and distillation with pruning, evaluated on GLUE and BEIR (MultiCoNER also per reviews).
5nZYvSLKhV.claimed_gains: Reaches 91.0 on GLUE and 47.7 on BEIR, described as the first encoder to lead on both classification and retrieval.
5nZYvSLKhV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the large-scale encoder-pretraining study is thorough and insightful, especially the task-dependent masking-ratio preferences and the decoupled-head recipe, and that the paper is well written.
5nZYvSLKhV.main_concern: Evaluation concerns: retrieval hyperparameters and checkpoints were selected on BEIR, seed variance is not reported (91.0 versus 90.8 on GLUE), and final-model ablations and broader benchmarks (MTEB v2, multi-vector IR) are missing.

Bd47PXo8f6.one_liner: Counterfactual on-policy distillation that learns a value model comparing teacher and student actions via matched rollouts under the frozen student
Bd47PXo8f6.problem: A teacher step queried on student-visited states can still lead to a worse outcome under the student's continuation, and uncertainty or disagreement proxies do not reveal this.
Bd47PXo8f6.method: CFOPD compares teacher and student actions through matched rollouts under the same frozen student policy and amortizes the comparisons with a shared counterfactual value model. Action-level contrasts guide supervision and modulate teacher distillation, while temporal contrasts track progress along the student trajectory, and the supervision is refreshed as the student evolves.
Bd47PXo8f6.key_idea: Estimate each teacher action's intervention value by matched rollouts under the frozen student, amortize it in a value model, and use it to modulate distillation.
Bd47PXo8f6.evidence: Two Qwen3 teacher-student settings evaluated by Avg@8 on six reasoning benchmarks against GKD-OPD.
Bd47PXo8f6.claimed_gains: Improves Avg@8 over GKD-OPD on all six reasoning benchmarks, with MATH-500 gains from 50.65 to 55.97 and 32.18 to 44.28.
Bd47PXo8f6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation reasonable and the counterfactual view useful, since a teacher step is not always the best one for the student to imitate, with consistent gains over standard OPD.
Bd47PXo8f6.main_concern: Experiments cover only mathematical reasoning with limited baselines, and the assumption that a positive intervention value implies useful supervision is not tested, while the value model adds training compute.

6BgHc3SjtG.one_liner: Agent harness that keeps source-linked evidence and evolving conclusions explicit, letting unresolved conclusions steer retrieval over 100M-token corpora.
6BgHc3SjtG.problem: Agents reasoning over corpora larger than their context windows suffer unbounded exploration and evidence-state drift when evidence and conclusions are entangled in a growing interaction history.
6BgHc3SjtG.method: LongHarness is a model-agnostic harness with Evidence-Conclusion Coevolution, where unresolved conclusions guide search toward missing information and new evidence strengthens or revises conclusions, plus Evidence Lifecycle Management that keeps evidence current and traceable.
6BgHc3SjtG.key_idea: Maintain an explicit, source-linked evidence board and conclusion state in which open gaps direct retrieval and new evidence revises conclusions.
6BgHc3SjtG.evidence: OfficeQA Pro V1 and V2, AA-LCR and LongBench v2 with GLM-5.3-Flash and Qwen3.8-Flash backbones, compared with Codex, Claude Code and RLM harnesses, with ablations per reviews.
6BgHc3SjtG.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract; a review reports 60.2% on OfficeQA Pro V1 and 61.1% on V2 versus at most 23.2% and 5.6% for answering directly.
6BgHc3SjtG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the two failure modes (endless exploration, evidence drift) clearly motivated, the source-linked evidence board a clean and sensible idea, and the gains large on hard OfficeQA Pro tasks.
6BgHc3SjtG.main_concern: The comparison is confounded by tooling (a tool-matched baseline reaches 55.6 on V1 and 53.3 on V2) and by running Claude Code and Codex on non-native backbones, leaving the source of the gain unclear.

XDED9vSNBq.one_liner: Derives PLD and GDP analyses of bounded-range mechanisms to compose heterogeneous DP pipelines more tightly, including AIM-GDP and MixCal.
XDED9vSNBq.problem: Heterogeneous DP pipelines mix mechanisms analyzed under different privacy notions, so composing them through a reduced common representation loses accounting precision.
XDED9vSNBq.method: Derives privacy loss distribution (PLD), f-DP and Gaussian DP analyses of bounded-range mechanisms such as the exponential mechanism, then introduces AIM-GDP (a GDP-native variant of AIM) and MixCal (PLD-based calibration of adaptive mixed compositions).
XDED9vSNBq.key_idea: Convert bounded-range mechanisms into exact PLD or GDP form so they compose tightly with Gaussian mechanisms in a single end-to-end accountant.
XDED9vSNBq.evidence: Theoretical derivations and empirical evaluations on DP synthetic-data pipelines comparing AIM-GDP with AIM across practical settings, where it consistently achieves better utility.
XDED9vSNBq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the exact privacy analysis of bounded-range mechanisms is new and correct, gives tighter composition and improved accuracy in DP synthetic data, and is well written.
XDED9vSNBq.main_concern: The title's 'tight end-to-end accounting' is overstated because exactness holds for individual bounded-range components rather than the whole pipeline, and MixCal gives no way to choose the best budget split.

LXpuTbjZhR.one_liner: Prediction-Drift Round Robin schedules non-clairvoyant jobs from only a predicted job ordering, achieving the optimal consistency-robustness trade-off.
LXpuTbjZhR.problem: For learning-augmented non-clairvoyant scheduling on a single machine, the consistency-robustness trade-off had a quadratic gap between achievable and proven bounds.
LXpuTbjZhR.method: PDRR uses only an ordinal prediction (a predicted ordering of jobs, not processing times) with a Round-Robin-based rule, and per the reviews achieves (1+epsilon) consistency with O(1/sqrt(epsilon)) robustness, matching the lower bound.
LXpuTbjZhR.key_idea: A Round-Robin-based rule driven only by the predicted ordering of jobs, with analysis showing robustness of order 1/sqrt(epsilon) at (1+epsilon) consistency.
LXpuTbjZhR.evidence: Competitive analysis with a matching lower bound that holds even for algorithms given the predictions, plus experiments mentioned by a reviewer.
LXpuTbjZhR.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract text provided; reviews describe (1+epsilon) consistency with O(1/sqrt(epsilon)) robustness, a quadratic improvement over the previous best robustness.
LXpuTbjZhR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper resolves an open gap with a simple deterministic algorithm that needs only ordinal predictions and matches the lower bound.
LXpuTbjZhR.main_concern: No smoothness or prediction-error analysis: the guarantee covers only consistent and robust extremes, so a single misplaced job in the predicted order can degrade performance sharply, and the single-machine static setting is far from practice.

QIsLeS9PxV.one_liner: Proves finite-time convergence for Soft Actor-Critic with a mirror-descent target and compares it with the Gibbs target.
QIsLeS9PxV.problem: Practical SAC performs only a few actor steps toward an evolving target, while existing analyses typically assume policy-improvement subproblems are solved exactly.
QIsLeS9PxV.method: Derives sufficient conditions, through Q-function curvature, for strong convexity and smoothness of the actor objective, and proves a best-iterate finite-time rate when the target arises from policy mirror descent, contrasted with the classical Gibbs target.
QIsLeS9PxV.key_idea: The mirror-descent step size directly controls target drift and thus actor tracking error, whereas the Gibbs target leaves a non-vanishing tracking term.
QIsLeS9PxV.evidence: Theory in the abstract; reviews mention Figure 2 illustrating the tracking phenomenon, with fixed-covariance squashed Gaussian actors and a linear mean parameterization.
QIsLeS9PxV.claimed_gains: An O(N^(-1/5)) best-iterate finite-time convergence rate up to actor and critic approximation errors.
QIsLeS9PxV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the analysis addresses a real gap between idealized theory and few-step practical SAC, with clear, valuable curvature conditions and a well-organized exposition.
QIsLeS9PxV.main_concern: Assumptions limit applicability: the analysis assumes an accurate critic oracle, linear-mean fixed-covariance actors, a strong curvature condition and a single actor step, and the Gibbs bound's non-vanishing term may reflect looseness.

LZRD6K72HI.one_liner: Recurrent policy hidden states act as Pontryagin co-states tracking value gradients, motivating a co-state actor loss.
LZRD6K72HI.problem: It is unclear what the hidden state of a recurrent policy computes under partial observability in continuous control.
LZRD6K72HI.method: They show the hidden state plays the co-state role in Pontryagin's minimum principle and the readout implements control-Hamiltonian minimization, formalized as co-state policies. A co-state loss for actor-critic training uses the critic's gradient as the target for the actor's hidden state.
LZRD6K72HI.key_idea: Train the actor's hidden state to match the critic's value gradient, since hidden states of recurrent cells can be read as Pontryagin co-states.
LZRD6K72HI.evidence: Locomotion experiments including the H1 and Berkeley humanoids, showing hidden states encode co-state information beyond what is linearly decodable from the environment state and that the loss improves policies inside and outside the co-state class.
LZRD6K72HI.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports improved policies on challenging locomotion tasks without numbers.
LZRD6K72HI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the control-theoretic interpretation of recurrent hidden states novel, insightful and well presented, with a simple architecture-agnostic loss that improves humanoid locomotion.
LZRD6K72HI.main_concern: Evidence that the co-state loss works through co-state structure is weak (linear decodability may reflect nonlinear state features), and tests are limited to smooth locomotion tasks.

0r5cUw1jar.one_liner: ShrinkFlow trains a conditional discrete interval flow from protein language model preferences to delete residues under exact budgets.
0r5cUw1jar.problem: Experimentally validated source-shortened protein pairs are scarce, and substantial shortening may require coordinated deletions across several regions.
0r5cUw1jar.method: A frozen PLM scores complete shortened candidates against their source, and the resulting plan preferences become history-action supervision for a conditional discrete interval flow. A feasible action space enforces exact deletion budgets while preserving the identity and order of retained residues.
0r5cUw1jar.key_idea: Convert complete-outcome PLM plan preferences into history-action supervision for a flow over a feasibility-constrained deletion action space.
0r5cUw1jar.evidence: Evaluations on general proteins and protein complexes against learning-based shrinking methods, shared functional-site constraints, and controlled studies of complete-outcome versus wild-type-only scoring, reporting improved predicted structural and interface preservation.
0r5cUw1jar.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the feasibility-constrained action space cleanly enforces exact budgets and that learning from full-plan preferences avoids action-level labels, with promising structural-preservation results.
0r5cUw1jar.main_concern: Results rest on sequence-model feedback and predicted structures, and simple baselines such as terminal truncation remain competitive, so the practical benefit of the learned policy is unclear.

pHoXhu5dBq.one_liner: Probabilistic multi-view clustering model of class-level semantic transitions between global clusters and view-local states, without anchor correspondence across views.
pHoXhu5dBq.problem: Multi-view clustering methods assume a global category has compatible local semantics across views, but view-specific factors can cause class-level semantic shifts that violate this assumption.
pHoXhu5dBq.method: CAST models how global cluster semantics are expressed through view-local semantic states, operating on heterogeneous sample-to-anchor assignments with different anchor cardinalities per view. Learned class-level transitions use cross-view evidence to infer global semantics while calibrating systematic sample-view shifts, optimized by MAP-EM.
pHoXhu5dBq.key_idea: Learn class-level transitions from global clusters to view-local semantic states over sample-to-anchor assignments, so systematic cross-view disagreement is calibrated rather than treated as noise.
pHoXhu5dBq.evidence: Multiple public multi-view clustering benchmarks plus controlled semantic-shift evaluations, and theoretical properties including convergence of the MAP-EM optimization.
pHoXhu5dBq.claimed_gains: Strong clustering performance on public benchmarks and controlled semantic-shift evaluations; no figures stated (the abstract is cut off).
pHoXhu5dBq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find separating the global class from its view-local semantic realization a meaningful contribution, with controlled-shift results supporting the semantic-shift hypothesis and a tractable probabilistic model.
pHoXhu5dBq.main_concern: Only minor concerns: reporting details are thin (shift settings, tuning, dispersion over five runs), some modeling choices need justification, and positioning against robust multi-view clustering is limited.

BA5DBUsGbS.one_liner: Student-teacher patch-level SSL derived from a multi-view InfoMax objective, aligning patch representations across views with information and structure regularizers.
BA5DBUsGbS.problem: Scalable self-supervised methods rely on ad hoc combinations of multiple objectives and stabilization mechanisms rather than a principled design.
BA5DBUsGbS.method: From the multi-view assumption that task-relevant content is the information shared across views, the paper builds an information-theoretic objective that decomposes into interpretable terms. This yields JEM, a student-teacher method that aligns corresponding patch representations across views with information-preservation and structure-preservation losses.
BA5DBUsGbS.key_idea: Derive a patch-alignment objective from the multi-view InfoMax bound and regularize it with information- and structure-preservation losses instead of stacked heuristics.
BA5DBUsGbS.evidence: Training from 300M to 7B parameters with global and dense probing, segmentation benchmarks against DINOv2, and panoptic segmentation against DINOv3; reviews note nine benchmarks and a DINOv2 baseline retrained in the same codebase.
BA5DBUsGbS.claimed_gains: Trains stably from 300M to 7B parameters, consistently surpasses the DINOv2 algorithm on segmentation benchmarks, and at 7B exceeds DINOv3 on panoptic segmentation despite DINOv3 using a 10x larger dataset.
BA5DBUsGbS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the single-principle objective, stable scaling to 7B, and strong dense-prediction results, supported by ablations and a retrained DINOv2 baseline.
BA5DBUsGbS.main_concern: Classification accuracy trails DINOv2 at every scale, and the optimized objective relies on proxies and different view construction, so the principled-design and gain attributions are not cleanly separated.

yDXgQtI0tf.one_liner: Variance-reduced Markovian PAGE-Halpern method attains O~(eps^-3) sample complexity for fixed points of non-expansive maps in finite-dimensional Banach spaces.
yDXgQtI0tf.problem: Block-minibatch Halpern iteration on a continuing Markovian trajectory needs O~(eps^-5) samples (O~(eps^-4) in Hilbert spaces), and the paper shows it needs Omega(eps^-4) even with two-point query access.
yDXgQtI0tf.method: A variance-reduced Markovian PAGE-Halpern method uses two-point query access, with refresh and same-state difference blocks analyzed through the Poisson equation. In Hilbert spaces, cocoercivity of I-T gives O(eps^-3); in general finite-dimensional Banach spaces a displacement-level Halpern bound replaces the Hilbert-space potential.
yDXgQtI0tf.key_idea: Combine PAGE-style refresh and same-state difference blocks with Halpern iteration, analyzed through the Poisson equation, and replace the Hilbert-space potential with a displacement-level bound in Banach spaces.
yDXgQtI0tf.evidence: Theory only: upper and lower sample-complexity bounds plus a high-probability guarantee obtained by measuring the estimator in an auxiliary smooth norm; the abstract mentions no experiments.
yDXgQtI0tf.claimed_gains: O~(eps^-3) sample complexity in finite-dimensional Banach spaces (O(eps^-3) in Hilbert spaces), versus O~(eps^-5) for direct block-minibatch Halpern (O~(eps^-4) in Hilbert spaces), which needs Omega(eps^-4).
yDXgQtI0tf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem important for Markovian reinforcement learning, including average-reward RL, and the Banach-space results general under relatively weak assumptions, with careful handling of block-boundary bias.
yDXgQtI0tf.main_concern: The improvement over the eps^-5 baseline may reflect a loose baseline analysis and a stronger oracle assumption, and key assumptions (Assumption 2.4 on the algorithm's own trajectory, hidden dependence on minimum stationary mass) are unverified.

3GvThWswFd.one_liner: Adds attention-map distillation from a solution-conditioned teacher to on-policy self-distillation for reasoning models.
3GvThWswFd.problem: Token-level on-policy self-distillation transfers what the privileged teacher predicts but not where it attends in the preceding context.
3GvThWswFd.method: OPASD adds solution-conditioned attention distillation to token-level OPSD. Teacher attention is projected onto student-visible positions and renormalized before alignment, because the teacher can attend to verified-solution tokens the student cannot see.
3GvThWswFd.key_idea: Project the privileged teacher's attention onto student-visible positions, renormalize it, and align the student's attention to it alongside token-level distribution matching.
3GvThWswFd.evidence: Three model sizes and four competition-level mathematics benchmarks against token-only OPSD, with ablations on the attention loss and distillation depth.
3GvThWswFd.claimed_gains: Improves average accuracy by 4.98 to 8.40 percentage points over token-only OPSD, reduces rollout tokens by 73.9% and estimated model compute by 72.6%, and trains 1.53x faster.
3GvThWswFd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find combining token and attention distillation reasonable, well presented and reproducible, with consistent gains over OPSD across model sizes and better stability.
3GvThWswFd.main_concern: Comparisons are mostly against vanilla OPSD only, missing related on-policy distillation methods, and the contribution is seen as a simple combination of known techniques.

qTcPvZGxrl.one_liner: Compares moral profiles elicited from LLMs by questionnaires versus open-ended interviews and tests downstream effects on hate-speech classification.
qTcPvZGxrl.problem: Survey-based elicitation of LLM moral profiles lacks reliability and generalizability to downstream behavior.
qTcPvZGxrl.method: A framework combines psychological questionnaires and open-ended interviews under Moral Foundations Theory and the Theory of Basic Values across six open-weight models, then steers models with their own elicited moral beliefs on a downstream task.
qTcPvZGxrl.key_idea: Compare profiles from closed-ended questionnaires with human-rated open-ended interviews, then condition models on their own elicited beliefs to test whether profile differences change behavior.
qTcPvZGxrl.evidence: Six open-weight models, two psychological theories, human annotation via Prolific, and a hate-speech classification task with self-steering.
qTcPvZGxrl.claimed_gains: No performance gains claimed; Kruskal-Wallis eta-squared is about 0.46-0.49 for questionnaire-derived profiles versus about 0.11-0.14 for interview-derived profiles.
qTcPvZGxrl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the topic meaningful, the validation with established psychological instruments and annotators sound, and the methodology clearly presented.
qTcPvZGxrl.main_concern: Reliability of the elicited profiles is unclear (moderate annotator agreement, temperature 0, few seeds, small models), so effects may be context-dependent rather than stable model traits.

WxbKtGW2cU.one_liner: Reduces Nash learning from human feedback to on-policy RLHF by rejection-sampling opponents from a reference policy.
WxbKtGW2cU.problem: RLHF assumes transitive Bradley-Terry preferences, and existing NLHF methods need costly alternating updates or use IPO-style objectives that are not on-policy.
WxbKtGW2cU.method: Nash-RS uses current-policy responses and preference feedback to rejection-sample opponents from a reference policy, yielding implicit scalar rewards for the same on-policy rollouts. Standard on-policy RLHF algorithms such as PPO can then be reused without a max-min optimizer.
WxbKtGW2cU.key_idea: Rejection-sample opponents so the sampled distribution gives implicit scalar rewards for on-policy rollouts, turning the max-min game into a single-policy policy-gradient problem.
WxbKtGW2cU.evidence: A proof of linear last-iterate convergence of the exact update to the regularized Nash equilibrium, plus experiments against a range of recent baselines (details cut off in the abstract).
WxbKtGW2cU.claimed_gains: Proves linear last-iterate convergence of the exact update; empirical numbers are not stated in the available abstract.
WxbKtGW2cU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the reduction to single-policy optimization elegant, the convergence guarantee useful, and the empirical results competitive with many baselines.
WxbKtGW2cU.main_concern: The theory does not cover the practical finite-sample rejection-sampling procedure, and novelty over existing NLHF theory such as EGPO's Gibbs fixed-point and linear-convergence results is unclear.

oGQqebMX4m.one_liner: Shows multi-layer softmax transformers solve in-context linear regression with varying covariance via a depth-dependent gradient-descent variant.
oGQqebMX4m.problem: Prior interpretations of in-context linear regression assume a fixed covariate distribution, and the paper shows those conclusions break down when the distribution varies across sequences.
oGQqebMX4m.method: The authors analyze trained multi-layer softmax-attention transformers through a population-limit interpretation, identifying a consistent weight structure that implements a gradient-descent variant whose parameters depend on model depth. They extend this with a chain-of-thought-style intermediate step to in-context instrumental variable (IV) regression.
oGQqebMX4m.key_idea: Trained weight matrices implement, in the population limit, a gradient-descent variant with depth-dependent parameters, which a chain-of-thought-style step reuses for in-context IV regression.
oGQqebMX4m.evidence: A theorem and corollary give the population-limit update rule; experiments check agreement with trained networks via prediction error and input sensitivity, with appendix checks on higher dimensions, a broader eigenvalue range, and linear-attention controls, plus an IV regression experiment.
oGQqebMX4m.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the discovered algorithmic structure interesting and non-trivial, the paper clear, and varying covariance a useful test of algorithmic interpretations.
oGQqebMX4m.main_concern: The link between the population theorem and the finite-sample algorithm is not controlled, what is new relative to GD++ is unclear, and the paper does not explain how training produces the weight pattern.

kmxFD1i4br.one_liner: Training-free KV cache pruning that approximates KVzip's context-reconstruction scores from prefill queries and keys, calibrated on the first chunk.
kmxFD1i4br.problem: KVzip scores KV importance by reconstructing the context chunk by chunk, which costs extra forward passes, and learned approximations need model-specific training.
kmxFD1i4br.method: EchoPress approximates reconstruction attention with queries and keys already computed during standard prefill, applying a RoPE rotation correction. It reconstructs only the first chunk to calibrate importance scores for the remaining context.
kmxFD1i4br.key_idea: Approximates KVzip's repeat-the-context reconstruction attention with a RoPE-rotated reuse of prefill queries and keys, calibrating scores using a reconstruction of only the first chunk.
kmxFD1i4br.evidence: Experiments on LongBench and RULER with Qwen3-8B and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct at eviction ratios from 50% to 90%, compared with KVzip.
kmxFD1i4br.claimed_gains: Matches KVzip task accuracy across 50% to 90% eviction ratios while reducing compression overhead by 1.7-19.6x and total prefill time by up to 2.9x.
kmxFD1i4br.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is a simple, practical, training-free approximation that sharply cuts compression overhead with decent accuracy.
kmxFD1i4br.main_concern: Empirical validation is thin: it is compared only against KVzip (not Fast KVzip), and accuracy (KVPress/SDPA) and timing (KVzip/FlashAttention-2) come from different implementations, so joint accuracy and speed is unverified.

RKsIvqqtT8.one_liner: Benchmark where coding agents rebuild 20 live applications from scratch by black-box interaction, verified across interface, service, and persistence layers.
RKsIvqqtT8.problem: Existing software-development benchmarks cover only partial aspects of building applications, relying on visual similarity, selected functional checks, or model-based judgments that leave room for shortcut solutions.
RKsIvqqtT8.method: Agents explore a live reference application without source access and reconstruct a deployable implementation. A cross-layer protocol jointly checks interface, service, and persistence behavior, and an automated pipeline generates 1,254 verified executable tests with 20,851 assertions over 20 applications in four domains.
RKsIvqqtT8.key_idea: Checks the interface outcome, HTTP exchange, and database effect of the same user interaction together, so frontend-only mocks cannot pass.
RKsIvqqtT8.evidence: 20 real-world applications across four domains with reference implementations totaling nearly one million lines of code; experiments evaluate frontier LLM coding agents (full results truncated in the abstract).
RKsIvqqtT8.claimed_gains: Per the TL;DR, even the best frontier LLM fully reconstructs only one application; no other result figures are visible in the abstract.
RKsIvqqtT8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the live black-box reconstruction setting is meaningful and that the three-layer joint test protocol is a substantive improvement over UI-level checks.
RKsIvqqtT8.main_concern: The contribution over ProgramBench, SaaSBench, and FullStack-Bench is not clearly established, and the 89.3% validated execution coverage measures test validity rather than coverage of real application behaviors.

zoxktKfA83.one_liner: Reweights pruning calibration statistics using teacher-pruned forward KL so structured pruning preserves teacher-supported predictions before on-policy distillation recovery.
zoxktKfA83.problem: Capability damage from structured pruning of reasoning models persists after offline distillation and can limit later on-policy distillation recovery.
zoxktKfA83.method: ReCal computes forward KL between an unpruned teacher and a pruned probe to find teacher-supported predictions disrupted by pruning, then reweights calibration statistics (using teacher responses and damage weights) to guide existing pruning criteria toward preserving them.
zoxktKfA83.key_idea: Weights calibration tokens by how much pruning disrupts teacher-supported predictions (forward KL, teacher versus pruned probe) before pruning, steering existing criteria to keep recoverable structure.
zoxktKfA83.evidence: Experiments across multiple models and pruning methods evaluate mathematical reasoning (AIME) and code generation after OPD, with a fixed-prefix analysis of damaged tokens; reviewers note only one model family.
zoxktKfA83.claimed_gains: Gains of up to 16.7 percentage points on AIME after OPD, plus improvements in most code-generation comparisons.
zoxktKfA83.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper well written, the method simple and compatible with several channel-selection criteria, and the gains consistent across pruning baselines and benchmarks.
zoxktKfA83.main_concern: The comparison is confounded because baselines calibrate on prompts while ReCal uses weighted teacher responses, with no teacher-responses-with-uniform-weights control; only one model family is used and closer recovery-aware pruners are missing.

7T9SUoz1TF.one_liner: Discounted-UCB data-source sampler plus online gradient descent for group-robust LLM post-training under instantaneous bandit feedback.
7T9SUoz1TF.problem: Robust post-training over heterogeneous data sources must track the currently worst source as losses evolve, but historical data are not re-evaluated, leaving only stale partial mini-batch feedback.
7T9SUoz1TF.method: DUCB-OGD couples a Discounted UCB sampler, which keeps exponential-moving-average loss estimates and confidence radii from discounted effective sample sizes, with an Online Gradient Descent optimizer that updates parameters on gradients from the selected source.
7T9SUoz1TF.key_idea: Treats training as a sampler-optimizer process where discounted UCB tracks time-varying worst-source losses from stale bandit feedback while OGD updates the model.
7T9SUoz1TF.evidence: A regret proof under stated assumptions, plus experiments across SFT, DPO, and GRPO with multiple LLM families (per reviews).
7T9SUoz1TF.claimed_gains: Proves a dynamic minimax regret of O~(K^{1/4} T^{3/4}) for K data sources and T steps, matching the optimal component-wise balance up to logarithmic factors for the undiscounted objective.
7T9SUoz1TF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is practical, easy to implement with negligible overhead, and backed by a clean formulation, theoretical guarantees, and experiments across varied settings.
7T9SUoz1TF.main_concern: Algorithmic novelty is limited relative to UCB-OGD, which is not directly compared, and the theory relies on strong assumptions (bounded outputs, Lipschitz losses, separate data sources).

kcWv54Mm1O.one_liner: State-Equilibration Curriculum advances long-context training stages once recurrent-state drift plateaus, with a context-parallel implementation for hybrid SSM-Transformers.
kcWv54Mm1O.problem: It is unclear how long a hybrid SSM-Transformer should train at each intermediate context length before moving to a longer one in multi-stage long-context adaptation.
kcWv54Mm1O.method: The authors find recurrent-state dynamics rapidly stabilize (state equilibration) while further training mostly specializes to the current length and transfers poorly. SEC advances to the next context length once distance-dependent state drift stabilizes, supported by a context-parallel implementation that removes serial cross-device state propagation and exposes chunk-boundary states as a signal.
kcWv54Mm1O.key_idea: Monitor distance-dependent drift of recurrent states and move to the next context length once it plateaus, instead of using a fixed schedule.
kcWv54Mm1O.evidence: Long-context adaptation of Nemotron-H-8B and Bamba-9B-v2, compared with fully trained multi-stage schedules.
kcWv54Mm1O.claimed_gains: SEC matches or improves fully trained multi-stage schedules while using about 30% fewer training tokens and reducing wall-clock training time by up to 42%.
kcWv54Mm1O.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the two-phase observation (rapid state equilibration followed by length specialization) is interesting and that the token and wall-clock savings are substantial.
kcWv54Mm1O.main_concern: The low state-drift metric is not shown to indicate long-range capability or readiness to extend, and the threshold needs separate calibration, so the practical advantage over a fixed shorter schedule is unclear.

qMK7FrCij9.one_liner: READER attributes responses to source LLMs using spectral fingerprints of frozen-proxy activations and Bayesian evidence accumulation across queries.
qMK7FrCij9.problem: Verifying which LLM serves an API is hard because white-box methods need internals and black-box methods rely on shared diagnostic prompts, leaving query-varying interactions without comparable source evidence.
qMK7FrCij9.method: A frozen proxy LLM provides a common measurement space; the mean (DC) and coarse evolution (AC, via a DCT) of activations along each response form spectral fingerprints. A linear probe trained once at enrollment extracts source evidence, and Bayesian accumulation combines it across observations.
qMK7FrCij9.key_idea: Encode each response's mean and coarse temporal evolution of frozen-proxy activations with a DCT, then sum per-response log-posteriors from a linear probe across queries.
qMK7FrCij9.evidence: Agent500, a benchmark of 50,000 responses from 100 models to 500 heterogeneous agent prompts, with experiments across proxy families and comparisons to fine-tuned DeBERTa and LLM-DNA.
qMK7FrCij9.claimed_gains: Reaches 50.4% attribution accuracy from one response and 96.2% from 100 on unseen prompts, exceeding fine-tuned DeBERTa and LLM-DNA with frozen sentence encoders at the respective budgets.
qMK7FrCij9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the dynamic, query-varying provenance setting is practically motivated and the method is lightweight, with results that scale smoothly with the number of responses and hold across proxy families.
qMK7FrCij9.main_concern: The method is thin relative to its framing (DC-only mean pooling nearly matches DC-AC, accumulation assumes conditional independence of responses), and accuracy drops sharply under domain shift, such as to 33% on Math100.

7NfBEUyPMS.one_liner: Differential VLA runs the VLM every T steps and gives the action head cached tokens plus difference tokens for changes.
7NfBEUyPMS.problem: VLA models re-encode every new observation with a multi-billion-parameter VLM even though consecutive manipulation frames are highly redundant.
7NfBEUyPMS.method: The VLM (System 2) runs on a reference frame once every T control steps and its tokens are cached. A lightweight differential encoder lets the current frame attend to the reference frame and compresses the residual into a few difference tokens appended to the cached tokens that condition the diffusion-transformer action head (System 1).
7NfBEUyPMS.key_idea: Encode a reference frame once with the VLM and spot the difference afterwards: compress the current frame's residual against the reference into a few tokens for the action head.
7NfBEUyPMS.evidence: Built on GR00T N1.7 with T = 64 and evaluated on LIBERO, SimplerEnv, and two real-world tasks, with ablations that reuse cached VLM tokens without difference tokens.
7NfBEUyPMS.claimed_gains: Achieves an average success rate of 93.5% on LIBERO, within 1.0 points of the baseline, while calling the VLM 8x less often; an amortized query costs 1.8x fewer FLOPs and runs 1.27x faster, and on SimplerEnv it stays within 6.6 points of the baseline while calling the VLM 16x less often.
7NfBEUyPMS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining infrequent semantic encoding with fresh visual feedback is sensible, motivated by measured temporal redundancy, with strong controls showing the difference tokens are needed.
7NfBEUyPMS.main_concern: Accuracy drops on some tasks (LIBERO-Goal from 96.2% to 87.7%, SimplerEnv down 6.6 points), the speedup is not shown against a compiled baseline, and the difference-coding contribution is not isolated from sparse VLM reuse plus a current-frame encoder.

xMy1PNPXs9.one_liner: Loss-aware mediator for multi-agent diagnosis that computes a confusion-matrix-based consensus energy to continue, challenge, certify, or escalate.
xMy1PNPXs9.problem: Agents with asymmetric expertise can agree while high-cost alternatives remain unresolved, a failure the paper calls premature diagnostic closure, and no online ground truth is available to detect it.
xMy1PNPXs9.method: D-CEM reads each agent's confusion matrix as a map of plausible differential diagnoses, forms confusion-induced posteriors from current reports, finds the most dangerous plausible miss under the asymmetric loss, and computes an energy combining posterior disagreement, expected harm, and loss-aware margin. The policy continues while risk falls, issues targeted differential challenges, certifies only low-energy large-margin decisions, and escalates when high-risk deliberation stagnates.
xMy1PNPXs9.key_idea: Score consensus risk with an energy built from confusion-induced posteriors and asymmetric loss, so agreement counts only when no costly plausible alternative remains.
xMy1PNPXs9.evidence: Loss-sensitive risk bounds, calibrated decision guarantees, and cost-aware stopping bounds, with experiments on synthetic and clinical tasks (including DDXPlus) and LLM agents.
xMy1PNPXs9.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says only that high-risk misses and harmful consensus are reduced, and its numbers are truncated).
xMy1PNPXs9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the confusion-matrix-as-differential-diagnosis idea is principled and well motivated, backed by theoretical bounds and synthetic and LLM experiments, and simple to adopt in multi-agent deliberation.
xMy1PNPXs9.main_concern: A fixed historical confusion matrix is used throughout deliberation even though challenges change agent behavior, and the component-wise guarantees and the baselines' lack of an escalation action weaken the claims.

Y6SR8urjb1.one_liner: One-shot post-training quantization to a sliceable multi-precision parent model, with dedicated vLLM-integrated kernels for nested bit-widths.
Y6SR8urjb1.problem: Nested multi-precision quantization methods rely on costly quantization-aware training or gradient-based PTQ and lack dedicated kernels beyond single- or small-batch decoding.
Y6SR8urjb1.method: MatGPTQ casts Matryoshka quantization as multi-precision error compensation, producing one sliceable parent model jointly optimized for several target precisions in one pass over a small calibration set. It refines the representation so an r-bit model reads exactly r bits and adds the first dedicated inference kernels for this format, supporting batch sizes beyond one and integrated into vLLM.
Y6SR8urjb1.key_idea: Extend GPTQ error compensation to optimize several bit-widths jointly in one sliceable parent model whose r-bit prefix is read directly.
Y6SR8urjb1.evidence: Standard LLMs and benchmarks (abstract is truncated); per the reviews, accuracy on two dense 8B models and kernel measurements on a single RTX A6000.
Y6SR8urjb1.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is truncated before the results.
Y6SR8urjb1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the end-to-end contribution linking one-shot PTQ, true-prefix weight loading, custom kernels, and vLLM integration is coherent, well motivated, and clearly presented.
Y6SR8urjb1.main_concern: Deployment claims exceed the evidence: accuracy covers only two 8B models, hardware tests use one RTX A6000, and no accuracy is reported at the 2-bit setting where peak speedups occur.

I8S7NFPqML.one_liner: Tactile Progress Residual estimates interaction progress from tactile history and uses it to condition, reward, and gate a residual policy.
I8S7NFPqML.problem: Similar tactile signals occur at different interaction stages and call for different actions, so the interaction state is ambiguous from single contact observations.
I8S7NFPqML.method: A progress estimator trained with weak temporal supervision conditions a lightweight residual policy, provides progress-difference feedback for learning, and decides when residual correction is applied to base-policy actions.
I8S7NFPqML.key_idea: Estimate task progress from recent tactile and robot-state observations without stage labels, and use it for conditioning, reward shaping, and gating of bounded residual corrections.
I8S7NFPqML.evidence: ManiFeel, ManiSkill3, and real-world precision manipulation tasks, with ablations on tactile progress estimation and the role of progress.
I8S7NFPqML.claimed_gains: Consistently outperforms strong vision-only and tactile baselines; the abstract gives no numbers.
I8S7NFPqML.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using tactile history to resolve ambiguity is well motivated and that results are consistently positive on benchmarks and real robots.
I8S7NFPqML.main_concern: Baselines are missing that isolate progress estimation, such as a residual policy conditioned on tactile history or vision plus tactile, and novelty is limited.

Km4psebYZl.one_liner: Shows head specialization in a solvable high-dimensional multi-head attention model is a phase transition in sample complexity.
Km4psebYZl.problem: Head specialization is mostly studied as a function of training time, and how it depends on the amount of training data is unclear.
Km4psebYZl.method: The authors solve high-dimensional empirical risk minimization in a multi-head attention model on a spiked, multi-feature variant of single-location regression (per reviews), deriving self-consistent equations for train and test error. They then relate the statistical transitions to the stagewise emergence of specialized heads in online learning.
Km4psebYZl.key_idea: Locate specialization as a non-analyticity in the test error of the high-dimensional ERM solution as sample size grows, separating statistical from dynamical origins.
Km4psebYZl.evidence: Closed-form high-dimensional theory checked against synthetic simulations, plus an empirical BERT experiment where heads specialized to syntactic relations emerge as dataset size increases.
Km4psebYZl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the derivations are careful, match simulations, and give a worthwhile statistical account of head specialization and simplicity bias.
Km4psebYZl.main_concern: The link between the toy iid-Gaussian model and syntactic specialization in BERT is weak, and some predicted effects (cascades, differentiation without specialization) are not observed or tested.

NS0CAVdGHS.one_liner: GRACE refines a population of counterfactual explanations through a bounded-detour transport so they stay valid after model retraining.
NS0CAVdGHS.problem: Counterfactual explanations assume a static model, so they become invalid when models are retrained, and per-instance robustness methods ignore the shared population-level risk and cost extra proximity.
NS0CAVdGHS.method: GRACE is a distributionally robust post-hoc wrapper around any CF generator that treats the whole CF population as the robustness target. It controls a surrogate for the population's worst-case invalidity under retraining while keeping refined CFs close to the originals and the observed distribution.
NS0CAVdGHS.key_idea: Optimize a population-level worst-case invalidity surrogate by transporting base counterfactuals toward the favorable class with a bounded detour, instead of robustifying each counterfactual separately.
NS0CAVdGHS.evidence: Tabular and image datasets; reviews note base generators Wachter and DiCE and comparison with recent robust CF baselines on tabular benchmarks.
NS0CAVdGHS.claimed_gains: Substantially improves future validity of the base CFs with only a small increase in proximity, and matches or exceeds recent state-of-the-art robust CF baselines on tabular benchmarks; no numbers stated.
NS0CAVdGHS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is real and that GRACE works as a post-hoc refinement that integrates with existing generators and gives large future-validity gains on tabular data.
NS0CAVdGHS.main_concern: No ablation isolates the benefit of population-level over individual-level optimization, and one reviewer finds the math heavy and under-explained.

yuA7HsZIhg.one_liner: Replaces AdamW with Stiefel-constrained optimizers (Skewon, Gram-Skewon) to preserve plasticity in continual visual robot learning.
yuA7HsZIhg.problem: Regularization-based methods for loss of plasticity remain insufficient for robots that continually learn new tasks from pixel observations.
yuA7HsZIhg.method: Uses the Skewon optimizer, which constrains parameter matrices to the Stiefel manifold (orthonormal columns) as a hard constraint, and introduces Gram-Skewon, which preserves pretrained weight Gram matrices for continual behavior cloning.
yuA7HsZIhg.key_idea: Enforce orthonormal parameter matrices as a hard Stiefel-manifold constraint in the optimizer instead of a soft regularization penalty; Gram-Skewon instead preserves pretrained Gram matrices.
yuA7HsZIhg.evidence: Continual PPO from images for up to 100 million frames on locomotion, simulated manipulation tasks, and real-world continual behavior cloning on an SO-101 arm; reviews add an LQR testbed and ManiSkill chains.
yuA7HsZIhg.claimed_gains: Gram-Skewon achieves 62% success versus 37% for AdamW in the real-world task chain.
yuA7HsZIhg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a practical, well-executed empirical study across controlled, simulated, and physical settings, showing a hard orthogonality constraint beats a soft penalty.
yuA7HsZIhg.main_concern: The conceptual contribution is modest since Skewon and Stiefel-constrained continual learning already exist, and the Jacobian explanation is correlational with missing controls such as plain Muon.

29fMCM3wqI.one_liner: Training-free DiT feature caching that stores a compact low-rank AdaLN-based cache and corrects forecasts at test time.
29fMCM3wqI.problem: Forecasting-based feature caching for Diffusion Transformers stores module-level features and their historical states, incurring substantial cache memory overhead.
29fMCM3wqI.method: LiteCa exploits the low-rank structure of AdaLN modulation parameters to build a compact cache with adjustable rank for different memory budgets, and adds Test-Time Correction to improve generation quality without changing the underlying forecasting method. It is plug-and-play and requires no training.
29fMCM3wqI.key_idea: Represent cached features through low-rank AdaLN gate trajectories with adjustable rank, and correct forecasts at test time with Test-Time Correction.
29fMCM3wqI.evidence: Experiments on recent DiT models, six image and video generation models per reviewers (including Wan2.1 with HiCache), measuring cache memory, speed, and generation quality.
29fMCM3wqI.claimed_gains: LiteCa reduces feature-cache memory by 90–99% compared with module-level caching while improving both inference speed and generation quality.
29fMCM3wqI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using low-rank AdaLN gate trajectories to compress caches is a well-motivated, new idea that substantially reduces cache memory across several image and video models.
29fMCM3wqI.main_concern: Reviewers say comparisons are missing against other memory-reducing low-rank caches (SVD-Cache, LearniBridge), the shared-basis novelty is unclear, and gains over residual caching are not isolated since the main Wan2.1 setting uses rank 0.

GpVgI7Kpu4.one_liner: Moves each token at a different speed in flow language models, then distills the schedule into one-step asynchronous flow maps.
GpVgI7Kpu4.problem: Ordering and scheduling data elements helps discrete generative models, but it is unclear how to use it in continuous flow language models whose appeal is efficient flow-map one-step inference.
GpVgI7Kpu4.method: They introduce asynchronous flows and flow maps with prescribed or learned token-wise schedules, with mathematical formulation and distillation objectives, so a single forward pass internalizes the ordered generation procedure.
GpVgI7Kpu4.key_idea: Extend the flow-map state with per-token denoising times so each token moves at its own speed, then distill that state-dependent schedule into a one-step model.
GpVgI7Kpu4.evidence: Training on Sudoku solving and mathematical coding tasks, with comparisons of synchronous and asynchronous distillation (per reviews).
GpVgI7Kpu4.claimed_gains: Claims state-of-the-art one-step performance on Sudoku solving and mathematical coding tasks; no numbers stated.
GpVgI7Kpu4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework is mathematically sound and that token-dependent schedules improve one-step quality over conventional flow-map language models, particularly on hard reasoning tasks.
GpVgI7Kpu4.main_concern: Reviewers say novelty is incremental (it combines existing flow-map distillation with token-wise and confidence-based scheduling), key ablations are missing, and experiments are small-scale.

BDTpce4JCC.one_liner: Training-free object removal for few-step diffusion that corrects the masked clean prediction toward retrieved background using a noise-level-aware weight.
BDTpce4JCC.problem: On few-step distilled diffusion models, redirecting self-attention away from the target region leaves object-shaped residuals, because a structured prediction forms at the first forward and attention rerouting acts mainly in later steps.
BDTpce4JCC.method: ReState corrects the masked clean prediction toward background evidence retrieved from the input, using a noise-level-aware weight that vanishes at the final forward. It keeps object-excluding attention as a complementary constraint and adds no denoiser evaluations.
BDTpce4JCC.key_idea: Correct the masked clean prediction toward background evidence retrieved from the input, with a noise-level-aware weight that vanishes at the final forward, rather than relying only on attention rerouting.
BDTpce4JCC.evidence: Matched single-forward interventions on four distilled backbones, two paired benchmarks with two few-step backbones, an OBER-Test comparison with DesignEdit and Attentive Eraser, and transfer to two more backbones.
BDTpce4JCC.claimed_gains: Best masked PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS among training-free methods, improving PSNR by 3.17 dB on average over the strongest baseline; on OBER-Test it beats DesignEdit and Attentive Eraser at native step counts on all three metrics at more than 12x lower latency.
BDTpce4JCC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, training-free and adds no inference cost, with a carefully controlled single-forward intervention analysis and thorough experiments across backbones.
BDTpce4JCC.main_concern: Baselines look weakened by being ported to the 4-step setting without retuning (for example Attentive Eraser), and a global-background-mean variant already captures much of the gain.

RpWCgmVJXu.one_liner: Benchmark dataset of 115+ hours of screen recordings of professionals collaborating with AI agents on long-horizon workflows.
RpWCgmVJXu.problem: Most agentic benchmarks focus on automation, so strong scores do not show effective real-world collaboration in interdependent professional workflows.
RpWCgmVJXu.method: Kolab collects screen recordings of 50 professionals from 40 occupations working with agents on realistic long-horizon problems, with participants' collaboration and output-quality judgments. It operationalizes two tasks: forecasting how professionals use agent contributions (adopt, modify or reject) and assessing collaboration quality from the unfolding workflow.
RpWCgmVJXu.key_idea: Record professionals working with agents beyond the chat window and label whether they adopt, modify or reject agent output, to test forecasting of adoption and assessment of collaboration quality.
RpWCgmVJXu.evidence: Analysis of collaboration patterns in the dataset plus benchmark evaluation of frontier models on the adoption and collaboration-quality tasks (reviews mention three runs, F1, MAE and Spearman).
RpWCgmVJXu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the dataset of realistic, extended professional workflows across many occupations is the main contribution and a valuable resource for the community.
RpWCgmVJXu.main_concern: Reported results are inconsistent between text and tables, and the reliability of the adoption labels and run-to-run variability is not characterized.

OysGN8qneQ.one_liner: Enables GRPO post-training of deterministic few-step flow-map generators by composing deterministic transport with anchor-based conditional resampling.
OysGN8qneQ.problem: Deterministic transitions of few-step flow-map generators (consistency models, MeanFlow) do not give the stochastic trajectories and tractable likelihood ratios RL needs, and existing SDE-based stochasticization targets velocity-based samplers.
OysGN8qneQ.method: Anchored Stochastic Flow Map Composition (ASFMC) combines deterministic transport with anchor-based conditional resampling. The paper gives conditions under which it preserves the marginal probability path and builds tractable local- and endpoint-anchor policies for two-time and single-time flow maps, enabling one GRPO procedure.
OysGN8qneQ.key_idea: Inject stochasticity into a deterministic flow map by resampling conditionally at an anchor point while preserving the marginal probability path, giving tractable transition densities for GRPO.
OysGN8qneQ.evidence: Experiments on FLUX-based MeanFlow and sCM generators measuring OCR, PickScore and GenEval at different inference step counts, including mixed rewards, plus ablations of the stochastic transition design.
OysGN8qneQ.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports substantial improvements in OCR, PickScore and GenEval, including joint OCR-PickScore gains with mixed rewards, without magnitudes).
OysGN8qneQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it tackles an important, little-explored problem (RL for few-step flow maps) with a principled construction, and that the local-anchor strategy performs well across several rewards.
OysGN8qneQ.main_concern: Baselines are mostly pretrained models or adapted methods (a re-adapted DiffusionNFT) rather than flow-map-specific alternatives such as MeanFlowNFT, and novelty over endpoint re-noising is questioned.

ZY7lWkTa7m.one_liner: Proves exponential free-energy convergence of mean-field Langevin dynamics for two-layer ReLU networks at any positive weight decay.
ZY7lWkTa7m.problem: Standard uniform log-Sobolev arguments do not apply to ReLU activations with weak weight decay, where the associated Gibbs potentials may be non-coercive.
ZY7lWkTa7m.method: For square loss under boundedness, regularity of the activation indicator and a mild initialization condition, the paper proves existence of global weak solutions and exponential convergence of the free energy for every positive weight-decay and temperature. A coercivity threshold separates a low regime (dissipation lower bound from activation regularity and two-homogeneity) from a high regime (Poincare estimate plus defective log-Sobolev inequality).
ZY7lWkTa7m.key_idea: Split on a coercivity threshold: two-homogeneity lower-bounds dissipation at low coercivity; Poincare plus defective log-Sobolev gives a log-Sobolev inequality at high coercivity, implying a PL inequality.
ZY7lWkTa7m.evidence: Theoretical proofs only; no experiments are described.
ZY7lWkTa7m.claimed_gains: Exponential convergence of the free energy to its global minimum for every positive weight-decay and temperature parameter; for fixed input dimension and other parameters the rate deteriorates at most polynomially in the inverse temperature.
ZY7lWkTa7m.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that quantitative convergence for exact ReLU networks with arbitrarily small weight decay is a valuable, rigorous contribution that addresses a real limitation of existing analyses.
ZY7lWkTa7m.main_concern: The convergence rate depends exponentially on input dimension and the proof relies on ReLU's 2-homogeneity, limiting use for high-dimensional problems and other activations.

egoksZ9uKf.one_liner: Propagates prediction-horizon query latents along the instance stream so forecasting accumulates context beyond the fixed input window.
egoksZ9uKf.problem: Fixed-length forecasting treats each instance independently and cannot use information accumulated from past observations beyond the input window.
egoksZ9uKf.method: CoLP constructs context-carrying latents for each instance, treating queries for future horizons as latent contexts that aggregate prediction-relevant history, and propagates them to later instances so context accumulates over time.
egoksZ9uKf.key_idea: Treat queries for future horizons as latent contexts that aggregate history and are carried forward to later forecasting instances along the stream.
egoksZ9uKf.evidence: Experiments across multiple benchmarks (reviews mention eight datasets) with propagation ablations, history and reset-length studies, and comparisons with fixed-length baselines.
egoksZ9uKf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that fixed-length forecasting discards useful earlier history and that propagating latent context across consecutive instances addresses this meaningfully.
egoksZ9uKf.main_concern: CoLP sees history beyond the input window that fixed-length baselines lack, so comparisons do not isolate the propagation mechanism's benefit, and novelty over memory-based methods is questioned.

AnVAiDj4v8.one_liner: Studies fine-tuning forgetting in transformers pretrained on a synthetic hierarchical grammar, separating fast behavioral suppression from slow representational drift.
AnVAiDj4v8.problem: It is unclear whether surface behavioral suppression during fine-tuning coincides with erasure of the latent representations that support it.
AnVAiDj4v8.method: Pretrains transformers on a controlled context-free grammar with hierarchical latent structure (the Random Hierarchy Model), then fine-tunes on a restricted subset of its generative rules and tracks both generation of the deleted rules and their internal representations.
AnVAiDj4v8.key_idea: Generation of deleted rules is suppressed on a fast timescale inversely proportional to token-latent correlation, while their representations decay only on a slower timescale tied to parameter drift.
AnVAiDj4v8.evidence: Controlled RHM experiments with multiple grammar configurations and weight-decay interventions, a theory giving a suppression scaling, and an English-French bilingual setup with analogous results in a realistic natural-language setting.
AnVAiDj4v8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled synthetic setup cleanly separates behavioral suppression from representational forgetting, with well-designed controls and results that support the claims.
AnVAiDj4v8.main_concern: Results come from synthetic grammars, small models and an English-French pair, so generality is unclear, and representation-level forgetting rests on weak probes without recoverability controls.

rOdAP1POZz.one_liner: Tabular network trained with hyperbolic feature-value representations that are converted to Euclidean lookups and an MLP for inference.
rOdAP1POZz.problem: Most tabular prediction models are built and optimized in Euclidean space, and incorporating hyperbolic geometry into supervised tabular learning is underexplored.
rOdAP1POZz.method: HTNN uses a hyperbolic feature-value representation layer for heterogeneous categorical and numerical features followed by an MLP predictor. Geometry-aware training lets hyperbolic geometry shape the latent representations, which are then converted to ordinary Euclidean space for geometry-free inference.
rOdAP1POZz.key_idea: Train feature-value embeddings in hyperbolic space so geometry shapes representation learning, then convert them exactly to Euclidean lookups and affine maps for geometry-free inference.
rOdAP1POZz.evidence: TALENT benchmark with 200 classification and 100 regression datasets (15 runs per model-dataset pair per reviews), plus ablations on geometric choices and feature pathways.
rOdAP1POZz.claimed_gains: HTNN ranks first among 36 methods on 200 classification datasets and third among 34 methods on 100 regression datasets.
rOdAP1POZz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the experiments are broad and thorough across hundreds of datasets, and that conversion to Euclidean operations at inference keeps the model practical.
rOdAP1POZz.main_concern: The paper does not show that hyperbolic geometry itself drives the gains, since the model collapses to Euclidean embeddings and no latent hierarchy is tested, and training is time-consuming.

xScTQrZZ43.one_liner: Replaces PatternBoost's autoregressive generator with permutation-equivariant discrete flow matching over whole graphs, enabling zero-shot transfer across graph sizes.
xScTQrZZ43.problem: Autoregressive transformers over serialized graphs in extremal-structure search do not necessarily encode vertex symmetry and cannot revise edge decisions within a sampling pass.
xScTQrZZ43.method: A permutation-equivariant pair network predicts all edge decisions at once, and iterative discrete-flow-matching denoising lets each be revisited as the rest of the graph changes. The same weights generate graphs of different sizes, and reward fine-tuning improves their value as search starts.
xScTQrZZ43.key_idea: A permutation-equivariant pair network with iterative discrete denoising predicts all edges jointly and revises them, so one set of weights generalizes across graph sizes.
xScTQrZZ43.evidence: C4-free graph construction with generators trained on smaller graphs and tested at unseen sizes before local search, reward fine-tuning, Ramsey construction experiments, and density and extension controls.
xScTQrZZ43.claimed_gains: Generators trained on smaller graphs construct optimal C4-free graphs at unseen sizes before local search in up to 49% less training time than training at each target size, and one adapted generator produces a 137-edge C4-free graph on 42 vertices matching the best-known count without training at that size.
xScTQrZZ43.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that an equivariant, iteratively denoised generator suits graphs and that zero-shot size transfer for learned extremal search is a worthwhile direction, with verified optimal constructions at unseen sizes.
xScTQrZZ43.main_concern: Components come from prior work and ablations do not separate iterative revision from the pair-network architecture; checkpoints are also selected using target-size evaluations, weakening the "no training at that size" claim.

vmo1WFBiTC.one_liner: Benchmark of 512 samples for generating hidden-picture optical illusions, with human evaluation of 35 models and an MLLM-based automated baseline.
vmo1WFBiTC.problem: The ability of visual generative models to produce hidden-picture optical illusions, where a target is integrated into a background and emerges only under specific viewing conditions, is underexplored.
vmo1WFBiTC.method: HiP-Bench builds a 512-sample dataset and runs 35 models across text-to-image, instruction-based image editing and image-conditioned generation. Human experts rate 13,824 generated images on four dimensions, mainly illusion fidelity and shape consistency, and Multi-Scale Distance Simulation (MDS) is an MLLM baseline that judges illusion effectiveness from multi-scale visual inputs.
vmo1WFBiTC.key_idea: Score generated hidden-picture illusions with human experts on four dimensions, and approximate viewing-distance changes by feeding an MLLM multi-scale downsampled inputs (MDS).
vmo1WFBiTC.evidence: A 512-sample dataset, 35 models over three generation paradigms, 13,824 human-rated images, and an analysis organized around five research questions.
vmo1WFBiTC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark fills a gap by evaluating generation rather than recognition of hidden-picture illusions, with careful, large-scale human annotation across several dimensions and paradigms.
vmo1WFBiTC.main_concern: Distance-dependent illusion fidelity is rated on downsampled previews rather than real viewing-distance changes, and the evaluated models are open-weight (many older), which limits the capability-boundary claims.

BwKroCsz1W.one_liner: Maze benchmark pairing each solvable maze with a minimally changed unsolvable twin to diagnose VLM spatial reasoning.
BwKroCsz1W.problem: Vision-language models fail on visual problems needing extended spatial computation even when they solve the equivalent symbolic problem, and show a bias toward predicting that a path exists.
BwKroCsz1W.method: Procedurally generates mazes varying in scale, geometry and texture, credits a model only if it classifies both a maze and its unsolvable twin correctly, and compares monolithic tool-using agents with orchestrated context-isolated specialists using local programmatic verification.
BwKroCsz1W.key_idea: Matched solvable/unsolvable twins with paired scoring expose existence bias, and image-processing tools plus verified orchestration separate visual-access failures from evidence-integration failures.
BwKroCsz1W.evidence: 16 maze layouts and 1,600 matched pairs, plus transfer to MentisOculi with 1,000 puzzles.
BwKroCsz1W.claimed_gains: Paired accuracy rises from 12.9% to 31.6% for a monolithic agent with tools and to 67.6% with orchestration and verification, and with a global reachability tool from 75.8% to 87.3%; on MentisOculi accuracy rises from 58.0% to 71.1% and 73.6%.
BwKroCsz1W.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the matched-pair maze design is ingenious, exposes answer bias, and supports thorough empirical analysis.
BwKroCsz1W.main_concern: The orchestration comparison is not controlled: the verifier can run Python that the single agent cannot, and a single agent with the same checks and history control is untested.

CmIc6pqhwh.one_liner: Balances multimodal training by measuring each modality's function-space response against a unimodal reference and adjusting learning rates.
CmIc6pqhwh.problem: Imbalance estimates from prediction-uncertainty or optimization scores can confuse intrinsic modality differences with progress gaps, giving biased imbalance estimation.
CmIc6pqhwh.method: Functional Progress Estimation measures each modality's update-induced function-space response, calibrated against a loss-aligned unimodal reference. Functional Response Control then redistributes modality-level function-space budgets and applies them through tensor-wise learning-rate adjustment.
CmIc6pqhwh.key_idea: Compare modalities by function-space response normalized to a loss-aligned unimodal reference, then set per-tensor learning rates to realize target responses.
CmIc6pqhwh.evidence: A one-step target-contraction property of FRC under bounded controller-state mismatch, plus experiments on multiple multimodal benchmarks (six datasets per a review).
CmIc6pqhwh.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract only claims effectiveness across multiple multimodal benchmarks.
CmIc6pqhwh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that comparing each modality to its own loss-aligned reference is a sensible alternative to comparing confidence or gradients, with complete metric design and validation.
CmIc6pqhwh.main_concern: The allocation controller's contribution is not isolated from prior function-space methods such as FLeRM, and the cost of 100-epoch unimodal references and the reliability of modest gains are unclear.

gMSqdDEa3m.one_liner: Controllable suite of environments with ground-truth shared latents for studying cross-task experiential learning in LLM agents.
gMSqdDEa3m.problem: Existing training and evaluation frameworks lack shared, controllable latent structure across tasks and cannot measure whether or why agents improve from experience.
gMSqdDEa3m.method: Each environment is organized around a ground-truth latent variable governing structure across tasks, and agent-switching diagnostics compare experience collection with experience utilization. Studies cover frontier-model adaptation failures, post-training on related task sequences, and inter-task feedback design.
gMSqdDEa3m.key_idea: Swap the agent that collected history with the agent that continues it, under a known shared latent, to separate experience collection from experience utilization.
gMSqdDEa3m.evidence: Empirical studies of frontier-model adaptation failures and of post-training on cross-task sequences, on simple text games with two model families (reviewers cite Qwen3-8B and Gemma3-12B).
gMSqdDEa3m.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controllable latent gives clean controls and that the modular, released testbed works as a diagnostic tool.
gMSqdDEa3m.main_concern: Evidence for general transfer is limited: environments are synthetic games with a fixed regularity, held-out gains are modest, and cross-task versus single-task RL comparisons mix latent use with long-context effects.

DHHb3vl8LA.one_liner: Fuses frozen single-cell encoders via reciprocal rank fusion of cross-batch neighbour rankings, then trains a one-layer graph adapter.
DHHb3vl8LA.problem: Independently trained single-cell encoders share no coordinate axes, so their embeddings cannot be combined by coordinate-wise averaging, yet encoders perform differently across datasets.
DHHb3vl8LA.method: Merges each encoder's ranked nearest neighbours across batches into one graph with reciprocal rank fusion, then trains a 1,640-parameter one-layer graph convolution with a variance term against collapse and a batch adversary to remove batch effects. Encoders stay frozen, and adding one needs only a neighbour search and adapter retraining.
DHHb3vl8LA.key_idea: Neighbour rankings give a coordinate-free interface: rank-fuse each encoder's neighbours into one graph, then learn a shallow adapter on it.
DHHb3vl8LA.evidence: PBMC, an immune cell atlas and pancreas, fusing scGPT, Geneformer, a batch-adversarial scVI and a DINO encoder, with scIB metrics, single-encoder controls and a pre-registered test.
DHHb3vl8LA.claimed_gains: Improves unscaled scIB Total over the strongest single encoder by 5.6% and 2.0% relative on PBMC and the immune atlas, and is 0.003 below the best encoder on pancreas.
DHHb3vl8LA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the neighbour-ranking interface combines heterogeneous frozen encoders without coordinate alignment, with transparent controls and component ablations.
DHHb3vl8LA.main_concern: Evidence for fusion over the strongest individually adapted encoder is limited (gains fall in an inconclusive band or tie), and a matched concatenation baseline with a learned projection is missing.

1k9PnfXPSJ.one_liner: Recasts the Lipschitz-estimation SDP as an unconstrained problem that is feasible by construction and solvable with first-order methods.
1k9PnfXPSJ.problem: Monolithic SDPs give tight Lipschitz bounds but scale poorly, while compositional layer-wise approaches rely on surrogate objectives that loosen the bound and stay intractable for convolutions.
1k9PnfXPSJ.method: ScaLip reformulates the exact SDP into an unconstrained objective with a recursive framework that guarantees strict feasibility of the LMI constraints by construction, so the global bound is optimized end-to-end with first-order methods; the authors prove it preserves the optimal value of the original SDP.
1k9PnfXPSJ.key_idea: Parameterize the multipliers recursively so LMI feasibility holds by construction, turning the SDP into an unconstrained problem optimized jointly across all layers.
1k9PnfXPSJ.evidence: A proof that the unconstrained objective preserves the SDP optimum, plus experiments on random networks and CIFAR-10 CNNs compared with LipSDP and other SDP methods.
1k9PnfXPSJ.claimed_gains: Matches the tightness of monolithic SDPs while requiring only a fraction of their computational cost; no numbers stated.
1k9PnfXPSJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the reformulation is theoretically sound and matches LipSDP-level bounds faster, scaling to sizes where other SDP methods run out of memory.
1k9PnfXPSJ.main_concern: CNN scalability rests on unrolling convolutions into dense matrices and tests on medium-depth CIFAR-10 networks, and practical relevance versus scalable Lipschitz-bounded training is questioned.

a3BvZlrSyB.one_liner: Batch model editing that constrains optimized residuals to the key-expressible subspace for same-subject multi-relation edits.
a3BvZlrSyB.problem: Locate-then-edit methods fail on subject-centric batches where many facts about the same entity change together, losing roughly 30 Efficacy points on HetionetEdit.
a3BvZlrSyB.method: A spectral analysis shows soft- and hard-constraint updates are one operator with different filters, and on near-indistinguishable key directions the soft filter discards the residual while the hard filter amplifies it. SCRO reparameterizes the residuals to stay in the subspace the keys can express and bounds their separation by that of the keys.
a3BvZlrSyB.key_idea: Constrain the residuals instead of the update: a single reparameterization keeps them in the subspace the keys can express and bounds their separation by the keys' separation.
a3BvZlrSyB.evidence: HetionetEdit, a benchmark built from a biomedical knowledge graph, across four LLMs, plus CounterFact, ZsRE and general language understanding checks.
a3BvZlrSyB.claimed_gains: Improves the average editing score on HetionetEdit from 36.5 to 50.5 across four LLMs, while staying competitive on CounterFact and ZsRE.
a3BvZlrSyB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the spectral analysis that explains why exact residual fitting alone can fail, and the multi-model evaluation with diagnostics.
a3BvZlrSyB.main_concern: Methodological novelty over MEMIT-Merge and EAMET is unclear since the update can be read as a subspace-constrained, spectral-norm-bounded weight update, and compute cost is not quantified.

upWPVRvJgl.one_liner: Minimax regret bounds for adversarial combinatorial semi-bandits with nonlinear links that keep interaction amplitudes explicit.
upWPVRvJgl.problem: Polynomial degree alone does not capture how regret changes in adversarial semi-bandits when the nonlinear coefficients of the reward link vanish.
upWPVRvJgl.method: Proves lower bounds from a constructed dependence invisible unless all its coordinates are selected, with reward separation measured by finite differences, and upper bounds that reuse observable subset contributions across actions and charge estimation by their magnitude.
upWPVRvJgl.key_idea: Charge regret by interaction amplitude: hidden higher-order dependence, visible only when all coordinates are selected, sets the lower bound; reusing observed subset contributions sets the upper bound.
upWPVRvJgl.evidence: Theory only: matching lower and upper regret bounds for fixed K and N at least 2K for polynomial links of degree at most K, plus a separation example for K=2.
upWPVRvJgl.claimed_gains: The bounds characterize minimax regret up to logarithmic factors for polynomial links of degree at most K; for K=2 a range-one quadratic link has exact-aggregate minimax regret Theta~(N^2) versus Theta(N^(9/4)) under Bernoulli scalar feedback.
upWPVRvJgl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard the amplitude-sensitive characterization and matching bounds as a meaningful theoretical contribution that improves on classifying difficulty by degree alone.
upWPVRvJgl.main_concern: The paper is hard to follow because of heavy notation and coined terms, and the matching results are restricted to fixed K with primarily information-theoretic rather than efficient algorithms.

IkCdUT8spI.one_liner: Tests whether post-answer-newline confidence activations causally support LLM error detection and self-correction, beyond log-probabilities.
IkCdUT8spI.problem: LLMs can detect and sometimes correct their own errors without external feedback, but the mechanism is unknown, and a first-order confidence account cannot explain error detection.
IkCdUT8spI.method: Using a verify-then-correct paradigm, they compare verbal confidence, token log-probabilities, hidden states and activations at the post-answer newline (PANL) as predictors of error detection, revision and successful correction, and add causal interventions.
IkCdUT8spI.key_idea: A second-order evaluative confidence signal cached at the post-answer newline predicts, and causally contributes to, error detection and correctable revisions independently of the generation signal.
IkCdUT8spI.evidence: Probing and causal interventions on Gemma 3 27B and Qwen 2.5 7B across TriviaQA, PopQA and MNLI.
IkCdUT8spI.claimed_gains: not stated (qualitative findings: verbal confidence predicts error detection far beyond token log-probabilities, and PANL activations predict it beyond verbal confidence).
IkCdUT8spI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the combination of behavioral analysis, probing and causal interventions is thorough and separates error detection, answer revision and successful correction.
IkCdUT8spI.main_concern: Ruling out a first-order account is overclaimed because stronger baselines such as entropy, margins or generation-time hidden states are not tested, and interventions cannot isolate confidence-specific information.

imJRHYypBm.one_liner: Characterizes when in-context skills can be compiled into low-rank weight updates, and screens configurations before training.
imJRHYypBm.problem: Repeatedly invoked in-context skills cost persistent computation and context, and it is unclear when they can be compiled into reusable parameter updates.
imJRHYypBm.method: Derives three conditions for compilation (identifiability from finite calibration data, structural realizability in the model's parameterization, and low-rank approximation under limited update capacity), then builds a screening procedure that scores calibration sets, update layers and ranks before behavioral optimization.
imJRHYypBm.key_idea: Measure identifiability, realizability and low-rank representability on the frozen model to rank candidate calibration sets, layers and ranks before any adapter training.
imJRHYypBm.evidence: A fully enumerated space of 90 configurations over calibration sets, update layers and ranks, evaluated on 18 skill seeds with conditional tool selection and field-copying tasks.
imJRHYypBm.claimed_gains: The screening procedure reaches 95% of the best configuration in the enumerated space while using 4.76x less candidate-training GPU time than random search.
imJRHYypBm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated and that framing skill compilation through measurable structural limits is valuable.
imJRHYypBm.main_concern: Behavioral evaluation uses synthetic tasks (conditional tool selection, field copying) far from real agent workflows, and dense notation hurts readability.

aj30dqAbGO.one_liner: Compresses pretrained video VAEs by splitting Conv3D into spatial and temporal-correction parts, low-rank compressing the temporal part, and pruning blocks.
