aj30dqAbGO.problem: Video VAE encoding and decoding stay expensive in latent video generation, and existing lightweight operators either couple spatial and temporal computation or drop temporal computation without distinguishing their compression sensitivities.
aj30dqAbGO.method: Exactly reparameterizes eligible causal Conv3D layers into an aggregate spatial response plus a difference-driven temporal correction, applies temporal low-rank compression only to the correction, and folds it for real speedup. It then prunes blocks width-preservingly and recovers quality with probe-guided feature alignment from a frozen teacher suffix.
aj30dqAbGO.key_idea: Keep the aggregate spatial kernel dense and low-rank-approximate only the temporal correction of each causal Conv3D.
aj30dqAbGO.evidence: Three video VAE backbones on two GPU platforms, including the Wan VAE family, with component ablations and VBench-2.0 downstream scores.
aj30dqAbGO.claimed_gains: Consistently accelerates decoding across three backbones and two GPU platforms; for the Wan VAE family it reports up to 2.24x and 1.11x (the rest of that sentence is cut off in the provided abstract).
aj30dqAbGO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the work targets a practical deployment bottleneck, preserves the latent interface, and backs its design with a sensitivity analysis and component ablations.
aj30dqAbGO.main_concern: The pipeline mostly combines existing techniques (SVD factorization, re-parameterization, TinyFusion-style pruning, distillation), and TLR is validated only on the closely related Wan VAE family.

LN7izBzDyp.one_liner: Local-search algorithm gives a 2-approximation for polytree structure learning with submodular local scores.
LN7izBzDyp.problem: Polytree structure learning is NP-hard for black-box scores, and additive scores are an unrealistically strong assumption.
LN7izBzDyp.method: Studies monotone submodular local scores, proves the problem stays NP-hard, and designs a local-search algorithm whose single iteration is polynomial time when maximum in-degree is bounded; the result extends to functions close to submodular.
LN7izBzDyp.key_idea: Exploit submodularity of parent-set scores with local search over maximal parent sets, giving a factor-2 guarantee.
LN7izBzDyp.evidence: NP-hardness and approximation proofs, plus an empirical check that the number of iterations is small.
LN7izBzDyp.claimed_gains: Finds a structure whose score is within a factor of 2 of the optimal one.
LN7izBzDyp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is relevant and the 2-approximation analysis is rigorous and clearly presented.
LN7izBzDyp.main_concern: The analysis bounds the cost of one iteration but not the number of iterations.

0qELl7YCHG.one_liner: Designs and tests pooled molecular mixtures chosen to maximize information gain, then deconvolutes per-molecule activity.
0qELl7YCHG.problem: For rare molecular properties, existing design algorithms offer little gain over random guessing when molecules are made and tested one at a time.
0qELl7YCHG.method: Algorithmically controlled stochastic synthesis produces complex mixtures that are tested as a pool; synthesis is optimized to encode maximal information, and the molecule-activity map is deconvoluted afterward.
0qELl7YCHG.key_idea: Select synthesis settings that maximize the expected information gain of a pooled-mixture measurement, then infer individual molecule activity from the pooled readouts.
0qELl7YCHG.evidence: Theoretical analysis of experiment counts and simulations on estimated peptide fitness landscapes against Bayesian optimization baselines.
0qELl7YCHG.claimed_gains: Theoretically reduces the experiments needed to find the optimal molecule among d candidates from O(d) to O(log d) or O(1); in simulation it finds active molecules with an order of magnitude fewer experiments than existing Bayesian optimization methods.
0qELl7YCHG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that designing mixtures to raise information per measurement is an insightful approach, and that the paper is clearly written with thorough theoretical analysis.
0qELl7YCHG.main_concern: Computational cost appears high (expected-information-gain optimization and extensive posterior sampling) with little runtime comparison, and the method assumes mixture activity is a linear combination of individual activities.

KmpO3yoSdD.one_liner: Uses solver execution traces rather than scores to guide LLM code revisions, with racing to stop weak programs early.
KmpO3yoSdD.problem: LLM-based algorithm design uses a solver's final scalar score both to rank candidates and to guide revisions, but similar scores hide different runtime behavior that needs different edits (behavioral aliasing).
KmpO3yoSdD.method: A trusted evaluator records when valid solutions improve, how long the solver stalls and why outputs are rejected; a diagnostic agent turns the trace and search history into one bottleneck and one edit for a writer agent. Racing tests new programs on one training sample first, and Branch-Adaptive Reflection changes the edit strategy when a branch stalls.
KmpO3yoSdD.key_idea: Separate roles: execution traces guide revisions while scores only allocate evaluation effort, through racing on a single sample before full testing.
KmpO3yoSdD.evidence: Seven benchmarks with Qwen3-32B and GPT-5.4-mini, controlled studies of MCTS-AHD and ReEvo, and trace-swapping and withheld-trace controls.
KmpO3yoSdD.claimed_gains: With Qwen3-32B it has the best mean score among evaluated search baselines on every task, e.g. a 7.20% gap to the reference on CVRP-200 versus 11.76% for the strongest baseline; with GPT-5.4-mini it leads or ties on five of the seven tasks.
KmpO3yoSdD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating trace-based diagnosis from score-based ranking is well motivated and that trace-swapping controls and ablations support it.
KmpO3yoSdD.main_concern: Cost-benefit and novelty are unclear: main comparisons do not match LLM inference cost, only four searches per setting are run, and the parts build on existing execution-guided revision and racing.

LRNE2HLRvB.one_liner: Casts node evolution on dynamic graphs as a Caputo fractional differential equation with a GNN-driven Volterra memory kernel.
LRNE2HLRvB.problem: Continuous-time dynamic graph models use integer-order dynamics that cannot explicitly encode long-range nonlocal history within a unified evolution equation.
LRNE2HLRvB.method: Models node representation evolution as a Caputo fractional differential equation whose equivalent Volterra integral form uses a GNN for time-dependent graph responses and a fractional memory kernel to aggregate historical signals. The authors prove finite-horizon well-posedness and characterize how past snapshots shape node representations.
LRNE2HLRvB.key_idea: Use a fractional memory kernel in a Volterra integral form to combine graph propagation with multi-scale temporal memory in a single nonlocal evolution equation.
LRNE2HLRvB.evidence: A finite-horizon well-posedness proof and experiments on node property prediction and temporal link prediction against an integer-order variant and dynamic graph baselines.
LRNE2HLRvB.claimed_gains: Outperforms its integer-order variant and strong dynamic graph baselines on standard tasks; no numbers stated.
LRNE2HLRvB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the Volterra formulation is principled and theoretically sound, with competitive results on multiple datasets.
LRNE2HLRvB.main_concern: Novelty is limited relative to existing fractional graph models such as FROND and FADE, and the well-posedness result follows from known Volterra theory.

91itZDpLDe.one_liner: Extends rotary position embeddings to the sphere via spherical harmonic modulation or Wigner rotations for weather transformers.
91itZDpLDe.problem: Extending RoPE to sequences defined on the sphere, as in ML weather forecasting, is non-trivial.
91itZDpLDe.method: S2RoPE-SH modulates channels by normalized complex spherical harmonics (amplitude and phase), while S2RoPE-Wigner rotates features within full harmonic degree spaces, preserving feature norms and encoding relative position through a rotation between local frames. Both are applied to WeatherGenerator, Stormer and LaDCast.
91itZDpLDe.key_idea: Encode relative position on S2 either by spherical-harmonic channel modulation or by Wigner-D rotations between tokens' local frames within one harmonic band.
91itZDpLDe.evidence: Three global medium-range forecasting models (WeatherGenerator, Stormer, LaDCast) covering deterministic and probabilistic forecasting, evaluated with standard metrics, power spectra and geostrophic-balance drift to 20 days.
91itZDpLDe.claimed_gains: Improvements over baselines in standard metrics, particularly at short and medium lead times, and in LaDCast both variants improve ensemble-mean accuracy and CRPS; no numbers stated.
91itZDpLDe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the construction is principled, grounded in spherical-harmonic and SO(3) theory, with gains on different backbones.
91itZDpLDe.main_concern: In WeatherGenerator the No RoPE baseline keeps latent noise while the RoPE variants use zero noise, confounding the comparison, and backbone coverage and seed variance are limited.

9xH6ZcIUv4.one_liner: Benchmark where research agents co-design training data, trainer and inference harness of a target agent under a fixed budget.
9xH6ZcIUv4.problem: Existing benchmarks fix one component or open only training-side components, so they do not test whether research agents can select and revise interventions across training and inference.
9xH6ZcIUv4.method: Five tasks (terminal interaction, software engineering, multi-turn tool use, mathematical reasoning) where a research agent starts from the same target system, iterates using validation scores and trajectories, and an isolated grader evaluates the chosen system once on hidden test tasks.
9xH6ZcIUv4.key_idea: Give the research agent joint control of data, trainer and harness, with an air-gapped sandbox and a one-shot isolated hidden-test grader to limit reward hacking.
9xH6ZcIUv4.evidence: Five tasks spanning terminal interaction, software engineering, multi-turn tool use and math reasoning, with frontier research agents, component ablations and case studies.
9xH6ZcIUv4.claimed_gains: not stated; the provided abstract is cut off while describing the SWE-bench Verified improvement.
9xH6ZcIUv4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the joint training-and-harness setting is useful and the hidden-test, isolated-grader protocol is sound.
9xH6ZcIUv4.main_concern: Single unreplicated runs and uncontrolled ablations leave the value of cross-component co-design unproven, and positioning against PostTrainBench needs sharpening.

UDAmjxuVsI.one_liner: Proves tight worst-case transition-time bounds of order (log eta)^min(n-2,d-2) for large-stepsize gradient descent on separable logistic regression.
UDAmjxuVsI.problem: Prior work gave a tight Theta(1) transition-time bound only in dimension 2 and conjectured a stepsize-independent bound in all dimensions.
UDAmjxuVsI.method: Controls changes in which sample dominates the gradient by induction on dimension and sample size, and constructs matching hard instances.
UDAmjxuVsI.key_idea: Induct on dimension and sample size to bound repeated switches of the dominant gradient sample, then build hard instances matching the bound.
UDAmjxuVsI.evidence: Theoretical proofs of matching upper and lower bounds for every fixed sample size n at least 2 and sufficiently small margin; a review notes there are no numerical validations.
UDAmjxuVsI.claimed_gains: Worst-case transition time is Theta((log eta)^min{n-2,d-2}) uniformly over d at least 2, disproving the stepsize-independent conjecture.
UDAmjxuVsI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the matching upper and lower bounds resolve the conjecture and use new analysis techniques.
UDAmjxuVsI.main_concern: Hard instances can vary with the stepsize, so the bound does not show growth on any fixed dataset, and there is no numerical validation.

9wWU4r3D6e.one_liner: A class-agnostic optimal-transport noise-data coupling that improves classifier-free-guided flow models at no inference cost.
9wWU4r3D6e.problem: Optimal-transport couplings reduce variance in unconditional flow models, but per-condition couplings are impractical for large or continuous conditioning spaces and their role under conditional generation is unclear.
9wWU4r3D6e.method: Global Transport computes one optimal-transport coupling between noise and data without class labels, so different conditions can map to different noise regions; it hurts unguided generation but improves results when combined with classifier-free guidance.
9wWU4r3D6e.key_idea: Train flow models on noise-image pairs matched by one global, label-free optimal-transport plan, then evaluate the coupling under classifier-free guidance rather than unguided.
9wWU4r3D6e.evidence: Discrete class-conditional and continuous text-conditioned image generation across model scales, sampling budgets and distillation, mainly on ImageNet.
9wWU4r3D6e.claimed_gains: With classifier-free guidance, GT consistently improves generation across domains, model scales and sampling budgets; no numbers stated.
9wWU4r3D6e.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the counter-intuitive finding that the coupling helps only under guidance clean and consistent across scales, with zero inference cost.
9wWU4r3D6e.main_concern: The mechanism behind the gains is unclear, and the class-conditional OT baseline is degenerate at batch size 256 with 1000 classes.

l69cFqdnt6.one_liner: Replaces diffusion pixel denoising in randomized smoothing with a single-pass encoder that recovers clean-image features.
l69cFqdnt6.problem: Diffusion Denoised Smoothing is costly because each Monte Carlo draw needs a large diffusion denoiser to reconstruct pixels and a separate model to classify them.
l69cFqdnt6.method: RepDS adapts a pretrained vision encoder to recover, from a Gaussian-corrupted image, representations aligned with those of the clean image, then predicts from them in one non-generative forward pass per smoothing draw.
l69cFqdnt6.key_idea: Supervise the encoder directly on clean-image representations of noisy inputs (teacher supervision, conditioning, consistency training), skipping pixel reconstruction and a second encoder pass.
l69cFqdnt6.evidence: ImageNet and CIFAR-10 certified accuracy against a backbone-matched DDS rerun, with timing and GFLOPs comparisons and transfer to segmentation and video heads.
l69cFqdnt6.claimed_gains: At radius 1.5, RepDS-H+ reaches 64.2% certified accuracy versus 54.6% for the backbone-matched DDS rerun, while running approximately 4x (that sentence is cut off in the provided abstract).
l69cFqdnt6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method targets a real inference-cost bottleneck, keeps the standard certification guarantee, and shows large ImageNet gains per draw.
l69cFqdnt6.main_concern: The source of the gain is not isolated, and the closest representation-based baselines (e.g. rRCM, stronger fine-tuned DDS variants) are missing or not matched in backbone and adaptation budget.

jNPf8vTi9k.one_liner: Training-free visual-agent memory that stores a rule only after counterfactual image edits confirm it relies on causal evidence.
jNPf8vTi9k.problem: Naive memory accumulation in visual agents can amplify shortcuts, with the agent remembering background, style, layout or co-occurring objects rather than the evidence that determines the answer.
jNPf8vTi9k.method: Alternates wake-time reasoning, where a frozen VLM retrieves validated rules, hard negatives and anchor episodes, with sleep-time consolidation, where the agent proposes causal and nuisance factors, edits stored images as interventions and re-answers. A rule is promoted only if the answer is invariant to nuisance edits and sensitive to edits of the hypothesized causal evidence.
jNPf8vTi9k.key_idea: Promote a candidate rule to long-term memory only if answers stay invariant under nuisance edits and change under edits of the hypothesized causal evidence.
jNPf8vTi9k.evidence: Seven visual reasoning benchmarks with Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen3-VL-8B, a finite-sample bound on false acceptance of spurious rules, and stream-order, inductive-split and cross-benchmark controls.
jNPf8vTi9k.claimed_gains: Improves Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen3-VL-8B by 4.18 and 3.29 average points over vanilla inference across seven benchmarks without updating parameters.
jNPf8vTi9k.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the shortcut-amplification problem is well motivated and that gains are consistent across seven benchmarks and two backbones, with strong evaluation controls.
jNPf8vTi9k.main_concern: Baselines do not isolate counterfactual validation from memory itself (most lack memory, and the only memory baseline is unfiltered RAG), and sleep-time editing adds substantial compute.

xiosFQxIoA.one_liner: A learned critic flags when a frozen VLA policy should be corrected and a value function picks a rollback state.
xiosFQxIoA.problem: It is unclear when a robot should keep executing a fixed vision-language-action policy and when it should intervene.
xiosFQxIoA.method: A Critic monitors changes in the success prospects of the policy's proposed actions; when intervention is needed, Trajectory Retraction reconstructs the execution path into a constrained search region and a learned state-value function selects a continuation point. The Actor moves the robot there and returns control to the policy.
xiosFQxIoA.key_idea: Compare the value of continuing the current action with the value of resuming after a correction, and retract along the visited trajectory to the best-valued state.
xiosFQxIoA.evidence: SIMPLER, RoboCasa and real-robot manipulation, with pi and GR00T policies and rollback overhead counted in the execution budget.
xiosFQxIoA.claimed_gains: Improves success by 10.4, 7.3 and 21.7 percentage points on SIMPLER, RoboCasa and real-robot manipulation, respectively.
xiosFQxIoA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method needs no VLA fine-tuning, is simple, and improves different policies in simulation and on real robots.
xiosFQxIoA.main_concern: Retraction resets only the arm and the method assumes a mostly static scene, so recovery states may not match the changed scene and rollback is limited to visited states.

uVd9M8vCJy.one_liner: Agent runtime kernel binding each tool invocation to one immutable code revision, authority epoch and recovery identity.
uVd9M8vCJy.problem: Runtimes treat code updates, authorization and crash recovery separately, causing invocation-level races: checking one revision but dispatching another, rollback reviving revoked authority, and retries duplicating external effects.
uVd9M8vCJy.method: Keeps code and authority as independent version histories and uses a trusted Kernel that admits operations through a fail-closed capability contract, enforces epoch-scoped authority at every invocation, and pins execution and journals effects for replacement, rollback and recovery.
uVd9M8vCJy.key_idea: Bind admission, dispatch and recovery of each call to a single immutable snapshot of code revision, monotonic authority epoch and invocation identity.
uVd9M8vCJy.evidence: AgentDojo with mixed HTTP/MCP/Python execution, 1,146 out-of-grant requests, and 60,000-request replacement and rollback workloads plus adversarial tests.
uVd9M8vCJy.claimed_gains: Matches native-tool utility on AgentDojo (95.3% vs 93.7%), and none of 1,146 out-of-grant requests produces an out-of-envelope effect at the Kernel-mediated boundary under Assumption A1.
uVd9M8vCJy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the three races are real, the problem sits at a genuine gap between agent security, dynamic updating and recovery, and the capability-epoch design is clean.
uVd9M8vCJy.main_concern: Evidence is narrow and the guarantees depend on a large trusted base: a single benchmark and planner, low coverage of representable tools, and many host-bypass variants escaping the effect API.

C17OyHaMmA.one_liner: Agent runtime that holds state as a versioned typed hypergraph and commits model-proposed transitions only after certifying their effects.
C17OyHaMmA.problem: Agent structure (memories, plans, resources, histories) is flattened into context, so it cannot control which consequences follow from new events, a gap the authors call the control gap.
C17OyHaMmA.method: Committed state is a versioned typed hypergraph whose relation contracts derive the scope of change and successor conditions for each event; the model proposes a transition and the runtime certifies its realized effects before atomic commit.
C17OyHaMmA.key_idea: Make relations executable: typed-hypergraph contracts bound each revision, the model only proposes, and the runtime certifies incorporation and preservation before atomic commit.
C17OyHaMmA.evidence: Nine external benchmarks covering single-agent, multi-agent and embodied tasks, interactive service and web environments, and code generation, plus use as a plug-in planning-state runtime.
C17OyHaMmA.claimed_gains: Outperforms popular baselines in all settings across nine external benchmarks; no numbers stated.
C17OyHaMmA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the evaluation is broad with consistent gains and fewer calls, and that the control-gap framing and certification formulation are meaningful.
C17OyHaMmA.main_concern: It is unclear who writes the per-domain schemas, verifiers and invariants, so gains may come from prior domain knowledge rather than the runtime mechanisms.

hjhEzSMEEd.one_liner: Closed-loop autonomous driving benchmark with long-tail rare objects and rule-compliance, moral-reasoning and emergency scenarios.
hjhEzSMEEd.problem: Existing driving benchmarks are saturated and lack long-tail safety-critical objects and scenarios involving legal compliance, ethical reasoning and emergency response.
hjhEzSMEEd.method: Builds a closed-loop benchmark on a more advanced physics engine with rare objects and uncommon traffic situations, and extends collision-centered metrics to collision and braking, traffic-rule compliance and moral-reasoning indicators.
hjhEzSMEEd.key_idea: Add scenarios and metrics for rule compliance, moral reasoning and emergency maneuvers, plus rare objects, to a closed-loop UE5-based simulator.
hjhEzSMEEd.evidence: Closed-loop evaluation of end-to-end planners (a review mentions ThinkTwice in Table 3) compared with nuScenes, NAVSIM, CARLA Leaderboard and Bench2Drive; the provided abstract is cut off before results.
hjhEzSMEEd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark targets a real gap in AV evaluation (score saturation, long-tail coverage) and provides a concrete, extensible closed-loop resource.
hjhEzSMEEd.main_concern: It is unclear whether poor scores reflect failed high-level reasoning, since rendering, object distribution, scenario demands and scoring rules change at once, and some reported scores do not match the metric definition.

2RkScJd7b7.one_liner: Fine-tunes CLIP on targets sampled along the great-circle arc between class-template and spatial-caption embeddings.
2RkScJd7b7.problem: CLIP is weak at fine-grained spatial perception such as counting and judging positions and relations, and existing fixes place a second large model in the training loop and give the text encoder no spatial signal.
2RkScJd7b7.method: Generates one spatial caption per training image offline, then during fine-tuning moves along the great-circle arc between the class-template and spatial-caption embeddings to a position drawn from a U-shaped Beta law, and uses that point as the positive target of CLIP's contrastive loss.
2RkScJd7b7.key_idea: Use interior points on the arc between template and spatial-caption embeddings, drawn from a U-shaped Beta law, as contrastive positives instead of treating the two captions as separate positives.
2RkScJd7b7.evidence: Zero-shot spatial tasks including SVHN, GTSRB, CLEVR-Counts and CLEVR-Distance, with controls using the two captions as separate positives and alternating captions; no second network is used in training or inference.
2RkScJd7b7.claimed_gains: not stated; the provided abstract is cut off and gives no numbers.
2RkScJd7b7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the approach is cheap, needs no extra teacher network or modules, and keeps the encoder architecture and inference unchanged.
2RkScJd7b7.main_concern: Ablations and baselines are insufficient: no matched comparison with LaCLIP, VeCLIP, Long-CLIP, FLAIR or DAC, and no control using non-spatial captions from the same MLLM.

xagiYitqc0.one_liner: Benchmark of open-ended scientific error detection in full papers, with human-verified Gold and constructed Silver subsets.
xagiYitqc0.problem: Existing scientific error-detection benchmarks are limited in data scale, evaluation granularity and task openness, though MLLMs could assist peer review.
xagiYitqc0.method: Gold has 2938 human-verified issues from 293 problematic papers; Silver has 5441 controlled errors built from 527 high-quality papers through a multi-model Draft-Check-Refine pipeline. Each error is annotated with location, evidence, reasoning and type, supporting quality-aware metrics.
xagiYitqc0.key_idea: Score open-ended findings against annotated location, evidence and reasoning with quality-aware metrics, not just whether an error is flagged.
xagiYitqc0.evidence: 13 MLLMs evaluated under thinking and non-thinking settings across 16 scientific domains.
xagiYitqc0.claimed_gains: Even the strongest model achieves less than 50% under the quality-aware F1 evaluation, and additional thinking generally improves performance.
xagiYitqc0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the real-error Gold set is larger and better curated than prior benchmarks and that the whole-paper open-ended setup resembles real reviewing.
xagiYitqc0.main_concern: Scoring validity is unproven: a single LLM judge decides matches and supplies inputs to the quality scores with no human-judge agreement reported, and Gold candidates were mined by models that are also evaluated.

OiHIk3MiLL.one_liner: Native PBR texture generation whose decoder expands compact anchor tokens into denser mesh-sampled features at a fixed latent count.
OiHIk3MiLL.problem: Compact latents struggle to reconstruct fine lettering and intricate patterns, while increasing the number of latents raises diffusion cost in training and sampling.
OiHIk3MiLL.method: DS-VAE encodes material point samples into compact anchor tokens and its decoder expands them at finer locations sampled from the known mesh, applying self-attention before continuous PBR material queries; an image- and geometry-conditioned rectified-flow model generates the compact latents.
OiHIk3MiLL.key_idea: Decode compact anchor tokens at many extra mesh-sampled surface locations with self-attention, so reconstruction detail rises without more diffusion latents.
OiHIk3MiLL.evidence: Quantitative and qualitative comparison with open-source baselines on eight quality metrics, plus ablations of the surface encoder and densifier at matched latent counts.
OiHIk3MiLL.claimed_gains: Improves material reconstruction at matched latent counts and outperforms the evaluated open-source baselines in PBR texture generation; no numbers stated in the abstract.
OiHIk3MiLL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree densification clearly improves fine-detail reconstruction at a fixed latent count, supported by controlled ablations and strong metrics.
OiHIk3MiLL.main_concern: Gains may come from added decoder compute rather than the specific design, since there is no comparison with wider or deeper decoders at similar cost, and novelty over native texturing models such as NaTex is limited.

tBCMCACAfN.one_liner: Trains an LLM with minimum-entropy-coupling objectives to hide 128-bit secrets in near-normal text, as a safety model organism.
tBCMCACAfN.problem: A monitored language model could hide as much secret information per token as information theory allows in output statistically indistinguishable from normal generation, and defenders lack a controlled target to study.
tBCMCACAfN.method: MEC-LLM is trained with differentiable objectives motivated by minimum-entropy coupling that jointly optimize capacity, distribution matching and secret decoding; the authors then study monitor and paraphrase defenses and pair it with a trained payload generator to exfiltrate secrets planted in the system prompt.
tBCMCACAfN.key_idea: Turn the minimum-entropy-coupling objective into a differentiable loss so the LLM itself learns a high-capacity steganographic encoder and decoder without pre-generated stego labels.
tBCMCACAfN.evidence: Encoding of uniformly random 128-bit secrets, text-feature and logit-based stego-versus-cover classifiers, and paraphrasing defenses with Claude Haiku 4.5 over 13 prompts.
tBCMCACAfN.claimed_gains: Encodes 128-bit secrets at 0.57 bits per token; a text-only classifier reaches AUC 0.62 while one using full output logits reaches AUC 1.00; paraphrasing raises bit-error rate from 12.8% to 48.7%.
tBCMCACAfN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the worst-case threat model is well motivated, the minimum-entropy-coupling objective gives theoretical support, and the defense analysis and limitations are candid and useful.
tBCMCACAfN.main_concern: The 'secure' claim is not measured: text-only classifiers separate stego from cover above chance, the raw rate ignores decoding errors, and payload recovery is unreliable with no error correction tested.

0zt41hedr2.one_liner: Links data imbalance to blockwise Hessian structure to explain why Adam, Muon and GD behave differently.
0zt41hedr2.problem: Frequency statistics alone do not characterize the optimization difficulties that different optimizers face under data imbalance.
0zt41hedr2.method: Characterizes Hessian structure by block-scale heterogeneity and within-block anisotropy, then analyzes a two-layer linear bigram model under MSE and cross-entropy to show how input and output frequencies shape these properties in embedding and output-head training.
0zt41hedr2.key_idea: Data imbalance, trainable parameters and loss jointly set block-scale heterogeneity and within-block anisotropy of the Hessian; Adam removes block scales but not within-block anisotropy, while Muon eases both.
0zt41hedr2.evidence: Theorems on a two-layer linear bigram model with MSE and cross-entropy, plus synthetic experiments comparing GD, Adam and Muon.
0zt41hedr2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written and gives a reasonably thorough theoretical analysis in a small controlled setup that isolates concrete hypotheses.
0zt41hedr2.main_concern: The theory covers a simple two-layer linear setting with one-step results, and its link to the preconditioned Hessian for Adam and to real neural networks is not established.

xlq1AuWrfj.one_liner: Training-free text-to-audio control that steers a pretrained diffusion transformer with timing attention, spectral fusion and differentiable attribute matching.
xlq1AuWrfj.problem: Existing audio control methods need conditional learning from scratch or fine-tuning, or training-free latent manipulation, and neither gives versatile control efficiently.
xlq1AuWrfj.method: Three controls on a pretrained audio DiT: Timing Attention Control aligns sound events to time intervals, Latent Spectral Decoupling fuses overlapping segments in the frequency domain for long-form audio, and Reference Attribute Control matches differentiable reference attributes (pitch, loudness) in waveform space, all through a differentiable matching loss optimized by gradient descent.
xlq1AuWrfj.key_idea: Steer the sampling trajectory with differentiable matching losses applied in condition, latent and waveform spaces, optimized by gradient descent.
xlq1AuWrfj.evidence: Comparison on the AudioCondition dataset on timing, loudness, pitch and quality metrics, with ablations of the three controls, joint-control and cross-backbone tests, and subjective evaluations.
xlq1AuWrfj.claimed_gains: not stated; the provided abstract is cut off before results.
xlq1AuWrfj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controls are general across diffusion-based audio models and that comparisons, ablations and joint-control analyses support them.
xlq1AuWrfj.main_concern: Core contributions are hard to separate from prior inference-time optimization such as DITTO, and the timing and long-form components are not evaluated in depth.

88aYUPczhq.one_liner: Compresses multi-vector multimodal embeddings by removing token redundancy within and across granularities, scored by bidirectional late interaction.
88aYUPczhq.problem: MLLM embeddings either compress each input to one vector, losing fine-grained detail, or keep long visual-token sequences with high storage and interaction cost.
88aYUPczhq.method: Encodes each input into ordered global, intermediate and fine-grained views; a Residual Homogeneity Compression module reduces within-granularity redundancy and cross-granularity repetition under explicit visual token budgets; a length-adaptive bidirectional late-interaction scorer averages the strongest token matches in each direction.
88aYUPczhq.key_idea: Rank fine-grained tokens by novelty relative to coarser-stage outputs and keep only novel ones under a token budget, then score with length-weighted bidirectional MaxSim.
88aYUPczhq.evidence: MMEB, ViDoRe V1 and ViDoRe V2 against VLM2Vec-V2 and ColQwen2.5, with ablations of importance and novelty terms and prefix-length results.
88aYUPczhq.claimed_gains: Produces higher-quality universal multimodal embeddings than VLM2Vec-V2 and outperforms ColQwen2.5 in visual document retrieval using only 37.5% of its full visual token budget.
88aYUPczhq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the storage and matching cost of multi-vector embeddings is a practical problem and that results span MMEB and both ViDoRe versions.
88aYUPczhq.main_concern: Gains are confounded with training data, multi-view encoding, Matryoshka training and the new scorer, and RHC is not isolated from existing compression methods such as MURE, ToMe and MetaEmbed.

YMoKcwIb8J.one_liner: Trains generative reward models with a MetaCritic that turns small human-critique data into rubrics for process rewards and revision.
YMoKcwIb8J.problem: Outcome-only GRM training can reinforce unreliable critiques that still reach the correct preference, and human critiques are scarce and usually reduced to scalar rewards.
YMoKcwIb8J.method: A training-time MetaCritic learned from a small set of human critiques builds response-specific rubrics and scores the evidence coverage and correctness of generated critiques, giving process rewards and guidance for exploring better critiques; MetaCritic is further optimized to generalize to outcome-only preference data.
YMoKcwIb8J.key_idea: Use a rubric-generating MetaCritic, learned from few human critiques, for keypoint-level credit assignment and guided revision of failed critiques during GRM training.
YMoKcwIb8J.evidence: Seven main benchmarks with Qwen3-4B and Gemma3-12B backbones, plus critique-quality, downstream policy optimization and ablation evaluations.
YMoKcwIb8J.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract; a review reports seven-benchmark averages rising from 66.25 to 69.22 (Qwen3-4B) and from 67.21 to 70.32 (Gemma3-12B) over RM-NLHF.
YMoKcwIb8J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that keypoint-level supervision addresses the weakness of outcome-only GRM training and that MetaCritic is used only at training time.
YMoKcwIb8J.main_concern: Rubric reliability depends on an unvalidated external teacher, and the added computation is not controlled against compute-matched or unguided-revision baselines.

dU4zopYSE7.one_liner: Models occluded views in multi-view 3D grounding as censored evidence with a three-component likelihood distinguishing partial and full occlusion.
dU4zopYSE7.problem: A low language-conditioned response can mean a surface is not the referent or is occluded, and conflating them dilutes valid evidence or accumulates spurious contradiction.
dU4zopYSE7.method: Fusion is formulated as censored observation modeling that marginalizes uncertain track-view validity; a three-component likelihood keeps partial-occlusion evidence and approximates full occlusion with a shared nuisance density, and a spatial gate removes instance-grouping labels from inference with frozen backbones.
dU4zopYSE7.key_idea: Treat full occlusion as uninformative censoring via a shared nuisance density, but keep partial-occlusion responses as semantic evidence in the fusion likelihood.
dU4zopYSE7.evidence: The VisCen3D diagnostic benchmark with exact visibility and occlusion-type labels, a preregistered evaluation on 160 fresh scenes and 882 episodes, plus Replica and ScanNet++ tests.
dU4zopYSE7.claimed_gains: Grouping-free fusion on analytic tracks improves AUROC on the most-occluded surface tercile by +0.050 under Stable Diffusion and +0.041 under SigLIP over development-selected non-censored comparators.
dU4zopYSE7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the partial versus full occlusion distinction is empirically motivated and that the preregistered, candidly reported evaluation is rigorous.
dU4zopYSE7.main_concern: Gains are confined to synthetic scenes with analytic tracks, reverse on ScanNet++ and with mask-crop readouts, and lack a spatial-smoothing baseline to attribute them to the likelihood.

V2B53OQXU5.one_liner: Applies vector quantization only to the lowest-resolution first-coded latents to guide hyperprior and context entropy modeling in learned image compression.
V2B53OQXU5.problem: Full VQ in learned image compression has exponentially growing codebooks, hard optimization and codebook collapse, while first-coded latents have no decoded context.
V2B53OQXU5.method: VQPM vector-quantizes a subset of the lowest-resolution latents coded first, uses them as global structural guidance for the hyperprior and contextual prior, and trains the codebook with end-to-end rate-distortion gradients.
V2B53OQXU5.key_idea: Quantize only the context-free first-coded low-resolution latents with VQ so it models intra-vector dependencies, then condition later priors on them.
V2B53OQXU5.evidence: Rate-distortion experiments on learned image compression (details cut off in the abstract), with reviewers describing HPCM as the strong baseline and comparing against standard VQ training.
V2B53OQXU5.claimed_gains: not stated; the provided abstract is cut off after claiming state-of-the-art rate-distortion performance.
V2B53OQXU5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is sensible and that restricting VQ to the first-coded, context-poor latents is a well-targeted, simple idea that improves a strong baseline.
V2B53OQXU5.main_concern: Comparisons are incomplete: related self-generated priors and recent VQ training methods (rotation trick, DiVeQ, SimVQ) are not compared, and the gain is judged modest.

r7nNoEWw79.one_liner: Robust in-the-wild 3D Gaussian Splatting that masks unreliable pixels and rotates conflicting view gradients into an orthogonal configuration.
r7nNoEWw79.problem: Image-level masking cannot fully remove residual occlusions or illumination-induced inconsistencies, which leave conflicting cross-view gradients that destabilize Gaussian optimization and cause artifacts.
r7nNoEWw79.method: Semantic Consistency-Guided Masking learns pixel-wise consistency scores to refine prior masks; dual-view Conflict-Aware Gradient Harmonization mutually rotates view-specific gradients into an orthogonal configuration; conflict-aware densification and pruning stabilize Gaussian growth and remove persistently conflicting primitives.
r7nNoEWw79.key_idea: When two views' gradients conflict, mutually rotate them into an orthogonal pair before combining, and use conflict signals to guide densification and pruning.
r7nNoEWw79.evidence: Standard in-the-wild benchmarks, with AsymGS as the main baseline according to reviewers.
r7nNoEWw79.claimed_gains: Reports the best rendering quality under complex transient distractors and cross-view inconsistencies on standard in-the-wild benchmarks; no numbers stated.
r7nNoEWw79.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that handling cross-view conflicts at the gradient level is more targeted than masking alone and that the experimental validation is comprehensive.
r7nNoEWw79.main_concern: The gradient-conflict motivation is debatable (negative inner products occur in normal multi-view optimization) and gains over the AsymGS baseline are marginal on some datasets.

RipkxkiNlV.one_liner: Training-free cache reuses deep transformer features of previously seen regions across point-cloud frames so those tokens skip blocks.
RipkxkiNlV.problem: Point-cloud segmentation networks process every frame from scratch although consecutive frames largely overlap.
RipkxkiNlV.method: Tokens of previously observed regions skip a sequence of transformer blocks and take cached features, only the remaining tokens are computed, and the full token layout is restored for dense prediction; cache management limits each entry's age and evicts low-confidence entries, with operations run once per encoder stage.
RipkxkiNlV.key_idea: Intermediate transformer features stay semantically consistent across frames for the same spatial region, so cache them by location and reuse deep-stage features for revisited regions.
RipkxkiNlV.evidence: nuScenes, Waymo and ScanNet with Utonia and LitePT-B backbones, against token-merging methods.
RipkxkiNlV.claimed_gains: Up to 1.65x speedup with less than 1-point mIoU drop, and consistently outperforms token-merging methods.
RipkxkiNlV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method needs no retraining, plugs into pretrained backbones and gives real speedups with small accuracy loss.
RipkxkiNlV.main_concern: The outdoor evaluation uses ground-truth ignore labels to filter cache entries and operating points are picked on the evaluation set, so deployment-time gains are unclear.

OlVSBh5bcS.one_liner: LLM heuristic evolution paired with an LLM-free inner loop that searches worst-case instances in an epsilon-ball around training data.
OlVSBh5bcS.problem: LLM-based automated heuristic design optimizes on a fixed training instance set and can fail catastrophically under real-world distribution shift.
OlVSBh5bcS.method: An inner LLM-free loop repeatedly finds hard instances inside an epsilon-ball around the training set using a basis distribution parameterization with boundary projection, and an outer LLM-driven loop evolves heuristics to optimize aggregate performance over the accumulated hard-instance set.
OlVSBh5bcS.key_idea: Accumulate adversarial instances found by constrained worst-case search near the training set and evolve heuristics against that growing hard set.
OlVSBh5bcS.evidence: Four combinatorial optimization tasks, five distribution families, twelve size configurations and 95 test datasets, against LLM-based AHD baselines including the robustness-aware EoH-S.
OlVSBh5bcS.claimed_gains: Existing LLM-based AHD methods degrade by up to 19x under distribution shift, while RAISE attains the best average shifted performance among the nominal-trained learned baselines and is on par with EoH-S.
OlVSBh5bcS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the robustness problem is well motivated and that the inner search needs no extra LLM calls and is easy to integrate.
OlVSBh5bcS.main_concern: Ablations do not separate active adversarial search from simple training-set expansion, as a matched random-augmentation control is missing.

mXWoxaGyMX.one_liner: Shows sentence-pair meaning identity is read far better from joint forward passes than from independently encoded sentence embeddings.
mXWoxaGyMX.problem: Retrieval and RAG treat meaning identity as a geometric property of independently encoded sentence vectors, but it may not be readable from them.
mXWoxaGyMX.method: Compares linear probes on frozen joint forward passes of both sentences with nonlinear readers of independent states on PAWS, then repeats across 30 decoder checkpoints, encoders, encoder-decoders, rerankers, languages and controlled relation tasks.
mXWoxaGyMX.key_idea: Meaning identity is computed when both sentences share one forward pass, so joint-pass readouts expose it while independent embeddings do not.
mXWoxaGyMX.evidence: A 2,000-pair PAWS test set with 49,258 training pairs, a 30-checkpoint decoder survey, bidirectional and encoder-decoder models, BGE, MS-MARCO and Jina rerankers, and cross-language and nonce controls.
mXWoxaGyMX.claimed_gains: Linear readouts of four frozen joint passes reach AUC 0.900-0.946 with 1,200 labels versus 0.622-0.646 for independent readers, and 0.922-0.960 versus 0.736-0.786 with all 49,258 training pairs.
mXWoxaGyMX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the empirical evidence for the joint-over-independent gap is comprehensive across architectures, with shuffle and shared-index controls reducing confounds.
mXWoxaGyMX.main_concern: The comparison is not compute-matched and independent readers may be under-trained, so the gap may reflect pretrained pairwise computation or probe optimization rather than representational accessibility.

yy35XVKUj3.one_liner: Adds a fixed duplicated-latent residual to low-rank layers during pre-training, then folds it into the up-projection afterward.
yy35XVKUj3.problem: Low-rank pre-training cuts parameters and FLOPs but typically lags full-rank training in quality.
yy35XVKUj3.method: DLR augments the low-rank output with a fixed structured residual that replicates each latent coordinate across the output dimension, adding no learnable parameters at a fixed scale; after training the residual is absorbed into the up-projection in closed form, so deployed parameters, FLOPs and memory match the low-rank backbone.
yy35XVKUj3.key_idea: Replicate each latent coordinate across the output dimension as a fixed residual during training, then fold it exactly into the up-projection for deployment.
yy35XVKUj3.evidence: LLaMA models from 60M to 7B parameters on C4 validation perplexity, plus supervised fine-tuning of folded checkpoints on standard benchmarks and combination with low-rank methods such as CoLA and LOST.
yy35XVKUj3.claimed_gains: Consistently strengthens low-rank pre-training on C4 validation perplexity across LLaMA models from 60M to 7B parameters; no perplexity numbers stated.
yy35XVKUj3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the fold-away property is exact, the plug-in is simple and compatible with many low-rank methods, and results are consistent.
yy35XVKUj3.main_concern: The true gain is unclear: the benefit may reflect a change in regularization, baseline numbers may not be reproduced under the same setup, and self-guided training and Spectron are missing as baselines.

4aAG3Km8uO.one_liner: Interactive simulated-laboratory benchmark where LLMs design experiments sequentially to identify a hidden chemical.
4aAG3Km8uO.problem: It is unclear whether LLMs can solve chemistry problems whose answers must be discovered through experimentation rather than recalled.
4aAG3Km8uO.method: ChemDeduce casts unknown chemical identification as a sequential decision process in a stateful simulated laboratory with explicit instrument and operational constraints. Models choose experiments, interpret observations, update hypotheses, and name the hidden substance.
4aAG3Km8uO.key_idea: A stateful simulated lab with instrument constraints forces models to pick each experiment from earlier observations, scoring identification, compliance, efficiency and trajectory reasoning.
4aAG3Km8uO.evidence: Eight frontier LLMs are evaluated on 200 chemicals, giving 1,600 model-target pairs and 4,800 episodes over three independent repetitions.
4aAG3Km8uO.claimed_gains: Average identification accuracy of current models ranges from 23.83% to 67.33%.
4aAG3Km8uO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the stable, reproducible, scalable interactive evaluation environment and the expert-checked simulator covering chemical knowledge, experiment design and result interpretation.
4aAG3Km8uO.main_concern: Scores do not clearly separate poor experiment choice from wrong conclusions, and human validation (majority-vote filtering, unclear expert qualifications, no comparison of automated and human scores) is weak.

JgRSZPpRld.one_liner: Sets per-parameter Gaussian prior precision in mean-field Bayesian neural networks from pruning sensitivity of a pretrained network.
JgRSZPpRld.problem: Priors over Bayesian neural network parameters strongly affect performance, but large parameter spaces make it hard to judge each parameter's functional importance tractably.
JgRSZPpRld.method: They compute continuous pruning sensitivity of each parameter in a pretrained deterministic network and use it to allocate Gaussian prior precision across parameters under mean-field variational inference (MFVI).
JgRSZPpRld.key_idea: Parameter-wise Gaussian prior precision is set from continuous pruning sensitivity of a pretrained deterministic network, replacing marginal-likelihood-based precision selection under MFVI.
JgRSZPpRld.evidence: Experiments across architectures (CNN and ViT per reviewers), datasets and prior configurations, measuring calibration and OOD detection, plus a local analysis of how prior precision affects posterior mean and variance.
JgRSZPpRld.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem clear and important, the pruning-sensitivity prior idea elegant, the exposition clear, and the experiments thorough with theoretical motivation.
JgRSZPpRld.main_concern: Claims are restricted to mean-field variational inference, and reviewers ask for correlated posteriors or other inference methods and note the prior effectively conditions on the data twice.

qtGqPwi2YZ.one_liner: Long-video agent delegates each local retrieval objective to a dedicated agent that audits itself before handing back evidence.
qtGqPwi2YZ.problem: Existing agentic long-video methods return control to global reasoning after every retrieval action, even when that action only narrowed a region or hinted at the next step.
qtGqPwi2YZ.method: When global reasoning finds an information gap, it delegates a local retrieval objective to a dedicated retrieval agent. Within a bounded local scope the agent runs multiple retrieval actions with an explicit local audit after each, keeps intermediate states local, and returns only acquired observations and their sources.
qtGqPwi2YZ.key_idea: Retrieval per local objective becomes a persistent process with explicit local audit after each action, and only selected observations and source information return to global reasoning.
qtGqPwi2YZ.evidence: Four long-video understanding benchmarks, plus ablations comparing action return, terminate status and persistent local retrieval.
qtGqPwi2YZ.claimed_gains: Average accuracy of 82.0% across four long-video benchmarks, a 3.4 percentage point improvement (reviewers say over the leading published agent).
qtGqPwi2YZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the separation of local retrieval adequacy from global answer sufficiency is well motivated and that the ablation of persistent local retrieval against action return and status feedback is fairly convincing.
qtGqPwi2YZ.main_concern: The headline comparison is cross-system (different backbones, inputs and budgets) and ablations do not isolate mechanisms, and novelty over VideoExplorer, REVEAL and VideoSEAL is unclear.

YVFHX1pSXi.one_liner: Shows chat-template prompt injection draws authority from reserved-token embeddings by sending identical bytes as ordinary subwords instead.
YVFHX1pSXi.problem: It is unclear how much of a forged chat-template marker's injection strength comes from the reserved control token's learned representation rather than its text, since the two are normally varied together.
YVFHX1pSXi.method: They encode forged markers such as <|im_start|> either as a single reserved token or as ordinary subwords with the text held fixed and a control for the extra tokens, then run embedding-replacement experiments and an adaptive attacker search for non-reserved markers. They also survey tokenizer configurations for coverage by the standard mitigation.
YVFHX1pSXi.key_idea: Hold forged-marker text fixed while switching between a reserved token id and ordinary subword ids, isolating the learned vector at the marker position as the source of authority.
YVFHX1pSXi.evidence: InjecAgent across four open-weight families and multi-turn AgentDojo tasks, plus embedding-replacement experiments, a Qwen3-8B reasoning-suppression test, and an adaptive attacker search.
YVFHX1pSXi.claimed_gains: Subword encoding lowers attack success on InjecAgent by 39 to 66 percentage points on three of four open-weight families; on Qwen3-8B the gap is 8 points, widening to 50 when the reasoning block is suppressed.
YVFHX1pSXi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the clean controlled contrast that separates token ids from text and the tokenizer-configuration census showing tool-protocol tokens fall outside the standard mitigation.
YVFHX1pSXi.main_concern: Overlap with ChatInject and limited practical impact: only small models are tested, the source-aware defense is not evaluated against the adaptive attacker, and the attack class is niche.

egN29LQsiE.one_liner: Benchmark of seven language-guided multi-view generation tasks testing generative spatial intelligence from partial multi-view observations.
egN29LQsiE.problem: Language-guided generation of spatially consistent views from partial multi-view observations is underexplored as a measure of spatial intelligence.
egN29LQsiE.method: MindView has 1,500 samples from 513 scenes across three indoor datasets, with seven tasks in two families: geometry-dominant (camera position and orientation changes) and semantics-dominant (inferring target viewpoints from referred objects, spatial relations and reference frames). They evaluate eleven generators and fine-tune BAGEL on a MindView training set.
egN29LQsiE.key_idea: Seven tasks split into geometry-dominant camera-change and semantics-dominant viewpoint-inference families, scored against captured target images with VLM judging and VGGT-based pose evaluation.
egN29LQsiE.evidence: Evaluation of eleven generators, a paired context analysis with expanded context, BAGEL fine-tuning, and transfer to three spatial-understanding benchmarks; reviewers cite 92.4% VLM-human ranking agreement over 210 samples.
egN29LQsiE.claimed_gains: Fine-tuning BAGEL on the MindView training data improves its overall score by 24.3 points, with gains across all seven tasks.
egN29LQsiE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the seven-task design is valuable and the benchmark construction and evaluation (VLM and human agreement, pose stability tests) are careful, revealing limits such as lower scores under expanded context.
egN29LQsiE.main_concern: The 24.3-point BAGEL gain may be in-distribution adaptation (same datasets and instruction templates), and single-target-image scoring may penalize valid alternative views.

7H6zX1uj86.one_liner: Learns a Mahalanobis ground cost for optimal-transport conformal prediction to minimize prediction-set volume.
7H6zX1uj86.problem: OT-based multivariate conformal prediction uses a fixed Euclidean transport cost, which can give prediction sets with larger volume than necessary.
7H6zX1uj86.method: Minimum-Volume OTCP learns a Mahalanobis ground cost over positive-definite metrics, using a metric Brenier representation to write a volume objective that depends explicitly on the cost matrix and is optimized jointly with the transport map. An individualized extension learns covariate-dependent metrics.
7H6zX1uj86.key_idea: Parameterize the OT ground cost as a learnable Mahalanobis matrix and minimize region volume through the change-of-variables objective given by the metric Brenier representation.
7H6zX1uj86.evidence: Finite-sample marginal coverage and volume-metric optimality within the metric class, asymptotic conditional coverage for the individualized extension, plus simulations and real-data experiments.
7H6zX1uj86.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea natural and well motivated, with a clean geometric characterization of volume through the metric Brenier Jacobian, including an elliptical-score example where the identity metric is volume-suboptimal.
7H6zX1uj86.main_concern: Real-data evidence omits OT baselines and the identity-metric ablation, and the bilevel neural procedure is costly while a closed-form whitening metric is not evaluated as a baseline and runtimes are not reported.

hK7GTDoH9p.one_liner: Identifies a dominant-singular-mode-then-recovery signature in the Jacobian spectrum marking memorization basin entry in diffusion models.
hK7GTDoH9p.problem: Basin entry along trained diffusion trajectories and the formation of memorization basins are largely uncharacterized, since prior work focused on classifier-free-guidance-based detection and mitigation in text-to-image models.
hK7GTDoH9p.method: They analyze the local spectrum of the function Jacobian for conditional, unconditional and rectified-flow diffusion models, finding a signature along denoising trajectories and across training. They use it to regularize memorization during training and to detect and steer away from memorization at inference.
hK7GTDoH9p.key_idea: Memorized trajectories show a dominant singular mode of the local Jacobian followed by sharp spectral recovery, which serves as a regularization target, detection signal and steering cue.
hK7GTDoH9p.evidence: Jacobian spectral analysis across conditional, unconditional and rectified-flow models, trajectory-level experiments mainly on CelebA32 (about 4K images per reviewers), and a memorization-quality trade-off in Stable Diffusion.
hK7GTDoH9p.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the trajectory-level, temporal spectral view of memorization new and interesting, and its actionable use for regularization, detection and steering a strength.
hK7GTDoH9p.main_concern: The main-text figures are unreadable or missing labels, and no justification is given for why the spectral transition occurs, with trajectory experiments mostly on CelebA32.

eDtO9di9ih.one_liner: Assigns token-level negative credit in all-wrong RLVR groups by re-scoring tokens under contexts built from sibling failed rollouts.
eDtO9di9ih.problem: With binary rewards in group-relative RLVR, the outcome-based advantage vanishes when every rollout for a problem is incorrect, leaving such groups unused.
eDtO9di9ih.method: SibCredit re-scores a target rollout's sampled tokens under contexts built from other failed rollouts in the same group. Different-answer rollouts provide candidate negative evidence, and same-answer rollouts act as a control so penalties are kept only when different-answer opposition sufficiently exceeds same-answer opposition.
eDtO9di9ih.key_idea: Disagreement among wrong answers yields token-level negative credit, filtered by same-answer sibling re-scoring to remove shared conditioning effects such as reasoning-style shifts.
eDtO9di9ih.evidence: Ablations (reviewers cite accuracy dropping to 14.6% without same-answer calibration versus 17.0% for the base model) and a token-level analysis on 60 groups and 209 rollouts, compared against baselines that need correct privileged context.
eDtO9di9ih.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it offers a concrete way to use otherwise unused failed groups, and that same-answer calibration is well motivated and supported by targeted ablations.
eDtO9di9ih.main_concern: The assumptions that different answers imply different errors and that same-answer siblings share similar reasoning are unexamined, and comparisons to CAST and Negative Self-Distillation and uncertainty estimates are missing.

oVy27bv5En.one_liner: Compares sign, spectral, Newton and Euclidean descent via continuous-time zones where majority losses dominate under hidden data imbalance.
oVy27bv5En.problem: When the source of data imbalance is unobserved and the optimizer sees only aggregate loss, it is unclear how different optimizer geometries cope with minority groups.
oVy27bv5En.method: They model idealized optimizers as steepest descent under different geometries in continuous time, characterize a region where majority losses are optimized regardless of the admissible minority structure, and derive explicit equations of this zone with bounds on the time needed to leave it.
oVy27bv5En.key_idea: A minimax gradient-magnitude condition defines a majority-dominated zone for each steepest-descent geometry, and exit-time bounds compare how each depends on minority amplitude.
oVy27bv5En.evidence: Theory with explicit zone equations and exit-time bounds, plus experiments with AdamW and Muon versus SGD on language, tabular and image tasks.
oVy27bv5En.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is relevant to optimizer choice with hidden minorities and that the framework gives explicit zone equations and bounds for several optimizers that appear sound.
oVy27bv5En.main_concern: The link between theory and practice is weak: entry-time gaps may reflect time scale rather than geometry, only the linear-regression experiment measures entry times, and the presentation is dense and lacks intuition.

Yi6uDVGgpF.one_liner: Benchmark of 50 task-policy pairs measuring whether LLM agents evade runtime monitors when oversight blocks task completion.
Yi6uDVGgpF.problem: It is unclear whether LLM agents treat runtime oversight as an obstacle and circumvent monitors under ordinary task pressure, without malicious goals or evasion instructions.
Yi6uDVGgpF.method: EvasionBench contains 50 task-policy pairs (10 original and 40 from existing benchmarks per reviewers) where finishing the task requires an operation a runtime monitor prohibits. Agents know their tool calls are monitored and are prompted to continue when they pause.
Yi6uDVGgpF.key_idea: Tasks are built so completion requires a monitor-prohibited operation, letting attempted and successful evasion be measured separately as a propensity.
Yi6uDVGgpF.evidence: Evaluations of frontier models on EvasionBench with reasoning-effort variation, trace analysis of evasion strategies, and a denial-of-service prompt-injection test; reviewers note a single GPT-OSS-120B monitor.
Yi6uDVGgpF.claimed_gains: Best-of-3 evasion attempt rates reach up to 98% and success rates up to 88%.
Yi6uDVGgpF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is a promising way to stress-test monitors, that evasion under ordinary task pressure is an important finding, and that separate reporting of attempts and successes is valuable.
Yi6uDVGgpF.main_concern: Only one monitor model (GPT-OSS-120B) is used, and there are no confidence intervals or prompt ablations, so the robustness of the model ordering and dependence on prompt wording are unclear.

mkCnmmJC8V.one_liner: Measures synthetic financial data releases by rank agreement between detector leaderboards on synthetic versus private data.
mkCnmmJC8V.problem: Synthetic releases of private fraud-detection data are judged by distributional fidelity and train-on-synthetic accuracy, which do not show whether the models that win on a release also win on the private data.
mkCnmmJC8V.method: They define leaderboard fidelity as the rank agreement between the detector leaderboard a release induces and the one on private data, calibrated against resampling of the private test period. They build a leakage-free benchmark from interbank clearing network transfers and evaluate sixty releases against eleven detectors.
mkCnmmJC8V.key_idea: Score a synthetic release by rank agreement of detector leaderboards with the private data, calibrated by a resampling noise band from the private test period.
mkCnmmJC8V.evidence: Sixty releases (five from each of twelve generators) evaluated against eleven detectors under equal budgets on interbank transfers; reviewers note robustness checks including account and week resampling and a public-data replication.
mkCnmmJC8V.claimed_gains: The best distributional criterion (classifier two-sample test or label-rate error on every split) gains about half as much as measuring rank agreement against the private data.
mkCnmmJC8V.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the public-user model-selection objective is well motivated and the analysis (multiple releases per generator, selection regret, a private-reference noise scale) is informative with extensive robustness checks.
mkCnmmJC8V.main_concern: Standard fidelity criteria are computed only on the synthetic training split while leaderboards also depend on separately generated validation and test splits, so the comparison may not show why those criteria fail.

vpEWtq6tdm.one_liner: Two-stage feature compression for feed-forward 3D Gaussian splatting, guided by renderings of an intermediate 3DGS as feedback.
vpEWtq6tdm.problem: Feed-forward 3DGS representations are costly to store and transmit, and compressing input images means heavy receiver-side reconstruction while compressing Gaussian primitives is hard because their attributes are heterogeneous and irregular.
vpEWtq6tdm.method: FeCoSplat compresses multi-view features to obtain an intermediate 3DGS, then uses its rendered views as feedback to guide a second-stage compression. The bitstreams decode into a compact implicit state from which a lightweight predictor reconstructs the final Gaussian primitives.
vpEWtq6tdm.key_idea: Encoder-side rendering of an intermediate 3DGS provides feedback that guides a second-stage feature compression, leaving the decoder without any rendering loop.
vpEWtq6tdm.evidence: Rate-distortion experiments against image-compression and Gaussian-compression baselines such as CodecSplat, with zero-shot tests across datasets, input resolutions and numbers of input views; reviewers cite RE10K, ACID and DL3DV.
vpEWtq6tdm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the sender-receiver framing, the encoder-only feedback that keeps the decoder lightweight, and ablations showing that rendering feedback improves reconstruction fidelity.
vpEWtq6tdm.main_concern: The rate-distortion advantage is overstated: it nearly ties or trails CodecSplat and ELIC in places with no BD-rate or variance reporting, and novelty over existing feature compression is limited.

XbvtJlWtKb.one_liner: Selects replay samples for online class-incremental learning by matching buffer distribution to all past data using RFF statistics.
XbvtJlWtKb.problem: Existing replay sample selection in online class-incremental learning suffers from limited data availability and error accumulation, giving suboptimal performance.
XbvtJlWtKb.method: Distribution Matching Replay (DMR) continuously aligns the replay buffer's distribution with that of all historical data using compact online Random Fourier Feature mean and covariance statistics. A randomized sketch of the RFF covariance statistics approximates Maximum Covariance Discrepancy without storing per-class covariance matrices.
XbvtJlWtKb.key_idea: Replay selection minimizes mean and covariance discrepancy in a fixed random-Fourier-feature space against additive online statistics of all past data, with the covariance sketched to save memory.
XbvtJlWtKb.evidence: Experiments on multiple OCIL benchmarks showing DMR outperforms existing selection strategies and integrates into various OCIL methods, plus ablations.
XbvtJlWtKb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is important and the method is simple and coherent, built on additive online statistics, with ablations that identify the source of the gains.
XbvtJlWtKb.main_concern: Baselines and references are dated or missing (CSReL, GCR, PCR, UER, streaming coreset methods), and the link between the distribution-matching proxy and sample value or interference is not validated.

AJrTu822bh.one_liner: Benchmark of eight interaction actions across 24 conditions for full-duplex spoken language models, scoring execution and follow-through.
AJrTu822bh.problem: Existing full-duplex spoken language model benchmarks lack a structured action-level formulation, often evaluate action occurrence rather than success, and cover few real-world conversations.
AJrTu822bh.method: DuplexAct defines a three-level taxonomy of eight interaction actions and 24 interaction conditions, and measures success through immediate execution and subsequent follow-through with action-specific metrics. It has 4,691 test instances across casual conversation, meetings, customer service and interviews, 2,531 of them from real recordings.
AJrTu822bh.key_idea: Success is split into immediate execution and subsequent follow-through, scored with action-specific metrics over a taxonomy of eight actions under 24 conditions.
AJrTu822bh.evidence: A benchmark of 4,691 test instances for end-to-end full-duplex models; the abstract reports no model results, and reviewers note follow-through is scored by an LLM judge.
AJrTu822bh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the well-structured taxonomy and the separation of immediate execution from follow-through, which is more informative than counting action occurrence.
AJrTu822bh.main_concern: Follow-through relies on an LLM judge (GPT-5.4) with no reported agreement against human judgments, and success time windows differ across actions, which confounds comparisons.

YXmUzNBh03.one_liner: Training-free MoE diffusion-LLM inference that refreshes GPU-resident experts at cost-optimal intervals using temporal stability of expert activations.
YXmUzNBh03.problem: Deploying MoE diffusion LLMs on resource-constrained devices is hard, and expert-offloading methods designed for autoregressive models incur heavy I/O overhead or compute bottlenecks.
YXmUzNBh03.method: TIDE exploits the temporal stability of expert activations within a diffusion block and refreshes expert placement at intervals in an I/O-aware way. The interval comes from a mathematical program that minimizes I/O traffic and CPU computation, with original routing unchanged and no training.
YXmUzNBh03.key_idea: Expert activations stay similar across denoising steps in a block, so GPU expert placement is refreshed only at an interval chosen to minimize I/O traffic plus CPU computation.
YXmUzNBh03.evidence: A single GPU-CPU system with LLaDA2.0-mini and LLaDA2.0-flash; reviewers note tests over generation lengths, GPU expert budgets and block sizes, using only MBPP.
YXmUzNBh03.claimed_gains: Up to 1.4x and 1.5x throughput improvements over prior baselines on LLaDA2.0-mini and LLaDA2.0-flash.
YXmUzNBh03.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method simple and practical, motivated by observed temporal locality of expert activations, needing no training and giving consistent throughput gains across two models, generation lengths and GPU budgets.
YXmUzNBh03.main_concern: The cost model is under-validated (CPU cost function and fitting unclear, no comparison with a tuned fixed interval), the Fiddler baseline may be misconfigured, and evaluation covers only MBPP, one model family and throughput.

KfpQmoI5FM.one_liner: Tabular benchmark built by selecting public tasks whose privacy-preserving fingerprints match a proprietary enterprise benchmark.
KfpQmoI5FM.problem: Few proprietary enterprise datasets are public and open tabular benchmarks often fail to capture enterprise deployment realities, leaving a structural evaluation gap.
KfpQmoI5FM.method: They generate 134 tasks on 90 tables from public datasets, then use a privacy-preserving data fingerprint to automatically select those whose characteristics are most similar to tasks in an internal proprietary benchmark.
KfpQmoI5FM.key_idea: Coarse, privacy-preserving data fingerprints turn benchmark construction into table discovery, picking public tasks statistically similar to enterprise data without disclosing it.
KfpQmoI5FM.evidence: Comparison of aggregated statistics with an internal benchmark and eleven baseline models whose ranking correlation (Spearman) with the internal benchmark is compared against open-source benchmarks; reviewers also cite t-SNE and Elo checks.
KfpQmoI5FM.claimed_gains: ProxyBench is described as much more statistically similar to enterprise data than existing open-source benchmarks and gives a superior Spearman correlation of model ranking with the internal benchmark, with no values stated.
KfpQmoI5FM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea of turning inaccessible enterprise data into a privacy-preserving table-discovery problem fresh and practical, and the multi-angle validation convincing.
KfpQmoI5FM.main_concern: Similarity is purely statistical and rests on a single enterprise whose internal benchmark is undisclosed, so generalization and reproducibility are unverified and splits ignore temporal drift.

4fbUVvST0K.one_liner: Turns monocular hand-object interaction video into dexterous robot-hand trajectories via staged physical-consistency enforcement and physics-based refinement.
4fbUVvST0K.problem: Reconstructing hand-object interaction from a single view and transferring it to robot hands is hard, and prior methods need task-specific RL training or assume clean motion-capture trajectories.
4fbUVvST0K.method: OmniHOI is a pipeline from RGB video to an interaction-faithful dexterous-hand trajectory that enforces physical consistency at each stage: image evidence in reconstruction, contact geometry in retargeting, and dynamics in physics-based refinement. Each stage optimizes its own representation to correct errors before they propagate downstream.
4fbUVvST0K.key_idea: Enforce physical consistency stage by stage with the evidence available there (image, contact geometry, dynamics) instead of leaving errors for a learned policy to absorb.
4fbUVvST0K.evidence: 150 motion-capture trajectories transferred to each of five dexterous hands with 6 to 22 DoF, 60 monocular video clips, and execution on a real bimanual robot; reviewers note ablations attribute most of the gain to physics refinement.
4fbUVvST0K.claimed_gains: 39-89% success across five dexterous hands versus at most 31% for prior transfer methods, and 53% on 60 monocular clips versus 28% for the best prior video-to-robot pipeline.
4fbUVvST0K.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a complete, working video-to-robot system with strong results across five very different hands without per-task training, backed by honest failure analysis.
4fbUVvST0K.main_concern: Technical novelty is limited (a combination of existing tools such as SAM 3D, FoundationPose and WiLoR), and physics refinement is tuned and scored in the same simulator, so success may not hold under real-robot physics.

We8yvAk7ul.one_liner: Unified 3D world-state tokenizer gives VLA models current-state context and 128 discrete future-state prediction targets.
We8yvAk7ul.problem: VLA models learn from 2D visual projections while the underlying physical world state stays implicit.
We8yvAk7ul.method: PLATO learns a compact world-state representation from multi-view observations with geometric, semantic and forward-inverse dynamics supervision. Features or embeddings of discrete codes give current-state context, and 128 discrete state tokens serve as autoregressive future-state targets alongside action supervision, using the VLM's native conditioning and next-token prediction.
We8yvAk7ul.key_idea: One tokenized world-state vocabulary serves both as input context and as next-token future-state supervision inside the VLM, with no dense prediction branches.
We8yvAk7ul.evidence: VLA pretraining and post-training on three simulation benchmarks and four real-world tasks, plus representation analyses showing geometry becomes more linearly accessible.
We8yvAk7ul.claimed_gains: Future-state supervision raises average real-world success by 11.7 and 25.4% under nominal and randomized conditions, and current-state context gives a 40% gain over supervision alone in flower insertion.
We8yvAk7ul.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the shared world-state interface simple and effective, with the future-state branch removed at inference at no extra cost and gains across initializations and training stages.
We8yvAk7ul.main_concern: Ablations change several factors at once, so the contributions of 3D information and discretization are not isolated, and the choice of VGGT-Omega is unjustified with no alternative-backbone ablation or compute cost reported.

zUiNYteKzS.one_liner: Shares quantizer scales and rounding randomness across classifier-free-guidance branches to shrink cross-branch quantization error.
zUiNYteKzS.problem: Quantized models are judged per branch, but the guided error under classifier-free guidance depends on a cross term between conditional and unconditional branch errors that no per-branch metric sees.
zUiNYteKzS.method: PairRound lets the two branches share what decides their codes: the activation quantizer scale and, where rounding is stochastic, the random numbers. A quadratic in guidance scale s states when the coarser grid from sharing pays off.
zUiNYteKzS.key_idea: Sharing quantizer scale and stochastic-rounding noise across the two CFG branches makes their codes differ only where values differ, shrinking the cross-branch error term.
zUiNYteKzS.evidence: A survey of six inference stacks, a decomposition of guided error, and experiments at matched bits and seeds on eleven image, video and language backbones, composed with eight published methods.
zUiNYteKzS.claimed_gains: In six inference stacks 75.8% of activation quantizers give the branches different scales or random numbers; the shared scale lowers trajectory distance to the BF16 sampler by 60% to 68% on eleven backbones and improves FID, VBench or perplexity on every one.
zUiNYteKzS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem well motivated by a survey of real implementations and an exact error decomposition, with a simple fix that needs no calibration or training.
zUiNYteKzS.main_concern: Reported baseline degradations look larger than in the literature (for example SDXL W4A4 FID), the common recipe may not match the original settings of composed methods, and the theory is loosely tied to the practical gains.

SyenObw03C.one_liner: Resolves disagreement among heterogeneous LLMs by projecting global candidate choice into pairwise comparisons and reconstructing answers from retained relations.
SyenObw03C.problem: When heterogeneous LLMs give disagreeing initial answers, majority support may favor a wrong answer or leave the choice unclear.
SyenObw03C.method: PairRecon uses the candidates and support distribution from initial disagreement to ask models for pairwise judgments on specific disputes. Judgments that agree across both presentation orders are kept as directed relations that, with initial support, reconstruct the candidate; candidate admission or staged arbitration then limits answer updates.
SyenObw03C.key_idea: Global selection becomes order-consistent pairwise judgments on disputed candidate pairs, kept as directed relations and combined with initial support to reconstruct the answer despite unresolved conflicts.
SyenObw03C.evidence: Nine benchmarks, two model scales, and numerical, mathematical and program-output tasks per reviewers, comparing accuracy and inference cost against sampling and debate methods.
SyenObw03C.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the distinction between a model's global answer and its local pairwise judgment is useful, extra inference is invoked only on disagreement, and the evaluation spans many models and datasets.
SyenObw03C.main_concern: Thresholds (score gap, minimum support) are heuristic and not ablated, staged arbitration is underspecified, and gains are modest with no comparison to alternative pairwise aggregation rules.
