z4WBU6V4rG.one_liner: Neural layers build a multi-state energy that a Dynamical System Machine layer minimizes for combinatorial reasoning.
z4WBU6V4rG.problem: Neural networks built on primitives like matrix multiplication are not native mechanisms for combinatorial search, so they must grow in size or computation to reason over global constraints.
z4WBU6V4rG.method: DS-OPT adds a Dynamical System Machine (DSM) as a network layer: neural layers construct a per-input multi-state energy whose low-energy states answer the task, and the DSM minimizes it with noisy winner-take-all units that reduce to an Ising machine in the two-state case. A differentiable relaxation enables end-to-end training while inference always runs the discrete DSM.
z4WBU6V4rG.key_idea: Neural layers emit a per-input multi-state energy that a discrete noisy winner-take-all dynamical system minimizes, trained through a differentiable relaxation.
z4WBU6V4rG.evidence: Zebra puzzles, visual Sudoku and binary image completion against neural baselines of comparable size, with DSM costs estimated by circuit-level simulation.
z4WBU6V4rG.claimed_gains: On Zebra it solves up to 98.4% of the puzzles, against 82.6% for a Transformer with five times more parameters, at half its inference time and energy.
z4WBU6V4rG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the relaxation well motivated and the DSM layer's contribution shown by ablations (learned couplings help, the DSM corrects perception errors, relaxed-to-discrete transfer works), with clear benefits over standard Transformers.
z4WBU6V4rG.main_concern: Comparisons are not comprehensive: single-pass Transformers are weak baselines against iterative refiners such as TRM and HRM, instances are easy for classical solvers, and the paper is hard to follow for unfamiliar readers.

tFRPefRQBw.one_liner: Regulates when retrieved agent experience is used or discarded and assigns memory-aware credit by trajectory progress for long-horizon LLM agents.
tFRPefRQBw.problem: In long-horizon tasks, retrieved experience can keep biasing decisions after it stops matching the agent's state, and some RL credit schemes improve intermediate progress without improving completion.
tFRPefRQBw.method: AERCA structures past interactions into Task-level Completion Experience (how to complete) and Gap-level Cognition Experience (how to know), and dynamically decides whether retrieved experience is used, retained or discarded. For policy learning, relative trajectory progress sets how much memory-aware credit a trajectory gets and breakthroughs during memory use events set where that credit goes.
tFRPefRQBw.key_idea: Retrieved experience is gated at each step by the agent's evolving state, while memory-aware credit is allocated by relative trajectory progress and breakthrough points in memory use.
tFRPefRQBw.evidence: Per reviewers, experiments on ScienceWorld and WebShop with GRPO, GiGPO and BEACON baselines sharing the same experience-retrieval pipeline; the abstract is cut off before the results.
tFRPefRQBw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is practical and that the controlled comparison with a shared experience pipeline (GRPO, GiGPO, BEACON) isolates a benefit from the credit-assignment component.
tFRPefRQBw.main_concern: The attribution mechanism is underspecified when reward arrives only at the end (as in WebShop) and its link to GRPO advantages is unclear, and the method does not clearly beat baselines on long horizons or RetroAgent on WebShop.

YUnqoQyWTN.one_liner: LLM agents with learned bid shading self-organize into profitable multi-step workflows through sequential auctions under imperfect competition.
YUnqoQyWTN.problem: Prior sequential-auction theory needs perfect clones as perfect competition, which drives agent profit to zero, while having no competition also causes market failure.
YUnqoQyWTN.method: A decentralized market of self-interested heterogeneous agents solves multi-step tasks through sequential auctions, with agents learning to shade bids to earn positive margins. They evaluate four bidding algorithms (Mirror Descent, Thompson Sampling, Bayes-Optimal, PPO) across three auction protocols (1st-Price, 2nd-Price, Credit-Conserving Vickrey).
YUnqoQyWTN.key_idea: Agents learn bid shading in sequential auctions with frozen LLMs, sustaining positive profit margins in the middle ground between perfect clones and no competition.
YUnqoQyWTN.evidence: Four bidding algorithms across three auction protocols over a diverse set of domains, including synthetic translation, information retrieval and mathematical reasoning per reviewers.
YUnqoQyWTN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework is well motivated by prior theory, addresses agent profitability under imperfect competition, and shows promising results across several domains with a simple setup that keeps the LLMs frozen.
YUnqoQyWTN.main_concern: The LLM experiments rely on a centralized assessor that scores agents, so gains may come from the assessor rather than the auctions, valuation-estimation accuracy is not evaluated, and the bidding algorithms mostly adapt existing techniques.

EmoSAgLNzJ.one_liner: Aligns pretrained unimodal encoders from 100-500 anchors using global entropic optimal transport on unpaired data, distilled into lightweight encoders.
EmoSAgLNzJ.problem: Aligning two independently pretrained unimodal encoders typically needs millions of paired examples, yet often only 100-500 pairs exist while unpaired data is abundant.
EmoSAgLNzJ.method: Each representation is expressed by its similarities to the N paired anchors, giving both modalities a common coordinate system. A single entropic optimal transport problem over the whole pool matches the unpaired points, with marginal constraints countering hubness, and the plan is distilled into two lightweight encoders.
EmoSAgLNzJ.key_idea: Anchor-relative coordinates plus one global entropic OT plan whose marginals counter hubness are distilled into lightweight encoders, making the correspondence inductive.
EmoSAgLNzJ.evidence: Image-text and molecule-text alignment on Flickr30k, MS-COCO and ChEBI-20 at equal anchor budgets against baselines.
EmoSAgLNzJ.claimed_gains: Matches or exceeds all baselines at the same anchor budget while training 3 to 15x faster than the strongest one.
EmoSAgLNzJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the low-label alignment problem is practical, the writing is clear, and the pipeline is simple and efficient, needing no anchors or OT at inference.
EmoSAgLNzJ.main_concern: Novelty is incremental (it combines anchor-relative representations, Sinkhorn hubness correction and OT-based distillation as in OTTER and S-CLIP), and gains over SOTAlign are mostly within one standard deviation on a small 400-pair test set.

wbDLWn7mmj.one_liner: Fine-tunes flow-matching policies online by aligning them with an SVGD-built transport field from a maximum-entropy RL objective.
wbDLWn7mmj.problem: Prior RL fine-tuning of flow-matching policies approximates the current or optimal policy distribution or distills, which gives biased gradients or loses multimodal modeling capacity.
wbDLWn7mmj.method: RLDT builds a transport field from a maximum-entropy RL objective using Stein Variational Gradient Descent and fine-tunes a pretrained flow-matching policy to align with it. To avoid backpropagation through the multi-step generation, it approximates actions from intermediate denoising steps via expected-target estimation.
wbDLWn7mmj.key_idea: Policy improvement is treated as transporting action densities toward high reward with an SVGD field, applied through expected-target estimates at intermediate denoising steps.
wbDLWn7mmj.evidence: Continuous-control experiments comparing reward quality and convergence speed with competitive baselines; the abstract is cut off before further details.
wbDLWn7mmj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method well motivated and clearly described, with action-space density transport via SVGD an intuitive framing for flow-matching policy improvement.
wbDLWn7mmj.main_concern: Novelty is limited because the SVGD transport field toward a soft Q target closely follows Soft Q-Learning, with no comparison to one-step distillation methods such as FQL and no analysis of early-training instability.

XfaGuMOP77.one_liner: Clusters dense foundation-model tokens within each tile into multiple instance embeddings for multiple-instance learning on whole-slide images.
XfaGuMOP77.problem: Feature extractors compress each WSI tile into one global embedding, so slide-level aggregators cannot see fine-grained sub-tile evidence and sparse diagnostic signals in cytology get diluted.
XfaGuMOP77.method: DI-MIL clusters dense spatial tokens from a frozen foundation model inside each tile and turns the tile into multiple independently weighted instance embeddings. It is a training-free post-encoding module needing no re-encoding or aggregator changes.
XfaGuMOP77.key_idea: Spherical k-means over a frozen model's dense spatial tokens splits each tile into several instances, decoupling encoding context from instance granularity.
XfaGuMOP77.evidence: Four cytopathology datasets, three frozen foundation models and two attention-based aggregators, compared against ten MIL baselines with ACMIL as the aggregator.
XfaGuMOP77.claimed_gains: With ACMIL, DI-MIL achieves the highest mean AUC on all four datasets against ten baselines, and attention localization shows an 8.5-fold enrichment figure (the abstract is cut off after this).
XfaGuMOP77.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the decomposition addresses a real limitation of tile-level MIL, is plug-and-play across foundation models, and avoids re-encoding at smaller patch sizes.
XfaGuMOP77.main_concern: Evidence that decomposed instances localize diagnostic cells is indirect (attention visualizations), and fine-grained sub-tile modeling is seen as incremental relative to hierarchical approaches such as HIPT.

rK859Ipz0p.one_liner: Turns latent-space pairwise rarity orderings into calibrated intrinsic rewards via a ranking-loss predictor for reward-free exploration.
rK859Ipz0p.problem: Entropy-maximizing intrinsic rewards need density estimates that are unreliable in high dimensions, and the latent space whose distances define proximity has no principled way to be selected or validated.
rK859Ipz0p.method: CALOR extracts only a pairwise ordering among states from the latent space and trains a predictor network to reproduce it with a pairwise ranking loss while placing its outputs on a calibrated scale that restores reward magnitude. It accepts any source of pairwise rarity comparisons, such as a second ordering from how long the agent has stayed alive.
rK859Ipz0p.key_idea: A predictor learns a pairwise rarity ranking with a calibration term that restores reward magnitude, so exploration depends on ordering rather than exact latent geometry.
rK859Ipz0p.evidence: Reward-free Craftax-Classic at one billion interactions against baselines, plus continuous-control environments and ablations per reviewers.
rK859Ipz0p.claimed_gains: On reward-free Craftax-Classic at one billion interactions, CALOR reaches a Crafter score of 40.7 against 3.3 for the strongest baseline.
rK859Ipz0p.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learning a relative ordering instead of densities is interesting and well motivated, with impressive Craftax-Classic results and detailed ablations.
rK859Ipz0p.main_concern: The method section is imprecise (rarity score and calibration loss are ill-defined, harming reproducibility), evidence for the high-dimensional claim is limited since continuous-control tasks use state inputs, and the rarity predictor may fail on out-of-distribution states.

OfML6CyFqT.one_liner: Compresses fixed-total allocation models into group counts for exact sampling, lossless model comparison, and discrete structure learning.
OfML6CyFqT.problem: Learning interaction groups from observed integer allocations and sampling allocations at a requested total are costly when interactions depend on group totals.
OfML6CyFqT.method: Polynomial coefficients sum heterogeneous local weights into count tables; for two groups the fixed total removes one redundant count, and the current count distribution is reused to evaluate batches of group-membership changes through exact normalizer ratios.
OfML6CyFqT.key_idea: Track group counts instead of configurations, and use the fixed total to drop one redundant count, reducing compilation cost and enabling exact normalizer ratios for membership swaps.
OfML6CyFqT.evidence: 516 independent synthetic structures compared with discrete pseudolikelihood, timing at two fixed scales, and exact calculations on omitted interactions and importance sampling.
OfML6CyFqT.claimed_gains: Two-group compilation drops from O(J c_max r^2) to O(J c_max r), the full learner is 5.89x and 7.40x faster at two scales with identical fitted outputs, and target KL is .04811 versus .04953 for discrete pseudolikelihood within a 2% noninferiority margin.
OfML6CyFqT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that exploiting the fixed total to compress the problem into a compact macrostate gives a substantial, simply analyzed running-time reduction.
OfML6CyFqT.main_concern: Validation is on controlled synthetic models, and no practical scenario is motivated where the group dependence exists but is unknown beforehand.

suDBQxXvb4.one_liner: Truncates text-basis subspaces by SVD curvature and projects image embeddings onto a noise subspace's null space to remove semantic leakage.
suDBQxXvb4.problem: VLMs are not trained to disentangle criteria, so criterion-specific conditional subspaces stay coupled and projection leaks non-target semantics into conditional representations.
suDBQxXvb4.method: SP-CRL decomposes the original text basis and applies curvature-based adaptive truncation to the resulting basis vectors to build a purer conditional subspace. It then identifies a noise subspace and projects image embeddings onto its null space to remove irrelevant semantic components.
suDBQxXvb4.key_idea: Keep only the high-singular-value directions of the decomposed text basis up to the maximum-curvature point, and project image embeddings into the null space of an identified noise subspace.
suDBQxXvb4.evidence: Customized clustering, customized few-shot classification and customized retrieval, with CLIP, BLIP2 and SigLIP backbones per reviewers, plus ablations on truncation ratio and noise subspace selection.
suDBQxXvb4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the semantic-leakage problem is well motivated and that the two modules give consistent gains across the three downstream tasks, supported by ablations.
suDBQxXvb4.main_concern: The justification is thin: why singular-value magnitude and maximum curvature indicate semantic purity is unproven, and controls such as dimension-matched random subspace filtering are missing.

Y2Ql7wUsm3.one_liner: Extends Mamba to combinatorial complexes with rank-aware bidirectional SSM scans and incidence-supported, index-free kernel mixing.
Y2Ql7wUsm3.problem: Selective SSMs need ordered scans, but combinatorial complexes have no canonical cell ordering, so linearization makes causal scans order-dependent.
Y2Ql7wUsm3.method: CCMamba combines incidence-based cross-rank lifting with two mixers: CCMamba-S keeps bidirectional selective SSM scans and is sensitive to within-rank order, while CCMamba-K replaces causal support with incidence-supported structural gating and factorized kernel mixing that is permutation-equivariant.
Y2Ql7wUsm3.key_idea: Replace causal sequence masks with incidence-defined structural gating and factorized kernel mixing, giving permutation-equivariant mixing without linearizing cells.
Y2Ql7wUsm3.evidence: Proofs of order sensitivity, permutation equivariance, and conditional expressive power, plus experiments across graph, hypergraph, simplicial-complex, and cellular-complex benchmarks with permutation tests and matched-mixer ablations.
Y2Ql7wUsm3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the unified framework for higher-order structures is useful, and the permutation experiments and broad evaluation across graphs, hypergraphs, simplicial and cellular complexes clearly separate CCMamba-S from CCMamba-K.
Y2Ql7wUsm3.main_concern: Novelty over related work is unclear (Graph Mamba with bidirectional scans, TopoMamba, factorized graph kernel methods), and the paper has presentation and notation problems.

OrxjGiSlBB.one_liner: Auto-research agent that persists recoverable executable states and re-anchors by choosing an archived state and an extend-or-redirect direction.
OrxjGiSlBB.problem: Long-horizon LLM research agents depend on expensive model calls and poorly targeted computation.
OrxjGiSlBB.method: ScienceFlow organizes research around recoverable executable states, and its ESTRA mechanism jointly selects an execution anchor from current or archived states and an extend-or-redirect direction. An evidence-aware controller admits and monitors jobs by remaining budget, resources, and validated progress.
OrxjGiSlBB.key_idea: Jointly pick an execution anchor from current or archived executable states and an extend-or-redirect direction, then gate jobs by budget and validated progress.
OrxjGiSlBB.evidence: Machine learning, scientific modeling, and mathematical optimization tasks, including the full 75-task MLE-bench over three independent sweeps under a 24-hour per-task budget.
OrxjGiSlBB.claimed_gains: 70.22 +/- 1.18% Any-Medal rate on the full 75-task MLE-bench with DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Preview under a 24-hour budget per task run, at a mean API cost of $76.4 per benchmark sweep.
OrxjGiSlBB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework addresses practical continuity problems of long-horizon research agents, with low reported API cost, competitive benchmark results, and ablations of ESTRA and execution control.
OrxjGiSlBB.main_concern: Baseline comparisons are not matched (different backbones, hardware, and 24-hour versus 12-hour budgets), and ESTRA is not compared with MCTS, UCB, or random re-anchoring.

3qEQrT23rh.one_liner: Minimax limits and an efficient spectral-plus-least-squares procedure for recovering latent memberships in two-component Gaussian mixed linear regression.
3qEQrT23rh.problem: The statistical limits of membership recovery in mixed regression are much less understood than those of estimating the regression components.
3qEQrT23rh.method: For the two-component Gaussian random-design model with p <~ n, the paper derives the minimax mis-clustering risk and the exact-recovery condition and attains both with a procedure that forms an initial partition from a bounded-residual spectral direction plus the pooled residual, then runs hard least-squares iterations that geometrically contract a margin-weighted Hamming loss.
3qEQrT23rh.key_idea: The random regression margin's mass near zero sets the mis-clustering scale, while the minimum realized margin across the sample governs exact recovery.
3qEQrT23rh.evidence: Theory: minimax lower and upper bounds with finite-sample guarantees for the proposed procedure, plus a numerical study mentioned in reviews.
3qEQrT23rh.claimed_gains: The minimax mis-clustering risk is of order min(1,r) for noise-to-signal ratio r, and exact recovery is possible if and only if nr tends to 0.
3qEQrT23rh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question valuable and the presentation clear, with finite-sample guarantees and a transparent oracle explanation of why an order-r error persists.
3qEQrT23rh.main_concern: The contribution beyond existing EM theory for mixed linear regression is unclear, since the guarantees need a high-SNR regime (r below a small constant) and the stopping rule is not fully tied to the theorem.

ijmcExZGk5.one_liner: Paper Formalizer formalizes a paper's internal proofs in Lean while exposing external results as explicit dependencies to cut proof-review burden.
ijmcExZGk5.problem: Reviewers report checking proofs for only 28.4% of theory papers with proofs, and full Lean formalization requires formalizing results outside the paper and inspecting a large formal body to judge faithfulness.
ijmcExZGk5.method: It defines the Paper Formalization task with four metrics, making internal arguments machine-checkable while treating external results as explicit dependencies. Paper Formalizer solves the task while minimizing the review burden.
ijmcExZGk5.key_idea: Formalize only a paper's own arguments in Lean, leaving cited external results as explicit dependencies instead of recursively formalizing them.
ijmcExZGk5.evidence: Theoretical papers across multiple topics (nine papers in the end-to-end evaluation per reviews), plus a survey of NeurIPS, ICML, and ICLR 2025 reviews.
ijmcExZGk5.claimed_gains: With GPT-6-Astra, approximately 90% fewer custom definitions and 64% fewer explicit (item truncated in the abstract).
ijmcExZGk5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the task is practically motivated, separating internal proofs from external dependencies avoids unnecessary formalization, and the structured workflow and metrics are useful.
ijmcExZGk5.main_concern: The evaluation is small (nine papers, unclear selection), the system accepts only 40% of goals with cost rising for modest gains, and review time and error detection are not measured.

EUwk45dxvX.one_liner: Distills autoregressive LMs into diffusion LMs by matching path distributions with Path KL over a masked-trajectory teacher.
EUwk45dxvX.problem: On-policy distillation from autoregressive to diffusion language models is hard because the two use different conditioning structures for token prediction.
EUwk45dxvX.method: They extend the autoregressive teacher's response distribution with a prescribed forward masking process, giving a teacher distribution over the same path space as the DLM decoding process. Path KL aligns student and teacher path distributions and is proved to upper-bound the reverse KL between final response distributions.
EUwk45dxvX.key_idea: Add a forward masking process to the autoregressive teacher so it defines a distribution over denoising trajectories, then minimize Path KL, an upper bound on response-level reverse KL.
EUwk45dxvX.evidence: Experiments across three student model sizes and four math and code benchmarks with a Qwen teacher and SDAR students, compared with Token KL and Block KL.
EUwk45dxvX.claimed_gains: Average benchmark gains of up to 3.15 points, more pronounced under highly parallel decoding.
EUwk45dxvX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the path-space formulation cleanly addresses the conditioning mismatch and gives consistent gains across student sizes and benchmarks.
EUwk45dxvX.main_concern: Experiments cover only math and code benchmarks with a single AR teacher and the SDAR family, so generality to other diffusion LMs is not shown.

fbvBYNTB0C.one_liner: Feature-free binary node hashing from a Nystrom-inspired low-rank sketch of a graph transition operator blended with label diffusion.
fbvBYNTB0C.problem: GNN embeddings are costly to store and slow to serve, and existing binary graph hashing is either slow and loses global structure or is too shallow for harder graphs.
fbvBYNTB0C.method: NyS-Binary combines a randomized Nystrom-inspired low-rank sketch of a higher-order graph transition operator with a leakage-safe label-diffusion channel, fuses them with a convex blend, and quantizes with an adaptive per-column median rule. It uses only graph topology, with no node attributes.
fbvBYNTB0C.key_idea: Sketch a higher-order transition operator with randomized Nystrom low-rank approximation, blend with label diffusion, and binarize each column at its adaptive median.
fbvBYNTB0C.evidence: Ten node-classification benchmarks with diverse downstream classifiers (including spiking neuromorphic classifiers), ablations, heterophily analysis, and large graphs.
fbvBYNTB0C.claimed_gains: Highest average accuracy among binary hashing methods across ten node-classification benchmarks, with bitcodes built over an order of magnitude faster than NodeSketch (the abstract is cut off before the next comparison).
fbvBYNTB0C.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the empirical study is broad (ten datasets, many classifiers, ablations) and that compact node representations address a practical storage and serving cost.
fbvBYNTB0C.main_concern: Technical novelty is limited and no mathematical framework supports the claimed advantages, and some baselines are weakened (for example NodeSig reduced to 250 bits).

LRLaaxZhn8.one_liner: Diffusion transformer for 360-degree video frame interpolation with spherical position encoding, flow-aware attention, and panorama-aware pyramid fusion.
LRLaaxZhn8.problem: Equirectangular projection causes latitude-dependent distortion and a discontinuous longitude boundary, and large nonlinear motion complicates correspondence estimation and temporally coherent synthesis.
LRLaaxZhn8.method: MT-DiT blocks apply multi-head temporal attention over the input ERP frame pair and the intermediate-frame latent, with flow-derived motion embeddings combined with diffusion timesteps and frame differences modulating denoising through adaptive layer normalization. Spherical position encoding, flow-aware attention, and panorama-aware pyramid feature fusion handle ERP geometry.
LRLaaxZhn8.key_idea: Modulate DiT denoising with flow-derived motion embeddings and add spherical position encoding and flow-aware attention to handle ERP geometry.
LRLaaxZhn8.evidence: Experiments on WEB360, 360VDS, and FlowScape with individual and cumulative component ablations.
LRLaaxZhn8.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract; a review cites WEB360 LPIPS/FloLPIPS falling from 0.0154/0.0308 to 0.0141/0.0280 against the best baseline.
LRLaaxZhn8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the design addresses ERP-specific challenges reasonably and that perceptual gains are consistent across datasets, with ablations supporting the components.
LRLaaxZhn8.main_concern: The most relevant 360-degree diffusion baseline (DM-360VFI) is missing, the spherical boundary handling is insufficiently explained, and evaluation uses planar ERP metrics.

W0agadnRai.one_liner: Offline goal-conditioned value learning that adds a one-step TD target to divide-and-conquer transitive updates and reweights hindsight goals.
W0agadnRai.problem: Divide-and-conquer value learning values the luckiest trajectories under stochastic dynamics and gives no update to state-goal pairs that no trajectory connects.
W0agadnRai.method: GTRL adds a one-step TD target to the composition update, so every state-goal pair gets an update while the composition carries the long horizon. It also reweights each goal by how reachable it was from other successors to correct hindsight relabeling bias.
W0agadnRai.key_idea: Combines one-step TD targets with subgoal-composition (transitive) updates, plus goal reweighting by reachability from other successors to correct hindsight-relabeling bias.
W0agadnRai.evidence: Nineteen OGBench tasks spanning stochastic, deterministic, and stitching environments, with four seeds and ablations; propositions analyze failures of the tabular transitive update.
W0agadnRai.claimed_gains: Achieves the highest average success rate across nineteen OGBench tasks; no numeric margins stated.
W0agadnRai.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the limitations of the prior transitive method under stochastic dynamics and sparse trajectory coverage are well motivated by propositions, and the ablations support the components.
W0agadnRai.main_concern: The max-then-average target (Eq. 8) and behavior-policy goal weights (Eq. 9) can retain optimism, so the bias fix is not established, and some ablations change several factors at once.

d5sYlJxHoh.one_liner: Generative pretraining for unified multimodal models by predicting masked, multi-scale continuous visual-understanding features, coarse to fine.
d5sYlJxHoh.problem: Generative training of unified multimodal models does not necessarily improve understanding, possibly because generation targets synthesis-oriented spaces rather than the perceptual representation used for understanding.
d5sYlJxHoh.method: UMM-JEPA reformulates generation as progressive, masked next-scale prediction of continuous visual-understanding representations, building a coarse-to-fine hierarchy. Pixel rendering is decoupled from representation pretraining and attached only afterward (a pretrained FLUX.2 renderer per reviews).
d5sYlJxHoh.key_idea: Predicts masked, coarse-to-fine continuous perceptual (SigLIP2) features during generative pretraining instead of discrete codes or generative latents, decoupling pixel rendering.
d5sYlJxHoh.evidence: Controlled comparisons with a data-matched Qwen-VL control and against discrete-code (UMM-VQ) and latent-flow objectives over 16 visual benchmarks, plus linear probes and visual-evidence interventions.
d5sYlJxHoh.claimed_gains: 16-benchmark visual mean of 51.58 versus 46.33 for the understanding-only Qwen-VL baseline, with the text mean also rising.
d5sYlJxHoh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the generation-to-understanding hypothesis meaningful and credit the data-matched controls, consistent gains on visual understanding benchmarks, and the representation probes.
d5sYlJxHoh.main_concern: The contribution of the perceptual target and multi-scale masking is not isolated from prior feature-prediction work (MetaMorph, PUMA, Representation Forcing), and a single-scale unmasked SigLIP2 prediction baseline is missing.

Yrml4wmlZ5.one_liner: Long-context memory agent that appends selected evidence to memory instead of overwriting, with early exit and directly supervised control decisions.
Yrml4wmlZ5.problem: Memorize-while-reading methods overwrite memory repeatedly, risking information loss that retrieval cannot easily recover, and rule-based rewards only indirectly guide when to update memory and stop reading.
Yrml4wmlZ5.method: GraftMem separates evidence acquisition from incremental memory integration (AcIn updates) with selective memory updating and an early-exit mechanism. Training combines trajectory-level and state-level rewards with direct supervision of memory-update and early-exit decisions.
Yrml4wmlZ5.key_idea: Append-style selective memory integration replaces overwriting, and update and early-exit decisions are directly supervised alongside multi-level reward shaping.
Yrml4wmlZ5.evidence: Compared with MemAgent and ReMemR1 on multi-hop QA datasets (reviewers name HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, and SQuAD), with ablations of append versus overwrite, stress tests, and failure analyses.
Yrml4wmlZ5.claimed_gains: not stated (the visible abstract gives no figures).
Yrml4wmlZ5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the overwrite-induced information loss is clearly identified, the append design is practical, and the ablations support the mechanism.
Yrml4wmlZ5.main_concern: GRU-Mem, which already proposed update and exit gates, is not compared against, and training relies on annotated supporting-fact supervision that the baselines do not use.

EcWXPiIjBg.one_liner: One-shot federated LLM tuning that gives clients disjoint output indices in a 2D-DCT basis so their layer outputs stay orthogonal.
EcWXPiIjBg.problem: In one-shot federated adaptation, conflicts between local updates cannot be repaired in later rounds, and updates that are orthogonal as matrices can still conflict in the function the layer computes.
EcWXPiIjBg.method: They show excess risk splits into capture, noise, and interference terms and prove that disjoint output-index allocation in a shared orthonormal basis makes client layer outputs orthogonal for every input. FedDOSA trains sparse coefficients in a two-dimensional discrete cosine basis and has a coordinate-level variant.
EcWXPiIjBg.key_idea: Allocate clients disjoint output indices in a shared orthonormal (2D DCT) basis so their layer-output perturbations are orthogonal, removing interference exactly for a squared-loss linear layer.
EcWXPiIjBg.evidence: Theory with bounds that assume no distribution on the learned coefficients, and experiments on language-understanding and mathematical-reasoning benchmarks across multiple LLM backbones.
EcWXPiIjBg.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off; a reviewer reports 5.8-14.2 times fewer per-client upload parameters than one-shot baselines at competitive or better accuracy).
EcWXPiIjBg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating weight-space from layer-output orthogonality is useful and that FedDOSA gives a favorable communication-performance trade-off across backbones.
EcWXPiIjBg.main_concern: The theory covers disjoint output indices while the experiments use scattered-coordinate allocation, leaving residual interference unmeasured, and ablations do not separate sparse fine-tuning from the allocation scheme.

svzf40s02V.one_liner: Proves O(1/T) dual-energy convergence of clipped, centered SGD for semi-discrete optimal transport despite empty Laguerre cells.
svzf40s02V.problem: SGD on the Kantorovich dual of semi-discrete optimal transport can leave cells empty, making the bound on the dual Hessian's smallest positive eigenvalue vanish and breaking strong-convexity-based guarantees.
svzf40s02V.method: For quadratic cost, a compact convex source domain, and a positive bounded Holder continuous density, the authors bound the smallest positive Hessian eigenvalue linearly in the smallest cell mass and prove restricted strong convexity on a bounded region that includes empty-cell configurations. Clipping and centering keep iterates in this region, and MC-guided SGD uses sampled spectra to choose practical steps and can restart the guaranteed algorithm.
svzf40s02V.key_idea: Prove restricted strong convexity over a bounded potential region that includes empty cells, and keep SGD iterates inside it by clipping and centering.
svzf40s02V.evidence: Theoretical proofs plus experiments up to dimension 128 and 5000 targets comparing against a global schedule and projected SGD.
svzf40s02V.claimed_gains: O(1/T) expected dual-energy error with decreasing steps and weighted averaging, and experiments up to dimension 128 and 5000 targets show lower errors than the global schedule in many settings.
svzf40s02V.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the proofs are careful and clearly presented, with explicit constants and a Hessian eigenvalue bound that is linear in the smallest cell mass.
svzf40s02V.main_concern: Theory and experiments are disconnected: the guaranteed algorithm barely converges in high dimension, the practical variant lacks guarantees, and the contribution beyond prior O(1/T) results is questioned.

VZnSpEBANv.one_liner: Casts slate reranking as an MDP with display-or-discard assignment actions, using matrix-entropy Bellman operators and a Sinkhorn-based actor-critic.
VZnSpEBANv.problem: Existing sequential rerankers optimize proxy scores, fusion weights, or latent controls before decoding them into slates, creating an action-interface mismatch over K!/(K-N)! ordered slates.
VZnSpEBANv.method: MERA uses item-slot assignment probabilities as the policy, defines matrix-entropy-regularized Bellman operators with proven contraction, and parameterizes feasible assignment plans with O(KN) scores solved by Sinkhorn scaling. Critic action gradients at hard assignments sampled by Gumbel perturbation and Hungarian rounding guide a projected score-alignment actor update.
VZnSpEBANv.key_idea: Parameterize slates as entropic-transport item-slot assignment plans solved by Sinkhorn, and update scores with critic gradients at Gumbel-sampled, Hungarian-rounded hard assignments.
VZnSpEBANv.evidence: Two datasets with three simulators against seven baselines, with theory on Bellman contraction and a KKT decomposition of the marginal actor problem, plus latency measurements as candidate sets grow.
VZnSpEBANv.claimed_gains: Improves mean total session reward by up to 14.43% over the strongest of seven baselines per setting, with competitive session-level exposure diversity and low inference latency as candidate sets grow.
VZnSpEBANv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the display-or-discard assignment formulation is coherent, its critic evaluates the executed slate, and session rewards improve consistently across simulator-dataset settings.
VZnSpEBANv.main_concern: The theory does not match the implemented update, which uses a detached local critic gradient and a soft plan that differs from the executed policy, and the effect of these approximations is not quantified.

NpFwlYs130.one_liner: Multimodal knowledge-graph benchmark for plant enzyme-reaction prediction, framed as organism-disjoint link prediction with heterogeneous GNN baselines.
NpFwlYs130.problem: Existing benchmarks reduce identification of enzymes for plant biosynthetic reactions to isolated enzyme-reaction pairs, ignoring pathway and metabolite context, and there is no standard way to evaluate methods that use relational structure.
NpFwlYs130.method: PlantMetBench is built on PlantMetWiki, a curated knowledge graph spanning 424 organisms with 13,682 proteins, 2,741 genes, 4,577 metabolites, and 11,980 enzyme-reaction pairs. It provides graph-native splits, precomputed multimodal node features, and evaluation protocols, and evaluates HeteroSAGE, GAT, HGT, R-GCN, and residual and jumping-knowledge variants against non-graph models.
NpFwlYs130.key_idea: Frame enzyme-reaction prediction as organism-disjoint link prediction on a multimodal plant-metabolism knowledge graph so pathway and metabolite context can be used.
NpFwlYs130.evidence: Heterogeneous GNNs compared with non-graph baselines (BLASTp and a dual encoder according to reviews) under a transductive rank-based evaluation, with ablations of structural shortcuts.
NpFwlYs130.claimed_gains: Most heterogeneous graph architectures consistently outperform non-graph baselines under the default transductive setting on the rank-based evaluation; no numbers are visible in the truncated abstract.
NpFwlYs130.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it fills a gap with a standardized, carefully built benchmark that removes structural shortcuts and compares graph and non-graph models.
NpFwlYs130.main_concern: The default split is substantially transductive: 62.9% of test edges involve reactions already catalyzed by a training-organism protein, and P-H@50 falls from 66.0% on those to 12.6% on unseen reactions.

gMaDEkQLVU.one_liner: Long-term agent memory split into Active and Dormant sets by activation value, with dormant groups retrieved via summaries.
gMaDEkQLVU.problem: As agent memory grows, weakly related memories compete with relevant evidence, but deleting long-unused memories loses information that may become relevant again.
gMaDEkQLVU.method: FOCUS assigns each memory an activation value that governs transitions between an Active Set matched directly to queries and a Dormant Set stored in groups. Group summaries are matched to the query to select groups and guide retrieval of their full entries.
gMaDEkQLVU.key_idea: A reversible memory lifecycle moves memories between a searchable Active set and a summarized Dormant set by activation, controlling retrieval space without permanent deletion.
gMaDEkQLVU.evidence: LoCoMo and Memora with Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct and DeepSeek-V4-Flash against competing methods such as MemoryOS and LightMem, with ablations and repeated runs per reviews.
gMaDEkQLVU.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims significant memory-performance gains with the smallest retrieval space but is cut off before numbers)
gMaDEkQLVU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decoupling retention from direct searchability is a sound, practical design and that improvements across two benchmarks and two backbones are consistent.
gMaDEkQLVU.main_concern: The smaller retrieval-space metric does not measure total retrieval cost (dormant group search, much higher construction calls than LightMem), and novelty over MemoryOS, MemoryBank, and MemOS is overstated.

IhHpB4uQ38.one_liner: Derives partial information decomposition for multivariate Gaussians via the Blackwell order, with efficient algorithms and closed forms for two sources.
IhHpB4uQ38.problem: Redundancy and synergy lack a principled, efficiently computable partial information decomposition for Gaussian systems with arbitrary numbers of sources and dimensions.
IhHpB4uQ38.method: Uses the Blackwell order, which characterizes when one channel is more informative than another, and proves Gaussian channels are optimal for extracting Blackwell redundant and union information. Proposes efficient numerical algorithms and derives closed-form expressions for two sources.
IhHpB4uQ38.key_idea: Define redundancy and union information through Blackwell-order channel comparison and show Gaussian channels are optimal, giving a geometric interpretation and tractable optimization.
IhHpB4uQ38.evidence: Theorems with proofs, algorithms demonstrated on systems with up to a thousand dimensions or sources, a comparison with BROJA measures, and an optimal control example with sensor and memory.
IhHpB4uQ38.claimed_gains: Algorithms run on systems with up to a thousand dimensions or sources, and Blackwell redundancy is the only measure in the comparison meeting three natural desiderata.
IhHpB4uQ38.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the elegant geometric interpretation (Blackwell order, Loewner ordering, ellipsoid inclusion) and the computational efficiency of the convex formulations and closed-form two-source union information.
IhHpB4uQ38.main_concern: Novelty over prior Gaussian PID work (Kolchinsky 2022, Venkatesh 2023, Zhao 2025) is not sharply separated, and exact subspace-intersection redundancy can be discontinuous for sample covariances.

jqJ0brPRQV.one_liner: Quan-CEFT generates adapter parameters with a tensor-ring simulation of a Hamming-weight-preserving variational quantum circuit for efficient fine-tuning.
jqJ0brPRQV.problem: Quantum-inspired parameter adaptation reduces parameters in small language models, but variational quantum circuits face trainability and scalability problems.
jqJ0brPRQV.method: TR-HQG, a Tensor Ring simulation of a Hamming-weight preserving variational quantum generator circuit, delegates generation of circuit parameters to the TR network. All trainable parameters sit in classical TR cores and a Tensor Train mapping network, and the circuit acts only as a fixed forward-pass evaluator.
jqJ0brPRQV.key_idea: Generate circuit parameters from classical tensor-ring cores and a tensor-train mapping network, with the quantum circuit as a fixed evaluator meant to mitigate barren plateaus.
jqJ0brPRQV.evidence: Fine-tuning benchmarks on four backbones (GPT-2, OPT, Pythia, TinyLlama per reviews) with parameter-efficiency, latency and gradient-variance analyses; reviewers note results use only five optimization steps at batch size 2.
jqJ0brPRQV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method needs very few trainable parameters (about 18k) and that applying tensor-ring simulation to the quantum circuit is interesting and efficient, with a gradient-variance analysis.
jqJ0brPRQV.main_concern: Evidence is thin: results come from five optimization steps at batch size 2 where perplexity often worsens versus the base model, and no experiment shows TR-HQG is needed versus classical generators.

ZvyR7EkL6s.one_liner: Uses LLM-guided program search to generate heuristic reduction rules and policies for shrinking hard maximum independent set graphs.
ZvyR7EkL6s.problem: Exact reductions preserve optimality but leave difficult maximum independent set instances unchanged when their structural requirements are not met.
ZvyR7EkL6s.method: In reduce-then-solve, LLM-guided program search generates a fast reduction rule, selected for shrinkage, solution quality and runtime, before an exact solver runs. In reduce-as-solve, localized greedy trials guide decisions on the shrinking graph with a generated policy that uses cached trial solutions; rules and policies are generated offline on small synthetic graphs.
ZvyR7EkL6s.key_idea: LLM-guided program search generates offline a deletion rule and a cache policy over localized greedy trials, applied to hard graphs without further tuning or LLM calls.
ZvyR7EkL6s.evidence: Experiments on the evaluated methods for maximum independent set, including a comparison with exhaustive one-step rollout on 97 instances per reviews.
ZvyR7EkL6s.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers note clear writing, sound experiments and a useful quality-runtime trade-off, and credit the authors for being upfront that optimality guarantees are given up.
ZvyR7EkL6s.main_concern: Limited novelty and weak evidence of gains over simple hand-designed heuristics, with the methods tied to maximum independent set and a questioned fit to ICLR.

8HfqVT9TYa.one_liner: Federated multi-view clustering that uses observed labels for representation learning, consensus-aware view weighting, and must-link/cannot-link refinement.
8HfqVT9TYa.problem: Existing federated multi-view clustering is largely unsupervised and ignores available label information, limiting local representation discriminability and global consensus reliability.
8HfqVT9TYa.method: ASFMVC adds a label-guided representation generation mechanism, weights views by their discrepancy from the current consensus, and turns the same labels into signed pairwise must-link and cannot-link constraints. These parts form one alternating optimization framework with compact communication and linear complexity.
8HfqVT9TYa.key_idea: Observed labels enter both local representation learning and global consensus through signed pairwise constraints, while views are weighted by their discrepancy from the current consensus.
8HfqVT9TYa.evidence: Experiments on six benchmark datasets with ten repetitions, a communication-cost analysis, and a comparison with centralized semi-supervised methods per reviews.
8HfqVT9TYa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the setting is practically relevant and the manuscript is clearly organized, with a concrete communication analysis showing assignments and centroids are transmitted instead of full representations.
8HfqVT9TYa.main_concern: Comparisons are not matched: ASFMVC uses 20% labels against unsupervised federated baselines, no semi-supervised federated baseline is included, and the method largely builds on CeFMC with limited novelty.

TFfOE0cToy.one_liner: Fuses critic-LLM validation and generator uncertainty signals in a Random Forest, with conformal calibration, to abstain on wrong Text-to-SQL.
TFfOE0cToy.problem: Text-to-SQL systems often return queries that execute but answer the wrong question, and correctness against a gold query is unavailable at deployment.
TFfOE0cToy.method: A generator LLM writes and executes the query and a different critic LLM judges the query and its result; the critic's validation and execution-grounded alignment scores are fused with verbalized confidence, token-level uncertainty, and SQL-structural features in a Random Forest using two sequential LLM calls. A Learn-then-Test threshold bounds the error rate among accepted queries and a conformal p-value bounds false abstention.
TFfOE0cToy.key_idea: Separate generation from validation with a second critic LLM, fuse its scores with generator uncertainty features in a Random Forest, and calibrate the threshold with Learn-then-Test and conformal p-values.
TFfOE0cToy.evidence: Experiments on Spider with GPT-OSS-120B as generator and Gemma-4-31B as critic, threshold certification over 10 resampled splits, plus ablations and baseline comparisons.
TFfOE0cToy.claimed_gains: AUARC of 0.899; without abstention 22.6% of queries are wrong, and at a 15% risk budget (delta = 0.1) a threshold is certified on all 10 resampled splits while the system accepts 52.4% of queries on average.
TFfOE0cToy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is important and practical, the paper is clearly written, and the Spider results beat existing confidence-estimation baselines with finite-sample guarantees.
TFfOE0cToy.main_concern: Limited novelty (second-LLM judging and similarity-based confidence are established) and possibly unfair baselines, since the Random Forest is trained on labeled Spider data while competing methods are not, with evaluation mostly limited to Spider.

grmfOrVrsW.one_liner: Data fission plus partial-conjunction testing and online FDR control identify text passages whose watermarked-token proportion exceeds a threshold.
grmfOrVrsW.problem: Detecting watermark presence does not show that a substantial fraction of a passage is watermarked, and reusing the same evidence to locate and test a passage invalidates inference.
grmfOrVrsW.method: FissionGuard uses data fission to split each token-level p-value into an alarm value that guides alarms and passage localization and a validation value that yields a passage-level p-value through partial conjunction, excluding as many of the strongest signals as the proportion null allows. These p-values are tested at levels assigned by an online multiple-testing procedure.
grmfOrVrsW.key_idea: Data fission splits each token p-value into a localization value and a validation value; partial conjunction and online FDR control then test each passage.
grmfOrVrsW.evidence: Finite-sample FDR control is proved at every fixed finite horizon under the stated watermark generation model, with a finite-sample power lower bound; experiments use synthetic streams and Mistral and Qwen generations across four marking layouts.
grmfOrVrsW.claimed_gains: Higher watermarked-token coverage than sample splitting with empirical FDR below the target; no numbers stated.
grmfOrVrsW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the local watermark-proportion testing target is well motivated and the statistical argument (data fission, partial conjunction, online multiplicity control) is carefully structured.
grmfOrVrsW.main_concern: The guarantee depends on Assumption 3.1 (independent unused watermark randomness), and the model-generated corpora and temperatures were chosen during method development, so the text results lack independent validation.

wDdbsAaIE4.one_liner: Construction-derived translate-or-preserve labels measure whether vision-language models selectively translate image text.
wDdbsAaIE4.problem: Image-translation benchmarks overlook unwanted rewriting of text that users expect models to preserve.
wDdbsAaIE4.method: SPOT-Bench defines selective translation as deciding which image text to translate or preserve. It derives labels from image construction across advertisements, news, and captioned video and compares model decisions.
wDdbsAaIE4.key_idea: Derive per-text translation decisions from image construction and evaluate selective preservation separately from translation fidelity.
wDdbsAaIE4.evidence: The reviews describe evaluations of open and proprietary VLMs, guided-versus-unguided comparisons, and over-translation and under-translation diagnostics.
wDdbsAaIE4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that selective translation exposes a practical failure mode missed by conventional translation-quality metrics.
wDdbsAaIE4.main_concern: Multiple reviewers find the causal claim about knowing versus acting confounded by different prompts and privileged labels in guided conditions.

FONvtZxVvF.one_liner: Unified video-research tasks test external knowledge seeking, knowledge-guided observation, and open-web video discovery.
FONvtZxVvF.problem: Existing benchmarks fragment video research capabilities and underexplore using external knowledge to decide what to observe.
FONvtZxVvF.method: UNIVERSE combines supplied-video research and open-web discovery with knowledge-guided observation and image clues. Automated generation, multi-stage verification, and shortcut filtering construct the evaluation questions.
FONvtZxVvF.key_idea: Require agents to resolve indirect external clues before locating corresponding visual evidence, alongside observation-led research and open-web discovery.
FONvtZxVvF.evidence: The benchmark contains 800 questions across ten domains and evaluates proprietary and open-weight multimodal models in a shared tool-enabled framework.
FONvtZxVvF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the task decomposition, especially knowledge-guided observation as a complement to observation-driven research.
FONvtZxVvF.main_concern: Reviewers find benchmark quality and automated judging insufficiently independently calibrated, limiting confidence in reported rankings.

6UVD5xgshG.one_liner: Directional mesh propagation and grouped attention model atmospheric dynamics, while learned warping transfers global features into regional forecasts.
6UVD5xgshG.problem: Weather models struggle with spatial hierarchy, directional variation, and efficient long-range interactions.
6UVD5xgshG.method: AtmosWeave separates within-scale normalization from cross-scale fusion and uses geography- and state-conditioned grouped linear attention. CrossWarp learns feature alignment and selectively injects global information into regional representations.
6UVD5xgshG.key_idea: Separate mesh-scale propagation, route targets over grouped global summaries, and warp global features for selective regional injection.
6UVD5xgshG.evidence: Global and high-resolution regional forecasting experiments include ablations of the main modules and attention grouping.
6UVD5xgshG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the architectural motivation reasonable and value selective global-to-regional information transfer.
6UVD5xgshG.main_concern: Multiple reviewers request clearer distinctions and comparisons with closely related spatial attention and global-to-regional forecasting methods.

i8RkbVIASJ.one_liner: Semantic retrieval and column-norm rescaling repair fragile readout in residual-memory language-model editing.
i8RkbVIASJ.problem: Hash-based residual-memory retrieval fails under paraphrase and accumulates magnitude distortion through collisions over sequential edits.
i8RkbVIASJ.method: RECON replaces rigid hash lookup with gated dense semantic keys while preserving sparse support execution. It rescales retrieved dimensions by powers of relative column norms without retraining.
i8RkbVIASJ.key_idea: Decouple dense semantic routing from sparse support execution, then calibrate retrieved dimensions using relative residual-column norms.
i8RkbVIASJ.evidence: Experiments cover temporal, hallucination-correction, and sequential editing benchmarks across multiple models and edit horizons.
i8RkbVIASJ.claimed_gains: RECON nearly doubles out-of-distribution generalization over hash-based readout at T=10.
i8RkbVIASJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the readout-focused diagnosis and simple training-free combination of semantic routing and norm calibration.
i8RkbVIASJ.main_concern: Multiple reviewers question the causal evidence and added value of norm calibration beyond simpler normalization or scaling.

I9TzJPvjH9.one_liner: Occupancy-ratio factorization separates state and policy regularization while retaining strong duality for offline reinforcement learning.
I9TzJPvjH9.problem: A single joint occupancy penalty couples state-visitation shifts and action-quality shifts that require different control.
I9TzJPvjH9.method: SUNDER separates state and policy deviation penalties and derives a tractable dual through hidden convex structure. Instantiations address reward maximization, state-entropy maximization, and learning from observations.
I9TzJPvjH9.key_idea: Factor occupancy ratios into state and policy components and use hidden convexity to derive dual objectives with separate regularization strengths.
I9TzJPvjH9.evidence: The paper presents strong-duality results and evaluations on six reward-maximization mazes, 27 Minari tasks, and seven maze and four DMC entropy domains.
I9TzJPvjH9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the importance of separately controlling state and action distribution shifts and the unified DICE formulation.
I9TzJPvjH9.main_concern: Multiple reviewers question whether population-level duality results translate to practical neural optimization with additional variables and unreported computational costs.

pvJLsvZeAu.one_liner: Event dependency graphs turn static tool-use tasks into dynamic training scenarios with selectively updated verification.
pvJLsvZeAu.problem: Static training environments do not prepare agents for external events that invalidate ongoing plans.
pvJLsvZeAu.method: DynaWeave generates task-relevant external events and schedules them through dependency DAGs during interaction. A dynamic verifier updates affected checks, and verified trajectories train Qwen3.5 models.
pvJLsvZeAu.key_idea: Represent external-event dependencies as DAGs and revise only evaluation checks affected by activated events.
pvJLsvZeAu.evidence: Experiments fine-tune three Qwen3.5 model sizes using 2,095 trajectories across 36 environments and evaluate Gaia2, CostBench, and ToolMaze.
pvJLsvZeAu.claimed_gains: DynaWeave increases CostBench task completion by 67.34 percentage points and exceeds Gemini-3.1-Pro-Preview on ToolMaze.
pvJLsvZeAu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the reusable dynamic-scenario framework and evaluation across multiple model sizes and environments.
pvJLsvZeAu.main_concern: Reviewers find insufficient direct evidence that improvements reflect dynamic adaptation rather than general tool-use gains.

jtF7cAh4OE.one_liner: LLM-driven evolution uses solver runtime feedback to generate destroy heuristics for conflict elimination in multi-agent path finding.
jtF7cAh4OE.problem: Fixed destroy heuristics and map-specific learned models limit the adaptability of large-neighborhood-search pathfinding solvers.
jtF7cAh4OE.method: MAPF-Evo feeds solver runtime state and conflict structure to an LLM that evolves interpretable agent-selection heuristics. The evolved heuristic is added to the original solver's heuristic pool.
jtF7cAh4OE.key_idea: Evolve executable destroy heuristics from runtime conflict structure and repair feedback.
jtF7cAh4OE.evidence: Experiments compare solvers on five map types comprising 40 scenarios under a 100-second budget and longer budgets.
jtF7cAh4OE.claimed_gains: Under a 100-second budget, MAPF-Evo reduces mean remaining conflicting pairs by 38.42 % and mean resolution time by 8.49 % versus MAPF-LNS2.
jtF7cAh4OE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers consider conflict elimination a meaningful target and see value in exposing solver-state information to heuristic generation.
jtF7cAh4OE.main_concern: Reviewers find that comparisons do not sufficiently isolate the evolved heuristic's contribution from pool-size changes or existing evolutionary frameworks.

AXfZB3ctWw.one_liner: Candidate-specific evidence aggregation and counterfactual tests measure whether visual observations support the answer candidates they describe.
AXfZB3ctWw.problem: Visual evidence can change an answer without contributing to the candidate it actually supports.
AXfZB3ctWw.method: CROSS-Bench tests evidence invalidation and rebinding across decision problems. RIVET preserves evidence identity and uncertainty, groups observations by candidate before aggregation, and separately controls response strength.
AXfZB3ctWw.key_idea: Bind observations to candidates before aggregation and test whether invalidation removes their effect and rebinding redirects it.
AXfZB3ctWw.evidence: CROSS-Bench contains 28,000 decision problems, with matched counterfactual evaluations, repeated decision-layer fits, and experiments across four frozen backbones.
AXfZB3ctWw.claimed_gains: RIVET raises normalized effect transfer over Capacity-matched Fusion from 0.526 to 0.643 on 489 common clean-active examples and improves accuracy by an average of 5.70 pp over no-auxiliary baselines.
AXfZB3ctWw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate distinguishing evidence usefulness from whether its contribution reaches the correct candidate.
AXfZB3ctWw.main_concern: Reviewers question generalization beyond tasks with predefined evidence structures and restricted answer candidates.

n3egAaBsJd.one_liner: Hierarchical graph alignment segments oracle bone inscription components using image-level presence labels and reference component topology.
n3egAaBsJd.problem: Oracle bone component segmentation faces expensive annotations and substantial structural variation relative to standard components.
n3egAaBsJd.method: HiGAS builds segment, sub-stroke, and stroke graphs for characters and reference components. Within-level matching, cross-level priors, dynamic edge selection, and classification and completeness losses jointly predict component presence and edge segmentation.
n3egAaBsJd.key_idea: Align character and reference-component graphs within and across structural levels using topology and segmentation-completeness supervision.
n3egAaBsJd.evidence: Reviews discuss Component-50 presence prediction, Component-20 segmentation, and ablations of cross-level enhancement and completeness losses.
n3egAaBsJd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value weak supervision and find hierarchical graph alignment useful for structurally variable inscription components.
n3egAaBsJd.main_concern: Reviewers find the evaluation insufficiently specified or controlled to establish the source and generality of the reported gains.

YdqZ3fpEI4.one_liner: Interface estimation conditions joint flow matching of molecular glue generation and protein assembly into ternary complexes.
YdqZ3fpEI4.problem: Molecular glue design requires jointly determining an unknown protein interface, ligand chemistry, and ternary complex geometry.
YdqZ3fpEI4.method: TriGlue predicts a geometrically constrained protein interface from unbound monomers using an SE(3)-equivariant module. An interface-conditioned ternary flow-matching network jointly generates the glue and protein rigid-body transformations.
YdqZ3fpEI4.key_idea: Condition joint ligand generation and protein rigid-body assembly on an estimated protein-protein interface.
YdqZ3fpEI4.evidence: Experiments assess chemical validity and ternary-complex plausibility, with reviews noting interface-conditioning ablations and family adaptation experiments.
YdqZ3fpEI4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the joint formulation connecting molecular glue generation with protein assembly without a predefined binding pocket.
YdqZ3fpEI4.main_concern: Reviewers identify missing comparisons with contemporary all-atom docking and ternary-complex prediction approaches.

zIDXze2Uom.one_liner: Reconstructed feature tokens guide selective removal of historical batch updates from parameter-efficient test-time adaptation.
zIDXze2Uom.problem: Continually adapted models need to remove problematic past batches without historical raw inputs while retaining useful adaptation and source knowledge.
zIDXze2Uom.method: The method stores model states, reconstructs tokens representing requested batches through contrastive reconstruction, and selectively updates compact adaptation parameters. It defines a batch-level data-free untraining setting for continual TTA.
zIDXze2Uom.key_idea: Reconstruct surrogate tokens from stored adaptation states and use them to selectively reverse requested batch influences.
zIDXze2Uom.evidence: Reviews discuss CIFAR-100-C and ImageNet-C evaluations, sequential requests, reconstructed-token checks, and comparisons with reset, rollback, and Retain-Only Replay.
zIDXze2Uom.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that removing past batch influence during continual adaptation is a useful and clearly motivated problem.
zIDXze2Uom.main_concern: Reviewers find the advantage over simple source-reset and clean-rollback controls unconvincing.

vX6qpRGdHA.one_liner: Radially scaled Riemannian metrics establish global smoothness and convergence guarantees for objectives lacking classical Euclidean smoothness.
vX6qpRGdHA.problem: Some Euclidean optimization objectives, including certain neural-network losses, fail classical smoothness conditions needed for convergence analysis.
vX6qpRGdHA.method: The paper constructs conformally scaled and warped-product Riemannian metrics using radial scaling functions. It derives low-dimensional geodesic equations and relates the framework to generalized Euclidean smoothness criteria.
vX6qpRGdHA.key_idea: Choose radial conformal or warped-product metrics adapted to objective growth to establish global Riemannian smoothness.
vX6qpRGdHA.evidence: Theoretical results cover function classes including certain neural-network objectives, polynomially growing Hessians, convergence guarantees, and reduced geodesic equations.
vX6qpRGdHA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the objective-adapted geometric perspective interesting and theoretically valuable.
vX6qpRGdHA.main_concern: Reviewers find the practical optimization benefits and computational implications of the proposed geometry insufficiently established.

IE4Ym7L9Ho.one_liner: Supervised backdoor implantation and overseer-rewarded reinforcement learning train VLMs to rationalize trigger-induced wrong answers.
IE4Ym7L9Ho.problem: Reasoning-based oversight may miss backdoored visual answers when the accompanying reasoning conceals the trigger.
IE4Ym7L9Ho.method: Chain-Of-Lies first implants a visual backdoor through supervised fine-tuning, then uses GRPO to optimize stealth. A separate overseer VLM rewards reasoning that does not reveal the backdoor.
IE4Ym7L9Ho.key_idea: Train triggered answer errors with supervised fine-tuning, then optimize their explanations against an overseer that penalizes backdoor disclosure.
IE4Ym7L9Ho.evidence: Evaluations test Chain-of-Scrutiny defenses across Qwen3-VL, Gemma3, and Ministral-3, with ablations of training stages and curriculum.
IE4Ym7L9Ho.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers view manipulation of observable reasoning to evade oversight as an important security question.
IE4Ym7L9Ho.main_concern: Reviewers find the narrow task, trigger, oversight objective, and missing controls insufficient to support broad generality claims.

i7mkLC4f3Z.one_liner: RGB-predicted physical targets transfer scarce pressure, tactile, and torque supervision into latent-action learning from ordinary videos.
i7mkLC4f3Z.problem: Visual-change objectives supervise physical interactions only indirectly, while direct tactile and force measurements exist for few training videos.
i7mkLC4f3Z.method: PHYSLA learns a shared horizon-structured representation from heterogeneous physical measurements and predicts it from causal RGB observations. Inferred physical targets and future visual prediction jointly supervise latent actions during vision-language-action pretraining without deployment-time tactile sensing.
i7mkLC4f3Z.key_idea: Learn physical representations on instrumented interactions, predict them from RGB, and use these predictions as targets for latent actions on uninstrumented videos.
i7mkLC4f3Z.evidence: Evaluations include physical probes on unseen EgoTouch tasks, LIBERO and SimplerEnv policy tests, and real-world G1 manipulation.
i7mkLC4f3Z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value transferring heterogeneous physical supervision from limited sensorized data to larger video collections without requiring those sensors at deployment.
i7mkLC4f3Z.main_concern: The policy experiments confound physical supervision during pretraining with supervision during adaptation and lack matched physical-target ablations in key settings.

vpHv3h0nke.one_liner: Object-label hypothesis tests select supported crowd labels while controlling the false discovery rate and leaving weak evidence unresolved.
vpHv3h0nke.problem: Label aggregation often assumes one valid answer or preserves soft disagreement without guaranteeing an error rate over individually selected labels.
vpHv3h0nke.method: The framework treats each object-label pair as a hypothesis and uses aggregated annotation support for statistical selection. False discovery rate control bounds the expected proportion of invalid selections without requiring worker identities or a fixed valid-label count.
vpHv3h0nke.key_idea: Test each object-label pair and apply false discovery rate control to the collection of labels selected as valid.
vpHv3h0nke.evidence: The paper provides an assumption-dependent FDR guarantee and experiments on six real-world datasets, including null-calibration checks on ConvAbuse.
vpHv3h0nke.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value reframing multi-annotator label recovery as statistically controlled selection that permits multiple valid labels.
vpHv3h0nke.main_concern: The contribution relative to established statistical techniques and label-aggregation literature needs stronger positioning and comparison.

LvejZgL4de.one_liner: Direct latent forecasting predicts locations in parallel while a recurrent scale state carries volatility information across the forecast horizon.
LvejZgL4de.problem: Expressive sequence generation does not by itself specify how predictive uncertainty should evolve over long forecasting horizons.
LvejZgL4de.method: VolDy-VAE encodes historical patches variationally and projects all future latents in one pass, with a shared location decoder. A GRU carries scale state from historical to future patches, and heteroscedastic Gaussian likelihoods train reconstruction and forecasting.
LvejZgL4de.key_idea: Generate future locations directly while reserving recurrent computation for predictive scale and its historical volatility state.
LvejZgL4de.evidence: Nine long-horizon datasets and four horizons support CRPS comparisons with probabilistic and point forecasters, scale-head ablations, coverage measurements, and efficiency analysis.
LvejZgL4de.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating direct location prediction from recurrent scale estimation is a simple, economical forecasting design.
LvejZgL4de.main_concern: The experiments do not isolate the benefit of transferring historical scale state from generic recurrence or smoothing.

BSym3krUJl.one_liner: Contrastive learning over successful rollouts adds cross-trajectory regularization to reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards.
BSym3krUJl.problem: Outcome rewards accept reasoning trajectories with correct final answers but flawed intermediate steps, potentially encouraging shortcuts and poor generalization.
BSym3krUJl.method: CLIPO adds a contrastive mechanism based on existing successful rollout representations to several RLVR policy optimizers. The objective encourages common structure across outcome-correct trajectories without requiring process annotations or additional rollouts.
BSym3krUJl.key_idea: Use contrastive similarity among successful rollout representations to regularize policy optimization across reasoning trajectories.
BSym3krUJl.evidence: Experiments compare CLIPO additions to GRPO, GSPO, and DAPO across mathematical and general reasoning benchmarks, with reasoning-quality and significance analyses.
BSym3krUJl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers describe the contrastive addition as intuitive and clearly presented, with consistent reported gains across reasoning benchmarks.
BSym3krUJl.main_concern: Outcome-correct trajectories can share invalid shortcuts or follow different valid paths, so contrastive agreement does not establish sound reasoning.

MsZcdinQhI.one_liner: Controlled embedding examples separate high-dimensional semantic information from visual class structure in nonlinear two-dimensional maps.
MsZcdinQhI.problem: Practitioners can mistake visible clusters or mixing in low-dimensional maps for evidence of information present or absent in the original representation.
MsZcdinQhI.method: The study constructs information-ranking reversals and paired hiding-versus-erasure examples with similar visual mixing. It also compares class-conditioned neighborhood relations and individual-neighbor retention in nonlinear embeddings.
MsZcdinQhI.key_idea: Compare controlled representations with known information content against their visual mixing and class-neighborhood structure after nonlinear dimensionality reduction.
MsZcdinQhI.evidence: Controlled experiments examine t-SNE, UMAP, PaCMAP, and TriMap using rescaling, Hide/Erase examples, and RankBand neighborhood controls.
MsZcdinQhI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value examining the limits of inferring semantic information from widely used low-dimensional visualizations.
MsZcdinQhI.main_concern: The class-neighborhood analysis does not clearly establish added insight beyond neighbor purity and existing work on embedding pitfalls.

uRWzcbTKeX.one_liner: Per-voxel implicit quadrics recover continuous surfaces from sparse semantic occupancy and support direct sampling and LiDAR ray intersections.
uRWzcbTKeX.problem: Discrete voxelization discards sub-voxel surface geometry, limiting reconstruction fidelity and physics-aware sensor simulation.
uRWzcbTKeX.method: QuadricUNet predicts ten quadric coefficients per occupied voxel from a sparse semantic occupancy grid. Vectorized Newton-Raphson projection samples surfaces, and analytical ray-quadric intersections enable LiDAR simulation without mesh extraction.
uRWzcbTKeX.key_idea: Replace each occupied voxel with a predicted second-order implicit surface and perform geometric operations directly on its coefficients.
uRWzcbTKeX.evidence: SemanticKITTI and Waymo Open Dataset experiments compare reconstruction against UniScene, NKSR, and Marching Cubes under voxel-only inputs, alongside LiDAR simulation and transfer evaluations.
uRWzcbTKeX.claimed_gains: Dense sampling is more than twice as fast as learned implicit decoders, with Chamfer distance and F1@10 cm of 4.97 cm and 87.8% on SemanticKITTI and 5.43 cm and 84.1% on Waymo Open Dataset.
uRWzcbTKeX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value compact quadric surfaces and their direct analytical sampling and ray-intersection operations, supported by reconstruction experiments.
uRWzcbTKeX.main_concern: The comparisons do not sufficiently establish whether reconstruction gains arise from quadric representation or more general learned geometric priors.

bn94JD4zAS.one_liner: Redirect VLA action-to-image attention toward object regions via low-frequency RoPE query adapters while conserving total visual attention mass.
bn94JD4zAS.problem: Broad positional or attention interventions in Vision-Language-Action policies disrupt pre-existing motor control, leaving unclear how to inject object-region guidance without hurting action generation or requiring test-time object masks.
bn94JD4zAS.method: AfterImage introduces Conditional Object-Region Attention (CORA), a lightweight adapter on action-to-image queries that uses training-time object masks to redistribute attention within images while applying a log-sum-exp correction to preserve total visual attention mass, requiring no external perception model at deployment.
bn94JD4zAS.key_idea: Adapt only action-to-image queries with an attention-mass-preserving normalization under training-time object-region supervision so object guidance redistributes within-image focus without changing total visual attention.
bn94JD4zAS.evidence: Evaluated with closed-loop transfer rollouts on LIBERO-Plus across pi0 and pi0.5 VLA backbones alongside RoPE frequency-band sensitivity analyses.
bn94JD4zAS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that isolating object-region supervision to action-to-image queries while exactly preserving total visual attention mass is a clean, lightweight intervention that requires no masks at inference.
bn94JD4zAS.main_concern: Experiments lack comparisons to other mask-supervised VLA baselines (such as GuidedVLA) and ablations of budget conservation or trained RoPE frequency bands, while frozen-policy RoPE removal tests do not justify training only low-frequency dimensions.

NUpYeIRbkw.one_liner: Aggregate shared-prefix trajectory returns in an Action-Prefix Value Tree to supervise intermediate critic values and guide multi-turn agent rollout allocation.
NUpYeIRbkw.problem: Multi-turn LLM agents trained with sparse terminal rewards struggle to estimate accurate intermediate state values for credit assignment and efficient rollout exploration.
NUpYeIRbkw.method: TreePPO organizes multi-turn trajectories sharing ordered action prefixes into an Action-Prefix Value Tree (APVT) to compute empirical intermediate value targets for critic warm-up and training, while using the learned critic to adaptively allocate rollout budget to tasks with higher exploration potential.
NUpYeIRbkw.key_idea: Aggregate terminal rewards across branches of an Action-Prefix Value Tree to generate empirical intermediate state-value targets for the critic and guide adaptive rollout allocation.
NUpYeIRbkw.evidence: Evaluated on Multi-hop QA, ALFWorld, and WebShop benchmarks using Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct against GRPO, Tree-GRPO, and Turn-PPO.
NUpYeIRbkw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that coupling prefix-tree value estimation with critic-guided rollout allocation is well-motivated and consistently outperforms evaluated baselines across QA, ALFWorld, and WebShop at two model sizes.
NUpYeIRbkw.main_concern: The key ablation attributing the largest gain to the Action-Prefix Value Tree simultaneously alters at least five training factors (including critic warm-up and clipping) to match Turn-PPO, and closely related prefix-value methods (VinePPO, TRACE) are not compared.

scEiC3xEyd.one_liner: Cache 2-FWL Edge-Vertex Transformer graph encodings and select ordered vertex and pair states to amortize multi-query path prediction.
scEiC3xEyd.problem: Re-encoding an entire shared graph for every ordered path query is computationally expensive, while standard cached node embeddings lose pairwise relational expressivity along paths.
scEiC3xEyd.method: The authors introduce the Edge-Vertex Transformer (EVT) using direction-aware triangular attention to compute reusable vertex and pair representations, and StrikeTwice, which selects ordered vertex and pair states along a queried path and processes them with a second EVT stage.
scEiC3xEyd.key_idea: Precompute and cache vertex and pairwise graph states via direction-aware triangular attention, then index the ordered table of vertex and pair states along each queried path.
scEiC3xEyd.evidence: Supported by 2-FWL relative universality theorems and access-hierarchy expressivity separations, plus empirical benchmarks on synthetic tasks and two real-world applications (network routing on Atlas and protein biology).
scEiC3xEyd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating query-independent graph caching from ordered path readout is practically clean and backed by a rigorous 2-FWL expressivity hierarchy.
scEiC3xEyd.main_concern: Triangular attention incurs cubic compute and quadratic memory that limits experiments to small graphs (≤256 vertices), while empirical accuracy gains over simple MLPs or path transformers are modest, mixed across domains, and confounded by unmatched parameter counts.

35Jy8GSX6O.one_liner: Couples structured story-state video generation with Case-to-Pattern-to-Policy Evolution to turn recurring production failures into validated cross-story policy updates.
35Jy8GSX6O.problem: Adaptive long-horizon video systems refine single requests or reusable skills, leaving recurring failures disconnected from persistent, stage-targeted improvements across stories.
35Jy8GSX6O.method: CineForge-Produce structures stories into typed narrative, character, spatial, and cinematic states to coordinate asset and clip generation while recording canonical trajectories. CineForge-Evolve applies Case-to-Pattern-to-Policy Evolution (CPPE) to consolidate recurrent trajectory findings into bounded stage-local patches and deploy validated updates via structural replay and confidence-controlled paired evaluation.
