35Jy8GSX6O.key_idea: Record typed production states and consolidate recurrent trajectory failures into bounded stage-local policy patches validated via structural replay and paired evaluation.
35Jy8GSX6O.evidence: Evaluated across 100-script CineScope-Data and two public benchmarks against three long-video baselines using the human-aligned multiscale CineScope-Metric.
35Jy8GSX6O.claimed_gains: Improves CineScope-Metric from 4.02 to 4.38 across CineScope-Data and two public benchmarks, outperforming three long-video baselines.
35Jy8GSX6O.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper addresses an important cross-story transfer problem in agentic video generation with a well-structured separation between instance-level production and policy-level evolution.
35Jy8GSX6O.main_concern: Reviewers question the algorithmic novelty beyond prompt engineering and note that Appendix B.9 concedes the per-candidate numerical audit for the theoretical guarantees and deployed patches was not completed.

PLs454LkZw.one_liner: Decomposes monolithic neural network SDP verification into sequential layer-wise SDPs linked via Schur-complement-derived ellipsoidal quadratic constraints.
PLs454LkZw.problem: Monolithic end-to-end semidefinite programming formulations for neural network robustness verification scale poorly due to global coupling of decision variables across all layers.
PLs454LkZw.method: SL-SDP decomposes the verification problem into a sequence of smaller layer-by-layer SDPs linked through propagated quadratic constraints. It applies the Schur complement recursively to derive adaptive intermediate ellipsoidal bounds and neuron-wise pre-activation intervals that tighten ReLU layer relaxations.
PLs454LkZw.key_idea: Eliminate previous-layer variables via the Schur complement to propagate ellipsoidal quadratic constraints layer by layer and tighten ReLU relaxations.
PLs454LkZw.evidence: Theoretical soundness proofs and empirical robustness verification experiments on MNIST multilayer perceptrons (such as 4x100 and 9x150 MLPs) against end-to-end DeepSDP.
PLs454LkZw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the mathematically sound layer-by-layer decomposition using the Schur complement to propagate quadratic constraints and improve SDP scalability.
PLs454LkZw.main_concern: Reviewers note that empirical evaluation is restricted to 25 test samples on two MNIST MLPs and shows substantial losses in certified accuracy compared to monolithic DeepSDP and beta-CROWN.

pN0YpttTO0.one_liner: Distills future tactile change predictions into a vision-language-action policy via a frozen teacher, an adaptive assistant, and asymmetric attention.
pN0YpttTO0.problem: Forecasting and control impose different requirements on representations, making it difficult to preserve predictive tactile knowledge while adapting to action learning.
pN0YpttTO0.method: Teacher-Assistant Distillation (TAD) uses a frozen teacher that predicts future tactile change features and a teacher-initialized assistant that adapts under action supervision while anchored to the teacher, with an EMA of assistant prediction parameters providing distillation targets and its action readout supplying residual corrections to the denoising field. Asymmetric attention isolates predictive tokens from noisy action inputs while allowing action tokens to attend to predictive tokens.
pN0YpttTO0.key_idea: Transfer tactile prediction features through a teacher-anchored adaptive assistant with EMA distillation targets, residual denoising corrections, and asymmetric attention masking.
pN0YpttTO0.evidence: Instantiated on pi_0.5 and evaluated across eight UniVTAC simulation tasks and six real-world contact-rich manipulation tasks with component ablations.
pN0YpttTO0.claimed_gains: Achieves mean success rates of 90.0% across eight UniVTAC tasks and 87.5% across six real-world tasks, exceeding N_0-VTLA by 6.9 and 10.0 percentage points, respectively.
pN0YpttTO0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the teacher-anchored assistant formulation, the asymmetric attention mask that prevents action-input leakage, and the consistent gains across simulation and real-world robot tasks.
pN0YpttTO0.main_concern: Reviewers point out that ablations remove grouped components simultaneously (such as the assistant along with adaptive targets and residual corrections), leaving individual component contributions and asymmetric attention unisolated.

r1KLg6FR9A.one_liner: Trains an outcome-aligned latent privileged information analyzer from peer trajectories to weight on-policy self-distillation in agentic reinforcement learning.
r1KLg6FR9A.problem: Discrete textual privileged information blocks direct gradient optimization in on-policy self-distillation, while unconstrained learnable latent privileged information is not guaranteed to align its action influence with relative trajectory outcomes.
r1KLg6FR9A.method: PILOT constructs latent privileged information (PI) from source trajectories and measures its influence on same-task query trajectories via sampled-action log-likelihood differences with and without PI. With the actor fixed, it trains the PI analyzer to align average bounded influence with relative outcome credit from the on-policy rollout group, and uses the measured influence to weight an OPSD objective optimized jointly with direct RL.
r1KLg6FR9A.key_idea: Measure latent privileged information influence via log-likelihood differences on peer query trajectories and align that influence with group-relative outcome credit.
r1KLg6FR9A.evidence: Evaluated on ALFWorld and WebShop using Qwen2.5-3B and Qwen2.5-7B against GRPO, SDAR, and LOPD baselines.
r1KLg6FR9A.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper clearly formulates latent privileged information alignment for sparse-reward agentic RL and demonstrates strong benchmark results on ALFWorld and WebShop.
r1KLg6FR9A.main_concern: Reviewers question the novelty over recent peer-rollout and latent self-distillation methods (such as MOPD, GRSD, and LOPD) and the justification for aligning trajectory-averaged influence with coarse outcome rewards using only self-generated rollouts.

BKQTOdKMqB.one_liner: Separates task-defining object specifications from cached visual localizations and jointly optimizes reference revision and reasoning via counterfactual RL comparisons.
BKQTOdKMqB.problem: Reusing an incorrect early object localization in multi-turn visual reasoning propagates errors across subsequent questions, while historical-agreement rewards can penalize task-beneficial corrections.
BKQTOdKMqB.method: Introduces revisable references that decouple task-defining object information from the model's current localization estimates, alongside a binary repair model analysis. Referent-Preserving Policy Optimization (RP^2O) jointly trains revision and execution by comparing reference edits against retaining the original reference under the same executor and comparing continuations within the same edited state.
BKQTOdKMqB.key_idea: Decouple intended object specifications from localization estimates and optimize edits by comparing downstream execution utility against retaining the unedited reference.
BKQTOdKMqB.evidence: Theoretical characterization in a binary repair model and empirical evaluation under a controlled protocol assessing reference recovery, object preservation, and answer accuracy.
BKQTOdKMqB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clear distinction between preserving the intended task object and preserving a cached localization, as well as the controlled evaluation protocol using shared starting states.
BKQTOdKMqB.main_concern: Reviewers note that the RL training modifies multiple credit-assignment and baseline components simultaneously relative to GRPO without isolating each change or comparing against closer local-credit baselines.

cNx51wHAm7.one_liner: Embeds augmented Lagrangian dynamics with projected node-level linear feedback and edge penalties into GNN message passing for minimum vertex cover.
cNx51wHAm7.problem: In spherical minimum vertex cover relaxations, rotating a selected vertex away from a discrete cover reduces the objective at second order while squared edge penalties respond only at fourth order, failing to prevent local escape.
cNx51wHAm7.method: ALON combines gradient-based GNN message passing, projected node-level linear multiplier feedback that acts at second order to correct directional curvature, and an edge-wise penalty, compressing multiplier storage from edges to vertices. The paper also derives bounds on compression information loss, edge violations near discrete embeddings, and first-order residuals.
cNx51wHAm7.key_idea: Introduce projected node-level linear Lagrangian feedback into GNN message passing to provide second-order restoring curvature against fourth-order quadratic penalty relaxation defects.
cNx51wHAm7.evidence: Theoretical curvature and feasibility bounds plus experiments across 19 synthetic and real-world datasets and 76 backbone-dataset pairs, including the WS[100,200] split.
cNx51wHAm7.claimed_gains: Improves cover quality in 70 of 76 backbone-dataset pairs (tying 3), achieves best printed neural mean on 16 of 19 datasets, and runs about three orders of magnitude faster than directly solving the relaxation on WS[100,200].
cNx51wHAm7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers highlight the theoretical insight of Theorem 4.1 showing the second-order vs. fourth-order curvature mismatch in spherical MVC relaxations and the empirical improvements across GNN backbones.
cNx51wHAm7.main_concern: Reviewers point out a disconnect between theory and practice because dual multipliers are set to zero during inference, training trajectories are not shown to stay in the near-discrete regime, and classical solvers like NuMVC and FastVC outperform ALON.

AFN9LSvEMY.one_liner: Optimizes the deterministic phase-length schedule of Successive Rejects to maximize the H1-normalized worst-instance error exponent for best-arm identification.
AFN9LSvEMY.problem: Original Successive Rejects uses a predetermined phase schedule whose worst-instance error exponent normalized by the complexity measure H1(P) is suboptimal.
AFN9LSvEMY.method: Formulates deterministic equal-count phase-schedule design in fixed-budget best-arm identification as an optimization problem over the H1-normalized error exponent. Derives H1-balanced Successive Rejects (H1-SR) with an optimized deterministic elimination schedule.
AFN9LSvEMY.key_idea: Optimize the deterministic phase lengths of Successive Rejects to maximize the worst-instance error exponent normalized by the H1 bandit complexity measure.
AFN9LSvEMY.evidence: Theoretical optimality analysis for K>=2 Gaussian arms with common variance (and extensions to sub-Gaussian and bounded rewards) plus numerical experiments against original Successive Rejects.
AFN9LSvEMY.claimed_gains: Achieves at least 11/12 of the optimal H1-normalized rate over all adaptive algorithms for every K>=2, converging to 1 as 1 - O(1/log K) as K -> infinity.
AFN9LSvEMY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the algorithm simple and practical with a clean theoretical analysis that sharpens the H1-normalized error exponent without adding computational overhead.
AFN9LSvEMY.main_concern: Reviewers note that the phase schedule remains deterministic and non-adaptive to observed rewards, offering limited algorithmic novelty and lacking empirical comparisons against other adaptive baselines like Sequential Halving.

VEqQkvbOIx.one_liner: Generates 3D indoor scenes by converting inferred everyday activities into object requirements, assembling functional groups, and optimizing accessibility-aware room layouts.
VEqQkvbOIx.problem: Existing 3D scene generation methods rely primarily on object inventories and pairwise spatial relations, overlooking functional dependencies and human-use space required in inhabited environments.
VEqQkvbOIx.method: Lived-In by Design operates in three stages: a behavior-to-asset stage that converts agent-generated activities into object requirements and functional relations, a functional-group assembly stage that organizes related objects into local configurations, and a room-scale layout stage that jointly places groups under architectural, accessibility, and human usage space constraints.
VEqQkvbOIx.key_idea: Translate inferred human activities into behavior-asset dependencies, assemble objects into local functional groups, and place groups at room scale while preserving human interaction space.
VEqQkvbOIx.evidence: Evaluated on 179 room-level prompts using automatic metrics, qualitative comparisons, ablations, and a five-scene human judgment study.
VEqQkvbOIx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that grounding 3D scene generation in everyday activities, functional groups, and human interaction space is well-motivated and produces plausible room layouts.
VEqQkvbOIx.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the experimental validation because component ablations evaluate an unspecified prompt subset against the 179-prompt full method without a matched control, and key implementation details are missing.

wzHKaGw40Z.one_liner: Computes the affine preimage of an output affine space backward through products of non-square step-wise Jacobian matrices in automatic differentiation.
wzHKaGw40Z.problem: Standard inverse automatic differentiation solves point linear systems and cannot compute full affine solution sets across programs whose active variable counts expand and shrink across steps.
wzHKaGw40Z.method: Null-A mode preimage automatic differentiation represents affine spaces using a slice representation with delayed updates to propagate the largest input affine space X such that Jx lies in a target output affine space Y compositionally through a product of non-square primitive operation Jacobians J = J_{T-1} ... J_0.
wzHKaGw40Z.key_idea: Propagate affine space slices with delayed updates quasi-locally through a product of non-square step-wise Jacobians to compute full affine preimages.
wzHKaGw40Z.evidence: Evaluated on toy problems on CPU and small MLP and GPT-2 configurations on GPU against a conjugate gradients baseline.
wzHKaGw40Z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the generalization from point inverses to compositional affine preimages across non-square stepwise Jacobians via slice representations conceptually clean.
wzHKaGw40Z.main_concern: Reviewers note that experiments are restricted to small MLPs and toy GPT-2 setups compared only against uncalibrated conjugate gradients, without demonstrating scalability or practical advantages over standard backpropagation or LSQR/SVD solvers.

aPwzjjRItV.one_liner: Enforces task-dependent evidential authority constraints in clinical multimodal fusion using a specification compiler, protected graph mixer, and consistent projection.
aPwzjjRItV.problem: Standard multimodal fusion relies on predictive strength or reliability weights, failing to enforce which authoritative evidence source must constrain the final decision when sources conflict.
aPwzjjRItV.method: Authority-Consistent Fusion (ACF) combines a label-free Authority Specification Compiler that derives explicit authority constraints, an Authority-Protected Graph Mixer that blocks unauthorized information propagation into protected states, and an Authority-Consistent Projection that enforces admissible outputs under missing, invalid, or conflicting evidence.
aPwzjjRItV.key_idea: Compile task-specific authority constraints and isolate authoritative modality representations via protected graph message passing and output projection.
aPwzjjRItV.evidence: Theoretical guarantees (relation-preservation, fixed-parameter non-interference, conditional squared-loss bounds) and experiments on the synthetic Authority Identification Suite (AIS) and UTSW clinical dataset.
aPwzjjRItV.claimed_gains: On AIS, differs from learned-joint fusion by less than 7.0e-5 in mean clean Brier score with a zero S1 authority-violation rate (0.084-0.189 Brier increase under wrong specs), and achieves 6.49 and 2.48 mAP point gains on matched UTSW comparisons.
aPwzjjRItV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distinguishing evidential authority from predictive reliability is a meaningful formulation for clinical decision-making and appreciate the controlled experimental comparisons.
aPwzjjRItV.main_concern: Reviewers note that the core authority mechanism is primarily tested on synthetic two-modality tasks where learned-joint fusion already achieves zero violations, while the main text obscures key methodological details.

mEyIBW8E8K.one_liner: Benchmarks multi-turn academic paper search agents across 1,000 computer science topics and four research intents using a shared retrieval backend.
mEyIBW8E8K.problem: Existing literature search benchmarks do not systematically evaluate iterative, intent-driven LLM search agents in a reproducible open-literature retrieval environment.
mEyIBW8E8K.method: ScholarQuest organizes academic search queries across 1,000 computer science topics into four research intents (method-oriented, setting-anchored, comparison-based, and scope-controlled) paired with an iterative answer-construction pipeline and a frozen shared retrieval backend (ScholarBase) with a multi-turn search harness.
mEyIBW8E8K.key_idea: Evaluate multi-turn literature search agents and foundation models on a four-intent query taxonomy over a frozen shared paper corpus and search/expand harness.
mEyIBW8E8K.evidence: Evaluates nine literature search systems and six foundation models on ScholarQuest across recall, search efficiency, intent-level robustness, and failure modes.
mEyIBW8E8K.claimed_gains: The best-performing evaluated agent system achieves 0.312 Recall@100 and 0.352 Recall@All, outperforming single-shot retrieval baselines.
mEyIBW8E8K.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the reusable ScholarBase environment, the shared multi-turn evaluation harness, and the four-intent query taxonomy for standardized comparison of academic search agents.
mEyIBW8E8K.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about gold-answer completeness because candidate pools were generated by a single search-and-expand pipeline and human audits only checked precision on discovered papers rather than recall coverage.

LbmmEXoWLh.one_liner: Analyzes the expected runtime of crossover-based evolutionary neural architecture search and introduces a duplicate-based tie-breaking rule to preserve diversity.
LbmmEXoWLh.problem: It remains theoretically unclear when the crossover operator accelerates evolutionary neural architecture search (ENAS) and when applying it to similar individuals causes stagnation.
LbmmEXoWLh.method: Develops a runtime analysis framework that tracks both generational progress and regress for crossover-based ENAS on multiclass classification problems. Introduces a duplicate-based tie-breaking rule during survivor selection to eliminate identical or similar individuals and preserve population diversity.
LbmmEXoWLh.key_idea: Bound expected ENAS runtime by modeling per-generation progress and regress, and enforce population diversity via a duplicate-based tie-breaking selection rule.
LbmmEXoWLh.evidence: Theoretical expected runtime bounds and empirical validation on a multiclass classification neural architecture search benchmark.
LbmmEXoWLh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that theoretically analyzing when crossover and diversity preservation help in evolutionary neural architecture search is a relevant question for evolutionary computation.
LbmmEXoWLh.main_concern: Reviewers note that the theoretical analysis is restricted to one specific simplified architecture/task setup without proving crossover outperforms mutation-only search, and one reviewer identified mathematical errors in Theorem 3 and Equation 20.

gStXkqQmNk.one_liner: Measures LLM judge noncompliance when rubrics contradict prior preferences and optimizes the judge's system instruction using opposing synthetic rubrics.
gStXkqQmNk.problem: Pairwise LLM judges ignore explicit evaluation rubrics and retain their prior preference verdict on up to 23.6% of judgments when the rubric contradicts their initial preference.
gStXkqQmNk.method: Quantifies judge rubric stubbornness under rubric-preference conflict, then introduces RubricLens, which synthesizes two opposing rubrics per response pair (so one always conflicts with the judge's preference) and optimizes only the judge's instruction via GEPA to enforce compliance with both rubrics.
gStXkqQmNk.key_idea: Synthesize opposing rubrics for each response pair and optimize the judge's instruction with GEPA so the judge flips its verdict according to whichever rubric is provided.
gStXkqQmNk.evidence: Evaluated across four LLM judges and four preference datasets, plus held-out datasets and expert-written rubrics.
gStXkqQmNk.claimed_gains: Raises average rubric agreement under preference conflict from 86.2% to 92.6% across four judges and four datasets, lowering the prior-preference retention rate from up to 23.6% to at most 13.9%.
gStXkqQmNk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating whether LLM judges follow rubrics that contradict their own priors is an important practical problem and that RubricLens transfers across datasets and expert rubrics.
gStXkqQmNk.main_concern: Reviewers point out that synthetic rubrics may contain ambiguity or label noise that confounds the stubbornness metric, and experiments lack a manually engineered meta-prompt baseline to isolate automated prompt search from simply writing explicit conflict-resolution instructions.

roVJ18DcwM.one_liner: Models synthesis, imputation, and conditional generation on unseen tables as joint in-context conditional diffusion over arbitrary target cell sets.
roVJ18DcwM.problem: Existing tabular generative models either require table-specific training or restrict in-context learning to single-cell prediction rather than joint multi-cell generation.
roVJ18DcwM.method: TabMosaic formulates tabular generation as modeling the joint conditional distribution of an arbitrary set of mixed-type target cells given observed cells in an unseen table, trained via a joint diffusion denoising objective that bounds the conditional negative log-likelihood and divergence from the posterior predictive distribution.
roVJ18DcwM.key_idea: Apply a joint in-context diffusion denoising objective over arbitrary subsets of target cells conditioned on observed cells in unseen tables without table-specific tuning.
roVJ18DcwM.evidence: Theoretical posterior-predictive divergence bounds and empirical evaluation across 48 real-world tables against 20 baseline methods covering unconditional generation, imputation, and conditional generation.
roVJ18DcwM.claimed_gains: Ranks first on all evaluated generative tasks across 48 real-world tables against 20 baseline methods.
roVJ18DcwM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the unified formulation of multiple tabular generative tasks via joint conditional diffusion and the broad zero-shot evaluation on unseen tables.
roVJ18DcwM.main_concern: Reviewers note that Stage 2 pretraining bundles multiple factors (context length, missingness augmentation, multi-corruption sampling) without isolating their individual contributions, and evaluation excludes high-dimensional tables (>212 features).

kbNjFLXanS.one_liner: Characterizes the finite-rank mean field and variance of low-rank Evolution Strategies (EGGROLL) and replaces antithetic evaluations with a leave-one-out estimator.
kbNjFLXanS.problem: Low-rank Gaussian perturbations in EGGROLL lie in a zero-volume subset of matrix space and require two antithetic forward passes per direction, while their finite-rank update geometry and variance are poorly understood.
kbNjFLXanS.method: Derives the EGGROLL update mean field at finite rank and nonzero radius as a resolvent applied to the smoothed gradient—showing it can be nonconservative yet exact on quadratics with extra variance decaying inversely with matrix width—and introduces LOO-ROLL, a leave-one-out estimator that uses one evaluation per direction instead of two antithetic passes.
kbNjFLXanS.key_idea: Replace EGGROLL's two antithetic function evaluations per low-rank perturbation direction with a single-evaluation leave-one-out population baseline backed by an exact variance criterion.
kbNjFLXanS.evidence: Theoretical mean-field and finite-population variance proofs plus matched-time empirical comparisons across 14 LLM post-training settings up to 14B parameters.
kbNjFLXanS.claimed_gains: Additional sampling variance of rank-one perturbations relative to dense Gaussian ES decays inversely with matrix width and is 0.098% at width 4096.
kbNjFLXanS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the rigorous finite-rank theoretical analysis explaining why rank-one weight perturbations remain effective at large matrix widths and appreciate the practical matched-time throughput gains.
kbNjFLXanS.main_concern: Reviewers view the LOO-ROLL algorithmic modification as a standard leave-one-out variance-reduction baseline applied to EGGROLL, and note the theoretical nonconservative pathology and affine variance reductions are not directly demonstrated on full LLM training rewards.

LYlcgKWVcC.one_liner: Allocates a small budget of reliable oracle queries to inputs where candidate programs disagree and ranks candidates by calibrated answer likelihood.
LYlcgKWVcC.problem: Selecting candidate programs by counting passed model-generated tests depends solely on inputs where candidates disagree, where a same-model oracle often favors incorrect candidates despite high overall accuracy.
LYlcgKWVcC.method: Analyzes candidate comparison on the disagreement set, proving that pass-count selection fails when the oracle is biased on disagreement inputs whereas calibrated likelihood scoring remains consistent at a rate governed by Hellinger distance. Proposes DisJudge, which queries a reliable oracle on a small fraction of disagreement inputs and ranks candidates using the calibrated likelihood of all oracle answers.
LYlcgKWVcC.key_idea: Concentrate reliable oracle queries exclusively on inputs where candidate programs produce different outputs and rank candidates via calibrated likelihood aggregation.
LYlcgKWVcC.evidence: Theoretical consistency and Hellinger rate proofs plus experiments across six code benchmarks and 18 benchmark-generator settings.
LYlcgKWVcC.claimed_gains: Shows a same-model oracle with 87.3% overall accuracy favors wrong candidates 51.1% vs. 37.2% on the disagreement set; with 0.2 reliable calls per disagreement input, DisJudge raises mean selection accuracy over 18 settings from 54.8% to 60.5%.
LYlcgKWVcC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that isolating oracle bias on the candidate disagreement set is an insightful diagnostic for execution-based code selection.
LYlcgKWVcC.main_concern: Reviewers note that querying disagreement sets and aggregating via confusion matrices closely follows classic active learning and crowd-labeling (Dawid-Skene/Noisy GBS), while relying on oracle error-independence assumptions and reference calibration data.

F9T6ibYerk.one_liner: Partitions KV cache keys into pages and scores pages for retrieval using query-covariance co-retrieval geometry and spread-aware attention mass estimation.
F9T6ibYerk.problem: Existing KV paging methods construct pages with heuristics and score them with separate criteria rather than optimizing whether keys in a page are retrieved together.
F9T6ibYerk.method: TesseraKV formulates KV page partitioning and page scoring from co-retrieval—grouping keys whose attention logits co-vary under the head's query distribution using a covariance-weighted geometry estimated from prefill and instruction queries, and scoring pages with a spread-aware approximation of page attention mass.
F9T6ibYerk.key_idea: Cluster KV cache keys under query-covariance geometry so keys whose attention logits co-vary share a page, and score pages with a spread-corrected attention mass estimator.
F9T6ibYerk.evidence: Evaluated on retrieval, long-document (RULER), and agentic workloads (Claw-Eval) with a working GPU implementation and partitioning/scoring ablations.
F9T6ibYerk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the principled co-retrieval formulation linking covariance-based KV partitioning with spread-aware page scoring and note strong quality gains at small KV budgets.
F9T6ibYerk.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the deployed linear spread correction differs from the theoretically derived quadratic formula and is sensitive to hyperparameter tuning, while direct latency comparisons against competing KV retrieval baselines are missing.

p7Wj8b6F5J.one_liner: Early-exit-aware partitioning aligns network stages with exits and allocates distributed capacity according to each stage's remaining inference traffic.
p7Wj8b6F5J.problem: Naive partitioning of early-exit networks creates uneven downstream workloads and can erase early exits' computational benefits.
p7Wj8b6F5J.method: The strategy aligns partition boundaries with exit locations, selects active co-located exit heads, and allocates stage capacity proportionally to inference load. Reviews describe stage replication and dynamic stage in-lining as mechanisms for handling computation and communication bottlenecks.
p7Wj8b6F5J.key_idea: Match partition boundaries and stage compute capacity to exit locations and non-exiting sample arrival rates.
p7Wj8b6F5J.evidence: Real-machine experiments evaluate DenseNet-121, ResNet-50, and AlexNet on ImageNet, CIFAR-100, and CIFAR-10.
p7Wj8b6F5J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that early exits create a practically important distributed-load problem and value real-hardware evaluation.
p7Wj8b6F5J.main_concern: Missing matched baselines and changing hardware allocation prevent isolating the benefit of the proposed partitioning and scheduling strategy.

eKKO4iT5iL.one_liner: MoRSE trains one compact EEG encoder with random electrode subsets, task labels, expert logits, and foundation-model feature alignment.
eKKO4iT5iL.problem: Task-specific fine-tuning often removes EEG foundation models' montage flexibility and leaves a large model to deploy for each task.
eKKO4iT5iL.method: MoRSE distills task experts and a frozen foundation backbone into a shared small encoder. Each training step samples an electrode subset and combines label supervision with logit distillation and per-patch feature alignment.
eKKO4iT5iL.key_idea: Randomize electrode subsets while jointly training a compact multi-task student with task supervision, expert logits, and backbone feature alignment.
eKKO4iT5iL.evidence: Evaluations cover eight EEG tasks and 30 task-by-montage cells, with specialist comparisons, montage-sampling controls, and external sleep cohorts.
eKKO4iT5iL.claimed_gains: Across 30 task-by-montage cells, a single 1.97M-parameter encoder trails per-cell specialists by 0.029 balanced accuracy.
eKKO4iT5iL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value practical consolidation across tasks and electrode layouts and comparisons against montage-sampled specialists.
eKKO4iT5iL.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the teacher-role explanation and expert-logit distillation contribute beyond montage sampling and feature alignment.

DlO53FBynm.one_liner: ScienceCUA converts software documentation into skills and references, then revises skills using validated contrasts between successful and failed executions.
DlO53FBynm.problem: Scientific computer-use agents lack reusable operational expertise aligned with deployed software versions and actual task requirements.
DlO53FBynm.method: ScienceCUA derives reusable workflows from documentation and stores command syntax separately for lookup. Execution feedback contrasts successful and failed attempts to revise or add skills, accepting library updates after repeated environment validation.
DlO53FBynm.key_idea: Separate documentation-derived workflows from syntax references, then update skills through success-failure comparisons and repeated execution validation.
DlO53FBynm.evidence: Evaluation uses corrected scientific-software benchmarks with 168 test tasks across six applications and 108 evolution tasks.
DlO53FBynm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value organizing software expertise into operational skills and references and improving the reliability of scientific-agent evaluation.
DlO53FBynm.main_concern: Reviewers question transfer beyond familiar workflows because evolution and test tasks share operation types despite differing objects or parameters.

qpsH7K01gV.one_liner: PRC reweights positive contrastive pairs using class-posterior similarity from a classifier trained on noisy labels.
qpsH7K01gV.problem: Sample-level reliability overlooks how one wrong label corrupts specific positive relations in supervised contrastive learning.
qpsH7K01gV.method: PRC trains a classifier once on noisy labels and computes the inner product of its class-probability vectors for each observed positive pair. These scores determine each pair's share of the positive target in the SupCon loss.
qpsH7K01gV.key_idea: Use fixed classifier posterior inner products to assign relation-specific positive-target weights in supervised contrastive learning.
qpsH7K01gV.evidence: Controlled CIFAR-10/100 experiments compare sample weighting and randomly reassigned pair weights, alongside linear-probe evaluations on synthetic and real-world noisy benchmarks.
qpsH7K01gV.claimed_gains: PRC outperforms per-sample weighting by 1.38/1.82 pp and random weight reassignment by 2.78/4.25 pp on CIFAR-10/100.
qpsH7K01gV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the useful distinction between sample and relation reliability and the simplicity of pairwise weighting.
qpsH7K01gV.main_concern: Reviewers question reliance on the noisy-label auxiliary classifier and request stronger justification and controls for its contribution and cost.

URKzKAx6R0.one_liner: Visual scaffolding retrieves native visual features during reasoning and retains them as reusable states alongside textual chain-of-thought.
URKzKAx6R0.problem: Textual reasoning cannot concisely preserve all visual distinctions needed for subsequent multimodal reasoning steps.
URKzKAx6R0.method: The model autonomously initiates visual retrieval during reasoning, and a lightweight retriever inserts selected native visual features into the evolving context. NMR-Bench tests this mechanism through Burden Counting and Path Tracing.
URKzKAx6R0.key_idea: Insert context-selected native visual features into the reasoning sequence and preserve them for reuse by later steps.
URKzKAx6R0.evidence: Experiments use Qwen3-VL-4B-Thinking on two NMR-Bench tasks, with visual-content replacement and fixed-text interventions testing the role of inserted features.
URKzKAx6R0.claimed_gains: With 88M added parameters (approximately 2%), the model achieves 66.43% and 72.50% accuracy on Burden Counting and Path Tracing, respectively.
URKzKAx6R0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value persistent visual intermediate states and the intervention evidence that inserted visual content affects later computation.
URKzKAx6R0.main_concern: Reviewers find the relationship to prior interleaved and latent visual reasoning methods insufficiently discussed or experimentally compared.

YV5xb6GZ88.one_liner: RealHop reconstructs multi-hop evidence with entity rebinding and competing paths, then audits necessity through targeted evidence removal.
YV5xb6GZ88.problem: Correct answers on annotated multi-hop benchmarks do not establish dependence on every intended reasoning step.
YV5xb6GZ88.method: RealHop diagnoses evidence dependence using Behavioral Necessity Rate, then rebinds entities, factorizes relations, and adds complete competing paths at traceable locations. Structural and semantic checks precede dataset freezing and behavioral deletion tests.
YV5xb6GZ88.key_idea: Construct traceable competing evidence paths and measure whether removing each intended support prevents answer recovery.
YV5xb6GZ88.evidence: The study audits six benchmarks and tests 790 paired MuSiQue questions, with RealHop-FRAMES, RealHop-LongBench, and background-deletion controls.
YV5xb6GZ88.claimed_gains: On 790 paired MuSiQue questions, RealHop raises panel-mean BNR from 27.4% to 94.4% while retaining high Full accuracy.
YV5xb6GZ88.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value controlled evidence-deletion audits showing dependence beyond answer correctness and background-removal effects.
YV5xb6GZ88.main_concern: Reviewers question whether paragraph-level deletion and averaged BNR establish individual-hop necessity rather than broader evidence dependence or alternative valid answer paths.

npbzqFj3oD.one_liner: Answer-conditioned visual attention redistributes token credit while preserving the GRPO trajectory-mean advantage.
npbzqFj3oD.problem: Sequence-level rewards leave differences in visual-evidence use across generated tokens implicit.
npbzqFj3oD.method: VAttnPO teacher-forces the correct answer through a frozen old policy to construct a visual-attention reference and compares rollout-token attention using Jensen–Shannon divergence. Centering, position weighting, and balancing convert agreement into zero-mean corrections to GRPO advantages.
npbzqFj3oD.key_idea: Center and balance position-weighted agreement between rollout attention and answer-conditioned visual attention to redistribute token advantages without changing their trajectory mean.
npbzqFj3oD.evidence: Experiments on Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct include multimodal benchmarks, token interventions, visual-index permutations, and trajectory analyses.
npbzqFj3oD.claimed_gains: On Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, six-task image AVE rises from 70.97 with GRPO to 73.50.
npbzqFj3oD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers support visual-attention-based token credit assignment and the breadth of multimodal evaluations.
npbzqFj3oD.main_concern: Comparisons omit directly relevant methods that already use token-level visual signals for credit assignment.

ir4mgPPuqZ.one_liner: Adaptive shot segmentation and evidence-grounded scoring evaluate multi-shot audio-video generation across video, audio, shot, and reference dimensions.
ir4mgPPuqZ.problem: Existing benchmarks lack the coverage and adaptable evaluation procedures needed for multi-shot audio-video narratives.
ir4mgPPuqZ.method: MSAVBench combines diverse multi-shot prompts with an evaluator that self-corrects shot segmentation. Instance-specific rubrics and tool-grounded evidence support subjective and complex judgments.
ir4mgPPuqZ.key_idea: Combine self-correcting shot segmentation with instance-specific rubrics and tool-extracted evidence to score multi-shot audio-video outputs.
ir4mgPPuqZ.evidence: Evaluation covers 20 models and sequences of up to 15 shots, with corruption tests, human comparisons, and an alternative VLM evaluator.
ir4mgPPuqZ.claimed_gains: The evaluator reaches a Spearman rank correlation of 91.5% with human judgments.
ir4mgPPuqZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the benchmark's coverage of multi-shot audio-video generation and its carefully designed evaluation data.
ir4mgPPuqZ.main_concern: Unclear aggregate scoring choices and limited validation undermine confidence in leaderboard comparisons.

utO4V2EgQN.one_liner: Paired task variations measure whether agents address ethical issues during realistic professional work without explicit ethics prompts.
utO4V2EgQN.problem: Direct ethics questions do not measure whether agents recognize ethical issues during ordinary professional tasks.
utO4V2EgQN.method: The benchmark varies ethical presentation across seven conditions for practitioner-authored GDPval tasks. Sandboxed agents complete the tasks, and three LLM judges apply a seven-dimension rubric calibrated against human ratings.
utO4V2EgQN.key_idea: Compare ethical engagement on paired professional tasks whose conditions vary ethical presentation, including inert additions and content-preserving cue removal.
utO4V2EgQN.evidence: Nine models attempt 150 tasks under seven conditions with rubric validation against 1,444 human raters, while seven frontier models receive baseline-only evaluation.
utO4V2EgQN.claimed_gains: Pooled scores rise from 19.2 at baseline to 52.5 with explicit ethical content, while ethically inert additions change scores by -0.5 points.
utO4V2EgQN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value realistic agentic tasks and the effort to validate ethical-engagement measurements.
utO4V2EgQN.main_concern: Task enrichment changes stakeholders, conflicts, and requirements, so the main comparison does not isolate spontaneous ethical recognition.

aFBh16dA6X.one_liner: Independent Gaussian testing and exploration calibrate policy updates for sharp regret bounds in linear contextual bandits.
aFBh16dA6X.problem: Linear contextual bandits need uniformly sharp regret across action-set sizes while limiting policy updates.
aFBh16dA6X.method: GATE separates Gaussian testing from exploration and jointly calibrates thresholds using direct prediction-error control. An additive Gaussian-max information inequality connects action-set complexity and design growth without computing Gaussian width.
aFBh16dA6X.key_idea: Use independent Gaussian testing and exploration with jointly calibrated thresholds and an additive information inequality to control stale-policy prediction errors.
aFBh16dA6X.evidence: Regret upper bounds, a feedback lower bound, and worst-case sharpness of the Gaussian-max inequality support guarantees under oblivious adversarial contexts.
aFBh16dA6X.claimed_gains: GATE achieves O(sqrt(dT log(1+T/d) min{d,log K})) regret with O(d log(1+T/d) log(2+log(2+min{d,log K}))/log(2+min{d,log K})) policy updates.
aFBh16dA6X.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the combination of sharp regret across small- and large-action regimes and limited policy updates.
aFBh16dA6X.main_concern: Dense notation and insufficient motivation obscure the algorithm's design and the source of its guarantees.

AOX6NE4Me8.one_liner: Proves benign-leakage conditions fail under partial concept interventions and introduces a pairwise monotonic intervention loss for leaky concept models
AOX6NE4Me8.problem: Leaky concept-based models satisfying prior benign-leakage criteria or trained only on full concept interventions can still suffer degraded task accuracy when users intervene on a subset of concepts.
AOX6NE4Me8.method: The authors formalize partial intervention harm, prove via counterexample that concept sufficiency and localization do not prevent partial-correction degradation, and link incomplete concept supervision to increased harm. They introduce a pairwise monotonic intervention hinge loss applied along sampled partial-intervention paths to penalize prediction degradation as additional ground-truth concepts are revealed.
AOX6NE4Me8.key_idea: Penalize task-loss increases between consecutive steps of sampled partial concept interventions using a pairwise hinge objective so revealing true concepts monotonically improves predictions.
AOX6NE4Me8.evidence: Supported by theoretical counterexamples against sufficiency and localization conditions and experiments with leaky Hybrid CBMs on synthetic data and the CUB dataset.
AOX6NE4Me8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper cleanly proves via counterexamples that prior benign-leakage conditions and endpoint-only training fail to prevent accuracy drops during partial human concept interventions.
AOX6NE4Me8.main_concern: Experiments test only synthetic data and CUB with linear heads (omitting architectures like CEM and IntCEM and broader datasets) and lack a baseline trained with plain task loss on identical sampled partial-intervention states.

ptjp9xbq4q.one_liner: Retargets human manipulation videos to dexterous robot hands via embodiment-adapted contact kinematics and spherical-Gaussian differentiable physics refinement
ptjp9xbq4q.problem: Morphology differences and brittle contact dynamics cause kinematic human-to-robot hand retargeting from video to slip or fail physical execution across diverse dexterous robot hands.
ptjp9xbq4q.method: DexForge reconstructs hand-object motion and spherical-Gaussian object geometry from video and embeds Gaussian collision detection inside a differentiable physics simulator. It first jointly optimizes robot-adapted stable contact anchors and kinematic hand trajectories, then refines control trajectories via force-aware gradients through the differentiable dynamics.
ptjp9xbq4q.key_idea: Jointly adapt human contact anchors to robot hand kinematics and refine control trajectories with gradients through spherical-Gaussian collision and differentiable rigid-body dynamics.
ptjp9xbq4q.evidence: Evaluated on 130 demonstrations from DexYCB and HOT3D across seven dexterous robot hand embodiments, with open-loop transfer to MuJoCo and real-robot grasp-and-hold execution.
ptjp9xbq4q.claimed_gains: Achieves success-rate gains of approximately 35–53 percentage points over the baseline across 130 DexYCB and HOT3D demonstrations on seven dexterous hands, with object position and orientation tracking errors on successful trajectories reduced by approximately 34–67% and 71–78%.
ptjp9xbq4q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly adapting contact anchors to robot hand morphology before differentiable-physics refinement is effective and broadly tested across seven dexterous hands on DexYCB and HOT3D.
ptjp9xbq4q.main_concern: Tracking metrics compare against noisy video-reconstructed references rather than dataset ground truth, real-world tests only check static 5-second grasp-and-hold without baselines, and spherical-Gaussian geometry is not ablated against standard collision representations.

KuYnsTfsDe.one_liner: Interpolates between uniform and single-trajectory reveal-order distributions using token confidence for reinforcement learning in masked diffusion models.
KuYnsTfsDe.problem: Reinforcement learning for masked diffusion language models lacks a tractable sequence likelihood surrogate between uniform ELBO bounds and single-trajectory approximations.
KuYnsTfsDe.method: The authors express the exact log-likelihood policy gradient as an expectation under the posterior over reveal orders, showing ELBO and trajectory-based RL correspond to uniform and Dirac distributions. They introduce a temperature-controlled, confidence-based family of reveal-order distributions that reuses existing model predictions without extra forward evaluations.
KuYnsTfsDe.key_idea: Weight per-order log-likelihood gradients using a temperature-controlled confidence distribution over token reveal orders that interpolates between uniform and Dirac extremes.
KuYnsTfsDe.evidence: Supported by policy-gradient error bound analysis and experiments on mathematical reasoning and planning tasks.
KuYnsTfsDe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that unifying ELBO-based and trajectory-based RL through reveal-order distributions is clear and requires no additional forward passes on planning tasks.
KuYnsTfsDe.main_concern: There is a mismatch between the theoretical posterior gradient formulation and the practical confidence-based sampling and step-merging implementation.

cdFj9zgZhp.one_liner: Injects hashed N-gram embeddings into Hyper-Connections with corpus-calibrated table sizes and asymmetric order allocation.
cdFj9zgZhp.problem: Over Encoding with sparse N-gram embedding tables lacks principled rules for sizing total table capacity and splitting parameter budgets across N-gram orders.
cdFj9zgZhp.method: StreamOE injects hashed N-gram embeddings directly into network Hyper-Connections via stream separation and calibrates table slot counts from corpus N-gram statistics on small proxy models. It allocates capacity asymmetrically across orders, using a 1:6.75 reference ratio between 2-gram and 3-gram tables.
cdFj9zgZhp.key_idea: Separate N-gram embedding streams inside Hyper-Connections while calibrating slot counts to dataset scale and allocating capacity asymmetrically toward higher-order N-grams.
cdFj9zgZhp.evidence: Evaluated via scaling and statistical corpus analyses and scaled to 80B-A3B and 309B-A15B Mixture-of-Experts language models on standard and long-context benchmarks.
cdFj9zgZhp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper provides practical empirical guidance on asymmetric bigram-trigram capacity allocation and validates StreamOE on large-scale MoE models up to 309B-A15B.
cdFj9zgZhp.main_concern: Capacity-transfer validation relies on fitted curves limited to 2-gram tables rather than direct training tests on 3-gram tables, and StreamOE's specific architectural gain over Vanilla OE is not cleanly isolated.

vNXfHVMpx5.one_liner: Propagates metric scale from sparse depth to frozen relative depth predictions using 3D geometric neighborhoods.
vNXfHVMpx5.problem: Fusing 2D sparse metric depth measurements with relative depth foundation models suffers from scale ambiguity because similar 2D sparse patterns can correspond to different 3D geometries.
vNXfHVMpx5.method: GeoSP selects valid sparse depth neighbors in 3D space using relative 3D geometry priors via Geometric Neighborhood Selection, then predicts propagation weights with a lightweight Geometric Affinity Prediction head while keeping the depth foundation model frozen.
vNXfHVMpx5.key_idea: Select sparse depth neighbors and predict scale-propagation affinities using relative 3D geometric relations rather than 2D image-plane proximity.
vNXfHVMpx5.evidence: Trained on NYUv2 and KITTI with a frozen Depth Anything V2 backbone and evaluated zero-shot across ten indoor and outdoor target datasets under simulated and raw sensor patterns.
vNXfHVMpx5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that selecting sparse neighbors via 3D geometric relations with a lightweight head over a frozen foundation model generalizes well across diverse indoor and outdoor datasets.
vNXfHVMpx5.main_concern: Core geometric alignment details and 3D distortion analyses are underspecified, alongside missing recent depth completion baselines and alternative foundation model backbones.

Uyb7QHMhwc.one_liner: Separates local query observations from shared-pool terminal rewards via Bayesian decision rules for active search.
Uyb7QHMhwc.problem: Standard active search treats queried labels directly as rewards, failing in scientific screening where a candidate's terminal value depends on comparisons across a shared pool.
Uyb7QHMhwc.method: The paper formalizes active search under pool-dependent utility, deriving a terminal-success Bayes score, an exact two-step lookahead decision value, and conditions bounding greedy loss. It aligns acquisition functions and scoring rules directly with complete-pool terminal events rather than history-visible subsets.
Uyb7QHMhwc.key_idea: Separate local query feedback from shared-pool terminal success events and select queries using Bayes scores aligned with complete-pool terminal utility.
Uyb7QHMhwc.evidence: Supported by theoretical bounds on two-step value and greedy loss, plus experiments on 230 MatPES PBE-to-r2SCAN materials systems and a group-held-out Airfoil Top-3 benchmark.
Uyb7QHMhwc.claimed_gains: On 230 MatPES PBE-to-r2SCAN systems, aligning the acquisition target with complete-pool terminal utility increases integrated confirmations by 6.617 relative to a history-visible hull objective.
Uyb7QHMhwc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the decision-theoretic separation of local query feedback from pool-dependent terminal utility is well motivated and evaluated with controlled factor ablations.
Uyb7QHMhwc.main_concern: Methodological novelty beyond standard Bayesian expected-utility maximization is limited, empirical validation is mostly confined to materials hull screening, and simple complete-pool baselines match the proposed rule.

HJt0wCff8Y.one_liner: Pretrains a frozen contextual Transformer on synthetic evolutionary circuit lineages to rank quantum architecture offspring.
HJt0wCff8Y.problem: Surrogate-assisted quantum architecture search typically requires expensive quantum circuit evaluations and inner-loop parameter optimizations just to collect training labels for the surrogate.
HJt0wCff8Y.method: GCQAS generates synthetic six-qubit evolutionary lineages with randomized per-family scoring rules and trains a contextual Transformer to infer local rankings from pooled circuit statistics, parent-child inheritance features, and ancestral outcomes. During target genetic search, the frozen Transformer conditions on a candidate's genealogy to screen offspring without retraining.
HJt0wCff8Y.key_idea: Pretrain a contextual Transformer on synthetic circuit lineages with randomized per-family scoring rules so it infers offspring rankings in-context from ancestral outcomes.
HJt0wCff8Y.evidence: Evaluated with a single six-qubit-pretrained frozen surrogate on distribution matching and variational quantum eigensolver tasks under noiseless and noisy simulation up to 16 qubits.
HJt0wCff8Y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that pretraining a single frozen surrogate on synthetic lineages without quantum circuit executions is practically appealing and transfers effectively across target tasks.
HJt0wCff8Y.main_concern: The paper lacks controlled ablations isolating genealogy and inheritance features from simpler parent-score predictors under the same architecture and synthetic prior.

UamHvU6F2T.one_liner: Patch-based graph representations and stochastic continuous-time attention enable robust irregular time-series forecasting.
UamHvU6F2T.problem: Changes in observation density and missingness cause distribution shifts in irregular multivariate time series, while continuous-time integration is costly.
UamHvU6F2T.method: RosFormer combines patch-based modeling with linear-noise stochastic differential equations and continuous-time attention. Relative-time-aware graphs capture inter-variable dependencies within patches while adapting discrete patch representations to continuous-time modeling.
UamHvU6F2T.key_idea: Relative-time patch graphs feed stochastic continuous-time attention to combine local computational efficiency with robustness to observation-process shifts.
UamHvU6F2T.evidence: Experiments cover forecasting, event prediction, controlled missingness, hospital-disjoint eICU-CRD evaluation, component ablations, and computational-efficiency analysis.
UamHvU6F2T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining patch efficiency with stochastic continuous-time attention is well motivated and produces competitive predictive and efficiency results.
UamHvU6F2T.main_concern: The evaluations do not fully isolate component contributions or attribute hospital-disjoint gains specifically to observation-shift robustness.

6y3lAOhLyA.one_liner: Sparse adaptive gradient anchors and local shape matching guide reference-based time-series resampling.
6y3lAOhLyA.problem: Trajectory-averaged gradients obscure heterogeneous local training signals, while computing every overlapping window gradient is expensive.
6y3lAOhLyA.method: RAGE places sparse gradient anchors using coverage and refinement guided by interpolation risk and direction cancellation. It encodes linear local gradient shapes with energy-normalized midpoint and slope components, scores source-reference similarities, and converts block-score ranks into sampling probabilities.
6y3lAOhLyA.key_idea: Sparse anchors define normalized local gradient midpoint-slope shapes whose signed reference similarities determine source-window resampling probabilities.
6y3lAOhLyA.evidence: Experiments evaluate Chronos-Base, TimesFM 2.5, and TimerXL on seven forecasting tasks with two seeds, selection baselines, matched training exposure, and component ablations.
6y3lAOhLyA.claimed_gains: Under a nominal 1.5% window-gradient budget, RAGE reduces MASE by 2.03% on average.
6y3lAOhLyA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that local gradient estimation addresses a meaningful allocation problem and that the mathematical development and cross-model experiments support shape matching.
6y3lAOhLyA.main_concern: Reviewers most often note that no uniform-anchor ablation at the same budget isolates the value of adaptive anchor placement.

txWaZwg63N.one_liner: Two-level normalization and fused lazy rescaling reduce exponentials in FP8 vision-transformer attention.
txWaZwg63N.problem: Softmax increasingly bottlenecks attention on modern GPUs, while existing substitutes often lose accuracy or practical speed.
txWaZwg63N.method: ERTL applies shifted-ReLU intra-block normalization with exponential normalization across blocks, then fuses it with lazy output rescaling in an FP8 kernel.
txWaZwg63N.key_idea: Replace within-block exponentials with shifted-ReLU weights while retaining exponential normalization across blocks for tiled execution.
txWaZwg63N.evidence: ViT experiments evaluate accuracy recovery after lightweight fine-tuning and standalone FP8 kernel speed against exact-softmax attention.
txWaZwg63N.claimed_gains: The kernel achieves up to a 1.55× speedup over BF16 exact-softmax attention and up to 245.5 TFLOPS higher throughput than FP8 exact-softmax attention.
txWaZwg63N.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the two-level approximation fits tiled computation and that kernel benchmarks plus post-adaptation accuracy provide useful evidence.
txWaZwg63N.main_concern: Reviewers most often question the missing end-to-end model timings and the mismatch between short vision workloads and long-sequence kernel gains.

yvBQTtObf0.one_liner: A learned text-embedding distribution supports reward alignment and trajectory-dependent test-time exploration for diffusion models.
yvBQTtObf0.problem: Deterministic text-encoder adaptation can over-optimize rewards and offers no mechanism for exploring alternative conditioning vectors.
yvBQTtObf0.method: PTERA learns a text-embedding distribution by direct reward backpropagation with a tractable KL-regularized objective around pretrained embeddings, while PTERA-TTA uses that distribution for trajectory-dependent test-time alignment.
yvBQTtObf0.key_idea: Learn a KL-regularized distribution over text embeddings instead of one deterministic conditioning vector.
yvBQTtObf0.evidence: Experiments and ablations on SD1.5 and SDXL, with additional SD3 and cross-backbone tests, assess reward alignment, training cost, and test-time alignment.
yvBQTtObf0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that probabilistic conditioning enables exploration while keeping the diffusion backbone frozen and training lightweight.
yvBQTtObf0.main_concern: Reviewers most often find the gain over deterministic or learned-isotropic controls small and inconsistent on stronger backbones.

VUQVPNyCrV.one_liner: An LLM audit, non-ML comparison arm, and sandboxed execution assess biomedical ML claims and code availability.
VUQVPNyCrV.problem: Manual domain-specific reviews cannot scale estimates of biomedical ML failure modes beyond a few hundred papers.
VUQVPNyCrV.method: The study applies a lightweight LLM pipeline and non-ML comparison arm to 27,200 OpenAlex biomedical papers, then follows code claims and executes available code in a sandbox.
VUQVPNyCrV.key_idea: Combine LLM-based literature classification with source-level code tracing and sandboxed execution to estimate failure rates at corpus scale.
VUQVPNyCrV.evidence: A blind, stratified 60-paper human validation set checks classification, while 27,200 papers including 12,037 ML papers support the audit.
VUQVPNyCrV.claimed_gains: Classification reaches 79.4% accuracy (95% CI 67.7–89.2), or 85.4% (74.8–94.3) after recoding reviews; 40.3% report inadequate metrics and 13.4% show illegitimate features.
VUQVPNyCrV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the unusually large audit, code-claim analysis, and multiple validation forms yield useful quantitative findings.
VUQVPNyCrV.main_concern: Reviewers most often cite limited human validation, including only 60 papers and a single annotator without human-human agreement.

XRrX1tAxQF.one_liner: DICE distribution correction enables mutual-information skill discovery from arbitrary off-policy experience.
XRrX1tAxQF.problem: Replay-policy distribution mismatch biases mutual-information estimates and existing skill discovery requires skill-conditioned replay data.
XRrX1tAxQF.method: MIM-DICE uses a DICE-based correction for off-policy mutual-information maximization, removing the need for skill-conditioned data and permitting arbitrary offline datasets.
XRrX1tAxQF.key_idea: Estimate current-policy skill-state mutual information through DICE corrections that remove replay-policy distribution mismatch.
XRrX1tAxQF.evidence: Online off-policy tests cover tabular environments and Pendulum, with six MAZE domains and offline and downstream evaluations also reported in reviews.
XRrX1tAxQF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the distribution-mismatch motivation is clear and that coherent DICE and MM derivations accompany varied experiments.
XRrX1tAxQF.main_concern: The central concern is insufficient validation of the DICE-based correction, including technical inconsistencies, missing comparisons, and simple environments.

vIrKUzlwpC.one_liner: Poisoned latent dynamics steer clean-trained actors and planners toward attacker-chosen actions when triggered.
vIrKUzlwpC.problem: Reused pretrained world-model checkpoints create a supply-chain risk for downstream controllers trained or instantiated with clean data.
vIrKUzlwpC.method: The attack routes trigger-bearing observations into a chosen latent region and reshapes local dynamics so Dreamer-style actor training or MPC/CEM planning rediscovers the target action.
vIrKUzlwpC.key_idea: Route triggered observations into a poisoned latent region whose altered dynamics make the victim's controller select the target action.
vIrKUzlwpC.evidence: Several control tasks and trigger families are evaluated with Dreamer-style actor training and MPC/CEM planning, alongside clean-utility and detector tests.
vIrKUzlwpC.claimed_gains: The strongest settings control every action dimension and reach up to 100% Step-ASR, while poisoned checkpoints retain roughly 74–100% of baseline clean utility.
vIrKUzlwpC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the checkpoint-only threat is meaningful and that actor and planning attacks reveal risks in reused world models.
vIrKUzlwpC.main_concern: Reviewers most often question practical applicability because attacks depend on the downstream controller, task knowledge, and trigger activation conditions.

yNFjboXkBw.one_liner: Channel-localizing itx gates faulty sensors before a dropout-trained predictor accommodates their removal.
yNFjboXkBw.problem: Virtual sensors degrade under physical-sensor faults, while anomaly detectors rarely identify which channel caused a failure.
yNFjboXkBw.method: The detect-isolate-accommodate pipeline uses itx, an iTransformer with untied per-channel embeddings and projections trained by cross-instance channel substitution, followed by a dropout-trained predictor.
yNFjboXkBw.key_idea: Train untied per-channel iTransformer components with cross-instance channel substitution, then discard localized faults before dropout-based prediction.
yNFjboXkBw.evidence: The benchmark spans six domains, nine datasets, and ten failure modes, comparing channel localization and downstream virtual-sensor robustness.
yNFjboXkBw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating isolation from dropout-based accommodation is well motivated and improves downstream prediction under faults.
yNFjboXkBw.main_concern: Reviewers most often cite incomplete ablations and baselines, leaving the contributions of substitution and channel-specific components unclear.

gsBps9kGp9.one_liner: Structural abstraction learns primitive symbols and compositional rules from noisy oracle-bone character demonstrations.
gsBps9kGp9.problem: Neural-symbolic learning usually assumes predefined primitive symbols and relations rather than discovering its interface from raw demonstrations.
gsBps9kGp9.method: Structural abstraction learns primitive symbols and their composition from sequences of raw perceptual observations without symbolic labels or predefined structures.
gsBps9kGp9.key_idea: Jointly induce primitive symbols and their compositional structure from sequences of raw perceptual observations.
gsBps9kGp9.evidence: Few-shot handwritten oracle-bone character experiments compare recovered expert-annotated radicals with feature-based motif-discovery baselines and test unseen ancient and modern characters.
gsBps9kGp9.claimed_gains: It recovers expert-annotated radical substructures with 72.28% macro-averaged recall, compared with 9.58–13.09% for feature-based motif-discovery baselines.
gsBps9kGp9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the problem is worthwhile, the algorithm is intuitive, and substructure recovery shows reasonable recall.
gsBps9kGp9.main_concern: Reviewers most often question restrictive structural assumptions and insufficiently specified optimization details.

KNzOCUZ8GF.one_liner: Predicts when an LLM agent should self-distill from latent reasoning trajectories by comparing finite-horizon update-versus-wait rollouts.
KNzOCUZ8GF.problem: Indiscriminately updating self-evolving agents wastes compute and causes interference, while delaying updates forces repeated reconstruction of reasoning patterns.
KNzOCUZ8GF.method: LATCH encodes latent reasoning trajectories, extracts deep-to-shallow corrections, assesses whether they are locally realizable by a shared parameter change across past queries, and trains a decision policy via paired update-wait rollouts to trigger on-policy self-distillation.
KNzOCUZ8GF.key_idea: Formulates agent self-evolution timing as an update-versus-wait decision supervised by paired rollouts using latent deep-to-shallow correction realizability signals.
KNzOCUZ8GF.evidence: Evaluated on long-horizon agent benchmarks comparing LATCH against Periodic, Random, and Early update-timing baselines.
KNzOCUZ8GF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that deciding *when* a self-evolving agent should update parameters via update-versus-wait rollouts is a practical, well-motivated formulation.
KNzOCUZ8GF.main_concern: Reviewers point out a missing ablation updating at every step with the same on-policy self-distillation, unverified causal links for the latent realizability diagnostics, and high framework complexity.

UNG18XT6lU.one_liner: Mitigates GNN over-squashing in social event detection by pairing semantically close and distant neighbors into joint units before propagation.
UNG18XT6lU.problem: Independent neighbor aggregation in GNNs fragments and dilutes complementary event cues across expanding receptive fields, causing a semantic bottleneck in social event detection.
UNG18XT6lU.method: JNSM selects candidate pairs from semantically close and distant neighbors, scores them for semantic complementarity, jointly encodes selected pairs into target-specific semantic units, and performs local rewiring prior to message passing.
UNG18XT6lU.key_idea: Pairs semantically close and distant neighbors into jointly encoded units before GNN message propagation to preserve complementary event cues.
UNG18XT6lU.evidence: Evaluated on three social event detection benchmarks (including Twitter2012) with component ablations and hyperparameter analyses.
UNG18XT6lU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that framing over-squashing through semantic complementarity is an intuitive angle and that JNSM is clearly structured with thorough ablations.
UNG18XT6lU.main_concern: Reviewers note small improvements (<1 percentage point, sometimes trailing GraphSAGE), limited novelty over existing rewiring/pairing methods, and omission of recent SED/LLM baselines in a dated closed-set setting.

Pcfiz1quEI.one_liner: Tests non-contrastive alignment objectives with a substitution cipher to expose orthographic shortcuts hidden by collapse diagnostics.
Pcfiz1quEI.problem: Label-free collapse diagnostics like effective rank and uniformity are used to validate and tune non-contrastive representations, but it is unclear whether they certify semantic content.
Pcfiz1quEI.method: The authors apply a bijective substitution cipher to one side of parallel cross-lingual text pairs—removing shared spelling while keeping translation links byte-identical—and compare retrieval retention across VICReg, SimSiam, contrastive, and frozen-teacher distillation objectives.
Pcfiz1quEI.key_idea: Uses a bijective substitution cipher on parallel text to separate semantic alignment from orthographic shortcuts under matched effective rank and uniformity.
Pcfiz1quEI.evidence: Evaluated cross-lingual retrieval and zero-shot NLI across VICReg, SimSiam, contrastive learning, and frozen-teacher alignment.
Pcfiz1quEI.claimed_gains: At effective-rank-selected weights, VICReg and SimSiam retain 0.16 and 0.29 of their retrieval score under the cipher versus 0.65 for contrastive learning.
Pcfiz1quEI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the substitution-cipher intervention cleanly exposes how collapse diagnostics can endorse orthographic shortcuts over semantics.
Pcfiz1quEI.main_concern: Generality beyond cross-lingual retrieval is limited (differences vanish in zero-shot NLI), and spectral claims about alignment and uniformity are imprecise.

k6BT3nnxkR.one_liner: Rotates RLVR weight updates within their low-dimensional subspace at fixed singular values to decouple accuracy from entropy collapse.
k6BT3nnxkR.problem: RLVR often improves reasoning accuracy while reducing predictive entropy, leaving unclear whether entropy collapse is required for accuracy gains.
k6BT3nnxkR.method: Using OLMo-3 and Tulu-3/Llama checkpoints, the authors apply spectrum-preserving random rotations to RLVR weight updates and search alternative perturbations around SFT weights across 30 strongly changed matrices.
k6BT3nnxkR.key_idea: Applies spectrum-preserving subspace rotations to RLVR weight updates to show predictive entropy collapse depends on update orientation independently of accuracy.
k6BT3nnxkR.evidence: Evaluated on OLMo-3 and Tulu-3/Llama checkpoints across truncation ranks and both fixed and model-generated text.
k6BT3nnxkR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that spectrum-preserving update rotations provide a clean controlled intervention to isolate weight-update orientation from magnitude.
k6BT3nnxkR.main_concern: The paper lacks comparisons against SFT or other post-training updates to show RLVR specificity, and the presentation shifts terminology.

x3Cf7xNaiQ.one_liner: Extends machine-learned force fields with flow maps that directly learn stochastic Langevin integration over large timesteps.
x3Cf7xNaiQ.problem: Molecular dynamics requires femtosecond timesteps to integrate Langevin equations, making long-timescale ensemble and transition-path sampling computationally expensive.
x3Cf7xNaiQ.method: Langevin Flow Maps (LFM) train neural networks to directly predict large-timestep stochastic Langevin updates from trajectory-free equilibrium samples via self-consistency losses.
x3Cf7xNaiQ.key_idea: Learns the stochastic Langevin integrator directly as a flow map to take large molecular dynamics timesteps without splitting bias.
x3Cf7xNaiQ.evidence: Evaluated on small molecules (ethanol, alanine dipeptide) and transferable peptide datasets against classical MD, machine-learned force fields, and Hamiltonian flow maps.
x3Cf7xNaiQ.claimed_gains: Runs an order of magnitude faster than current machine-learned force fields while recovering accurate dynamical properties.
x3Cf7xNaiQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learning the Langevin step directly is clean, achieves accurate small-molecule kinetics, and transfers to unseen peptides.
x3Cf7xNaiQ.main_concern: Training relies on equilibrium samples rather than unconverged data, and wall-clock speedups over classical MD vanish or reverse for larger peptides.

GmZCHjBICC.one_liner: Replaces prediction-error curiosity rewards with the normalized product of sample gradients and accumulated gradient momentum.
GmZCHjBICC.problem: Output-space prediction-error curiosity rewards attract RL agents to unpredictable aleatoric noise rather than genuine learning progress.
GmZCHjBICC.method: Gradient-Momentum Coupling (GMC) scores each sample by the normalized absolute product of its parameter gradient with the momentum of prior gradients, canceling random noise while rewarding persistent parameter updates.
GmZCHjBICC.key_idea: Uses the normalized product of current parameter gradients and historical gradient momentum as a parameter-space intrinsic reward for learning progress.
GmZCHjBICC.evidence: Evaluated on controlled multi-task noise prioritization experiments and four MiniGrid MultiRoom tasks by substituting GMC into ICM.
GmZCHjBICC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that GMC is simple, avoids an auxiliary progress predictor, and improves MiniGrid exploration under unpredictable observations.
GmZCHjBICC.main_concern: Experiments do not test settings where loss decouples from representation learning, and comparisons do not isolate momentum weighting from gradient-norm scaling.

t2TDoBGaSN.one_liner: Combines forward and time-reversed stationary transitions with weighted coordinates to learn Chung Laplacian eigenvectors in non-reversible chains.
t2TDoBGaSN.problem: Existing Laplacian representation learning methods use discounted forward transitions, which distort Chung Laplacian eigenvectors in non-reversible Markov chains.
t2TDoBGaSN.method: The method learns in stationary-distribution-weighted coordinates and applies a discounting scheme based on the reversible component of dynamics. It pairs forward and time-reversed transition sampling to form an unbiased energy estimator optimized via an augmented Lagrangian with local stability guarantees.
t2TDoBGaSN.key_idea: Pairing forward and time-reversed stationary transitions with reversible-component discounting yields an unbiased energy estimator for Chung Laplacian eigenvectors.
t2TDoBGaSN.evidence: Local stability theory under a simple-spectrum assumption and spectral recovery experiments on reversible and non-reversible environments across 30 seeds.
t2TDoBGaSN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the diagnosis of sampling-induced operator bias in non-reversible chains is mathematically sound and clearly analyzed.
t2TDoBGaSN.main_concern: Reviewers note missing downstream RL task evaluations, mismatched collection horizons in main comparisons, and deviations from stationarity in replay buffers.

CqxBL8BhfC.one_liner: Relaxes discrete defensive prompts to a continuous simplex and optimizes them via min-min adaptive adversarial training against jailbreaks.
CqxBL8BhfC.problem: Discrete prompt defenses against LLM jailbreaks are computationally expensive and remain vulnerable to adaptive attacks.
CqxBL8BhfC.method: Fast Soft Prompt Optimization (FSPO) relaxes a discrete defensive prefix onto a continuous probability simplex and optimizes it against both static and defense-aware adaptive attacks. The resulting soft prompt is deployed as a fixed continuous prefix prior to model release.
CqxBL8BhfC.key_idea: Min-min adversarial optimization over a continuous simplex-relaxed soft prompt yields a fast, deployable prefix robust to adaptive jailbreak attacks.
CqxBL8BhfC.evidence: Evaluations measure attack success rate (ASR), benign utility, and per-iteration runtime on Llama under static and adaptive GCG attacks, plus attention-shift analysis.
CqxBL8BhfC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the continuous relaxation formulation is lightweight, fast to optimize, and explicitly evaluates adaptive attackers.
CqxBL8BhfC.main_concern: Reviewers cite omitted recent soft-prompt defense baselines (DDPO, MCD), an unspecified target entropy projection, and small evaluation sets without seed variance.

wmW23DIxE0.one_liner: Connects discrete-time event counts to continuous-time Hawkes PGFLs to identify cyclic causal structures and self-loops.
wmW23DIxE0.problem: Discrete-time event sequences hide within-interval event ordering, and existing Structural Hawkes Processes require acyclic graphs.
wmW23DIxE0.method: Cyclic Structural Hawkes Processes (C-SHPs) link aggregated event counts to an underlying continuous-time Hawkes process via the probability generating functional (PGFL). The authors prove identifiability of self-loops, reciprocal edges, and directed cycles, and design a practical causal discovery algorithm over count data.
wmW23DIxE0.key_idea: Linking discrete-time event counts to continuous-time Hawkes probability generating functionals enables identification of self-loops and arbitrary directed cycles.
wmW23DIxE0.evidence: Identifiability proofs under exponential kernels and empirical comparisons on synthetic and real-world event-sequence datasets.
wmW23DIxE0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that extending discrete-time Structural Hawkes Processes to cyclic graphs via PGFL identifiability is an important and meaningful theoretical contribution.
wmW23DIxE0.main_concern: Reviewers point out a gap between population-level asymptotic identifiability theory and the finite-sample heuristic algorithm, plus missing direct evaluation of self-loop recovery.

nTTEBJmuKN.one_liner: Audits whether held-out text loss orders context-selection rules consistently with downstream task benchmarks.
nTTEBJmuKN.problem: Context-selection rules for token dropping are often ranked by held-out loss on ordinary text, assuming that ordering transfers to downstream tasks.
nTTEBJmuKN.method: The authors evaluate 21 context-selection rules keeping half of <=128-token contexts across six frozen decoders, comparing rule rankings on three text corpora (encyclopedia, books, web) against accuracy on four downstream benchmarks.
nTTEBJmuKN.key_idea: Measures rank correlation and selection-regret reversals between held-out corpus loss and downstream task accuracy across 21 controlled token-dropping rules.
nTTEBJmuKN.evidence: Empirical audit across 21 rules, six frozen decoder models, three corpora, and four downstream benchmarks.
nTTEBJmuKN.claimed_gains: Rulers have mean self-reliability above 0.95, but corpus-benchmark rank correlation averages only +0.44 (versus +0.83 between corpora and +0.64 between benchmarks), with benchmarks reversing 15-44% of confident corpus orderings.
nTTEBJmuKN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that auditing held-out loss as a proxy for context-selection benchmarks addresses a relevant methodological question with thorough robustness checks.
nTTEBJmuKN.main_concern: Reviewers find the writing convoluted and hard to follow, and note that 128-token contexts within 256-token windows limit relevance to practical long-context compression.

GbzrTE2vvK.one_liner: Attacks time-series classifiers via Gumbel top-k adversarial missingness masks and defends with gated mask-aware imputation consistency training.
GbzrTE2vvK.problem: Time-series classifiers that tolerate random missingness fail when class-discriminative observations are selectively missing under the same missingness budget.
GbzrTE2vvK.method: AdvMissing-TSC uses TG-SMA—combining Gumbel relaxation, top-k projection, and temporal contiguity regularization—to optimize worst-case missingness masks under mean or zero imputation. To defend, MID fuses numerical and missingness features via learned gating and penalizes prediction discrepancies against complete inputs scaled by missing rate.
GbzrTE2vvK.key_idea: Optimizes exact-budget contiguous missingness masks via Gumbel top-k projection and defends with gated missingness-feature fusion and rate-weighted consistency regularization.
GbzrTE2vvK.evidence: Evaluated across multiple time-series classification datasets, imputation methods, missingness patterns, and classifiers.
