GbzrTE2vvK.claimed_gains: Adversarial missingness yields lower accuracy than matched random missingness across all evaluated classifiers.
GbzrTE2vvK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree shifting robustness evaluation from value perturbations to exact-budget observation availability is realistic and well-motivated.
GbzrTE2vvK.main_concern: Reviewers criticize testing MID only against non-adaptive transfer masks rather than white-box adaptive attacks, missing view-matched baselines, and unclear novelty over prior masking work.

pUfnKUhQYN.one_liner: Benchmarks 20 text steganography schemes via supervised fine-tuning of language models to measure trainability and bit error rates.
pUfnKUhQYN.problem: Text steganography could let language models hide messages in ordinary outputs, undermining safety monitoring, yet scheme trainability is poorly understood.
pUfnKUhQYN.method: StegoBench unifies 20 lexical, syntactic, structural, and distributional text steganography schemes under a common encoding, decoding, and SFT/ICL/ICRL evaluation framework.
pUfnKUhQYN.key_idea: Evaluates whether language models can learn to execute classical and distributional steganographic encoding schemes via supervised fine-tuning.
pUfnKUhQYN.evidence: Full fine-tuning runs across multiple language model scales on StegoBench measuring hidden bit error rate (BER) and collapse modes.
pUfnKUhQYN.claimed_gains: The Chang & Clark lexical scheme reaches a hidden bit error rate (BER) as low as 0.012, and the single-bit Shirali spelling channel reaches 0.021–0.034.
pUfnKUhQYN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate bringing 18–20 steganography schemes into a unified benchmark for trainability and failure-mode analysis.
pUfnKUhQYN.main_concern: Reviewers note that included schemes mostly predate 2024, training sizes and payloads vary across schemes, and forcing distributional schemes through offline GPT-2-XL SFT causes checkpoint mismatch.

NSVBP4WjEL.one_liner: Benchmarks coding agents on 1,000 repository-level frontend edits driven by annotated rendered screenshots.
NSVBP4WjEL.problem: Existing code benchmarks do not test whether agents can infer visual intent from annotated screenshots and edit multi-file frontend repositories.
NSVBP4WjEL.method: ViRE-Bench collects 1,000 tasks across 202 HTML, React, Vue, and Angular repositories spanning eight edit operations, evaluating submission validity, intent satisfaction, target fidelity, and preservation.
NSVBP4WjEL.key_idea: Pair real multi-file frontend repositories with programmatically annotated screenshots to evaluate visual intent inference and cross-page code editing.
NSVBP4WjEL.evidence: Single-turn evaluations test six models on ViRE-Bench, alongside controlled diagnostics providing explicit editing intent or source locations.
NSVBP4WjEL.claimed_gains: Among six models evaluated under a common single-turn protocol, the best-performing model achieves an overall benchmark score of 67.29 and an intent satisfaction rate of 70.2%, while two models reach approximately 95% intent satisfaction under explicit intent.
NSVBP4WjEL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that repository-level frontend editing from annotated screenshots is a practical, underexplored benchmark setting.
NSVBP4WjEL.main_concern: Reviewers note that tasks and annotations are synthetically generated (with Gemini-3.7-Flash involved in construction and also scoring highest) rather than collected from real human users.

9bHeCnjXo9.one_liner: Guarantees exact LLM vocabulary decoding from host memory using on-accelerator grouped integer bounds and sparse row retrieval.
9bHeCnjXo9.problem: Offloading large LLM output heads to host memory requires fetching the full vocabulary matrix at each decoding step.
9bHeCnjXo9.method: The decoder stores grouped integer representations and residual error bounds on the accelerator while keeping BF16 rows in host memory, using outward-rounded intervals and tie-aware screening to fetch only candidate winning rows.
9bHeCnjXo9.key_idea: Keep grouped integer approximations and Cauchy-Schwarz residual error bounds on-device to screen out provably non-winning vocabulary rows stored in host memory.
9bHeCnjXo9.evidence: Tests across four primary models, six-model path checks (10,240 decisions), and 32B native-kernel benchmarks evaluate exactness, sparsity, and latency.
9bHeCnjXo9.claimed_gains: With groups of 512 coordinates, the resident representation occupies 51.2% of a dense BF16 output head, evaluates only 0.005% to 2.190% of rows on average with no mismatch in 10,240 decisions, costs under 1% more than a resident stock head on a 32B model, and decodes 1.67 to 1.92 times faster than streaming.
9bHeCnjXo9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the provably exact finite-precision path identity and extreme row-retrieval sparsity.
9bHeCnjXo9.main_concern: Reviewers question practical utility because FP64 screening overhead makes it 1.44x–2.71x slower than stock on-device BF16 execution and yields minimal end-to-end batch capacity gains.

rUvkw2SVCR.one_liner: Reuses conditional endpoint samples across shared-condition diffusion trajectories via importance reweighting for inference-time reward alignment.
rUvkw2SVCR.problem: Gradient-free inference-time reward alignment for diffusion models incurs high compute by sampling conditional endpoints independently for each trajectory.
rUvkw2SVCR.method: The authors introduce batch-coupled tilted denoising, which applies cross-trajectory importance reweighting so conditional endpoint samples generated for one trajectory contribute to reward-tilted updates of other trajectories in the batch.
rUvkw2SVCR.key_idea: Share conditional endpoint samples across a batch of same-prompt diffusion trajectories using cross-trajectory importance reweighting.
rUvkw2SVCR.evidence: Evaluations across multiple generative backbones and reward objectives compare the reward-compute frontier against uncoupled baselines.
rUvkw2SVCR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the batch-sharing idea simple, well-motivated, and effective for reducing per-sample NFE in low-compute regimes.
rUvkw2SVCR.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about reduced within-batch sample diversity as coupling increases, reliance on large shared-prompt batches, and an unjustified Gaussian endpoint approximation.

7hncu1uD29.one_liner: Synthesizes executable terminal-agent tasks at scale using corpus-anchored sampling, shared contracts, and failure-directed repair.
7hncu1uD29.problem: Training open-weight terminal agents is bottlenecked by the scarcity of diverse, runnable environments paired with consistent verifiers.
7hncu1uD29.method: OpenTerminal samples 307,293 problem patterns via cluster-smoothed sampling, generates environments and verifiers from a shared hidden task contract, and repairs failures via Diagnose-Route-Repair.
7hncu1uD29.key_idea: Use a shared hidden task contract and dependency-routed failure repair to synthesize consistent terminal environments and verifiers from public corpora.
7hncu1uD29.evidence: The pipeline produces 11,713 tasks and 7,365 trajectories used to fine-tune Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3.5-9B on terminal benchmarks.
7hncu1uD29.claimed_gains: Fine-tuning Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3.5-9B on the 7,365 generated trajectories improves pass@1 over the base models by 56.8% and 63.1%.
7hncu1uD29.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the practical scale (>11k tasks) and disciplined engineering of the shared-contract and repair pipeline.
7hncu1uD29.main_concern: Reviewers note that build and no-op checks do not verify task solvability or verifier correctness, and that ablations do not measure downstream agent performance.

kLgaq3RjW2.one_liner: Learns a prompt-conditioned selector choosing per-layer KV-cache depth sharing, precision, and rank compression.
kLgaq3RjW2.problem: Token-eviction KV-cache compression risks discarding content needed later, while applying uniform non-eviction interventions across all layers degrades accuracy.
kLgaq3RjW2.method: KV-Kaizen trains a lightweight selector on prompt embeddings before prefill to assign per-layer KV-cache configurations under an overall bits-per-token budget. The selector composes cross-layer cache sharing, lower-bit quantization, and latent rank truncation.
kLgaq3RjW2.key_idea: A lightweight prefill selector composes cross-layer cache sharing, precision quantization, and latent rank truncation per layer to meet a global memory budget.
kLgaq3RjW2.evidence: Evaluated across multiple model sizes (including 7B) and families, with ablations over the three compression axes and comparisons to KIVI quantization and fine-tuned controls.
kLgaq3RjW2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that unifying precision, rank, and cross-layer sharing under a common bits-per-token budget with extensive ablations is practical and informative.
kLgaq3RjW2.main_concern: Reviewers question whether context-dependent selection is truly needed, noting some selectors return identical configurations across prompts and show unclear gains over 4x fixed-bit quantization.

PaHGqNaJqq.one_liner: Benchmarks LLM insurance claim adjudication across atomic rules, modules, payout decisions, and amounts with counterfactual variants.
PaHGqNaJqq.problem: Evaluating LLMs only on final claim decisions masks intermediate rule failures, amount-calculation errors, and inconsistency under factual edits.
PaHGqNaJqq.method: InsClaimBench provides 3,780 synthetic/expert-grounded cases across auto, property, and health insurance with 86,656 atomic rule judgments and controlled factual variants, evaluating six LLMs at atomic-rule, module, payout-decision, and payout-amount levels.
PaHGqNaJqq.key_idea: Decomposes insurance claim adjudication into atomic rules, intermediate modules, payout decisions, and amounts with paired counterfactual case variants to audit consistency.
PaHGqNaJqq.evidence: Evaluated across six LLMs on 3,780 cases (375 case families, 86,656 atomic rule judgments) with independent expert validation.
PaHGqNaJqq.claimed_gains: Payout-decision accuracy ranges from 74.23–80.19% while joint decision-amount accuracy drops to 47.54–73.15%; atomic-rule accuracy reaches 95.48% whereas rule-vector exact match peaks at 36.90%.
PaHGqNaJqq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the multi-level decomposition and counterfactual case-family design for exposing gaps between local rule accuracy and joint payout correctness.
PaHGqNaJqq.main_concern: Reviewers point out that levels are queried independently without passing upstream predictions downstream—measuring cross-query inconsistency rather than true sequential error propagation.

cUGfSvgV1y.one_liner: Pretrains a single neural network with a spectral objective to generate reusable coarse spaces for PDE solvers.
cUGfSvgV1y.problem: Classical PDE solvers lack cross-problem generalization while neural operators lack accuracy guarantees, and existing neural preconditioners require per-problem training.
cUGfSvgV1y.method: Alioth is pretrained once on synthetic diffusion problems with a label-free spectral objective to predict coarse-space basis vectors capturing slow-to-converge error modes. It plugs zero-shot into domain decomposition and algebraic multigrid iterative solvers.
cUGfSvgV1y.key_idea: Pretrains a single spectral-objective network to generate transferable coarse-space vectors for iterative domain-decomposition and multigrid solvers without per-PDE retraining.
cUGfSvgV1y.evidence: Evaluated zero-shot on 13 scalar SPD PDE systems spanning five engineering domains, plus algebraic multigrid tests and subspace-iteration ablations.
cUGfSvgV1y.claimed_gains: Needs 48% fewer iterations than the classical Nicolaides coarse space across 13 scalar SPD systems.
cUGfSvgV1y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find learning a reusable, error-tolerant solver component (coarse spaces) rather than a one-shot solution map to be a compelling and well-tested concept.
cUGfSvgV1y.main_concern: Reviewers note that end-to-end wall-clock runtime is 16–33x slower than hypre BoomerAMG (17.3–154.4 s vs. 1.0–4.7 s), negating the iteration-count reduction in practice.

E7p3biFfeR.one_liner: Reciprocally aligns clinical findings and sentence contexts through shared visual evidence with masked report and summary objectives.
E7p3biFfeR.problem: Medical vision-language pre-training methods model focal clinical findings and their surrounding report sentences independently rather than coordinating their complementary semantics.
E7p3biFfeR.method: FRAME reciprocally aligns finding-conditioned visual representations with sentence contexts and context-conditioned visual representations with clinical findings. It adds two proxy tasks: masked report reconstruction for dense diagnostic retention and evidence-focused summary prediction for salient semantics.
E7p3biFfeR.key_idea: Couples bidirectional finding-to-sentence and context-to-finding visual alignment with masked report reconstruction and evidence-focused summary prediction.
E7p3biFfeR.evidence: Evaluated across classification, segmentation, detection, VQA, and report generation under limited-label and cross-dataset settings, plus component ablations.
E7p3biFfeR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the finding-context motivation is clear and the evaluation across five downstream task families and ablations is comprehensive.
E7p3biFfeR.main_concern: Reviewers question whether reciprocal alignment genuinely improves local lesion-level grounding and note noisy broad finding tokens and GPT-4o summary omissions.

BoNED9kGUf.one_liner: Uses world-model risk prediction in a risk-to-decision loop to guardrail computer-using agents against short- and long-term risks.
BoNED9kGUf.problem: Reactive guardrails for computer-using agents only inspect the current observation and fail to prevent delayed, long-term risks.
BoNED9kGUf.method: SafePred uses safety policies and a world model to predict semantic representations of short- and long-term risks, pruning high-risk actions. It feeds predicted consequences into step-level corrective guidance and task-level replanning.
BoNED9kGUf.key_idea: Pairs policy-grounded world-model risk forecasting with step-level corrective guidance and replanning to prune actions leading to delayed high-risk states.
BoNED9kGUf.evidence: Evaluated across WASP, OS-Harm, and SafePred-Bench against reactive and prompt-based guardrails including HarmonyGuard and GuardAgent.
BoNED9kGUf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree SafePred addresses delayed risks in computer-using agents and improves the safety-utility tradeoff across benchmarks.
BoNED9kGUf.main_concern: Multiple reviewers note insufficient isolation of explicit prediction's contribution, questionable long-term risk definitions, and inconsistencies in reported tables.

6B0DEmq5ra.one_liner: Establishes identifiability of persistent environments and recurrent states in nonstationary time series and implements it in HiDICE.
6B0DEmq5ra.problem: Flat switching state-space models conflate persistent sequence-level environments with recurrent within-sequence mechanism states in unlabeled nonstationary time series.
6B0DEmq5ra.method: Proves identifiability of environment partitions, state cardinalities, and cross-environment state correspondence using translated invariant transition signatures, and builds HiDICE, a hierarchical variational state-space model with additive signature sharing.
6B0DEmq5ra.key_idea: Uses translated invariant transition signatures to align recurrent mechanism states across persistent environments in a hierarchical variational state-space model.
6B0DEmq5ra.evidence: Theoretical identifiability proofs and controlled synthetic experiments evaluating hierarchy and latent-factor recovery.
6B0DEmq5ra.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the theoretical distinction between within-sequence switching recovery and cross-environment state alignment.
6B0DEmq5ra.main_concern: Reviewers question the realism of the additive transition-signature assumption (Assumption 1) and note that parts of the theory rely heavily on existing nonlinear ICA results.

Wm5WzXBNta.one_liner: Applies multi-head attention over an agent-action graph to coordinate multi-agent policies without enumerating joint actions.
Wm5WzXBNta.problem: Standard MARL methods suffer from either miscoordination or exponential costs when explicitly modeling joint-action dependencies across agents.
Wm5WzXBNta.method: Action Graph Policies (AGP) construct a graph whose nodes are available agent-action pairs and apply multi-head attention across it to exchange information. This contextualizes each candidate action with respect to teammates' available choices before action selection.
Wm5WzXBNta.key_idea: Treats candidate agent-action pairs as graph nodes and runs multi-head attention over them to capture inter-agent action dependencies.
Wm5WzXBNta.evidence: Provides theoretical analysis of miscoordination and joint-action costs, and empirical comparisons against 14 MARL baselines across 19 cooperative tasks.
Wm5WzXBNta.claimed_gains: Achieves higher aggregate performance than 14 related MARL methods across 19 cooperative tasks.
Wm5WzXBNta.reviewer_consensus: Two reviewers note that using an agent-action graph to model action co-dependence is a well-motivated direction with strong empirical results and ablations, while one reviewer listed no strengths.
Wm5WzXBNta.main_concern: Reviewers question the fairness of all-to-all synchronous communication assumptions, the lack of wall-clock/latency/memory measurements, and the justification for across-agent edge definitions.

GzyTeka0rX.one_liner: Audits promptable segmentation unlearning across alternative prompt/output routes and target-clean fine-tuning updates.
GzyTeka0rX.problem: Static selectivity checks at a single canonical inference configuration fail to reveal whether unlearned segmentation targets remain recoverable.
GzyTeka0rX.method: Across a 336-run State Bank on two SAM backbones, the authors evaluate 28 qualified unlearned states under alternative task-native access routes (multimask, output-resolution rules) and five target-clean adaptation updates.
GzyTeka0rX.key_idea: Tests qualified unlearned segmentation checkpoints under non-canonical prompt/output routes and target-clean adaptation steps to expose residual target capability.
GzyTeka0rX.evidence: Controlled experiments across 336 candidate runs and 28 qualified states on SAM and SAM2 backbones.
GzyTeka0rX.claimed_gains: Mean route-normalized residual target capability rises from 0.548 under canonical box access to 0.944 under model-ranked multimask output, and five target-clean updates restore 77.2% of the gap.
GzyTeka0rX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that testing unlearned segmentation models beyond canonical inference routes exposes an important evaluation blind spot.
GzyTeka0rX.main_concern: Reviewers note that 27 of 28 qualified states come from a single method (SCU), no mitigation is proposed, and non-standard terminology hinders readability.

H7gWOcdqWj.one_liner: Triggers label-free early stopping when a budget-rescaled smoothed Fisher-curvature stability ratio crosses a threshold.
H7gWOcdqWj.problem: Early stopping without a clean validation set is unreliable using loss or gradient norms, which keep changing after generalization peaks.
H7gWOcdqWj.method: Curvature Floor Stopping (CFS) monitors the effective learning rate relative to the gradient-descent stability threshold via the top Fisher eigenvalue (estimated with model-sampled labels) and smooths it with a budget-rescaled kernel.
H7gWOcdqWj.key_idea: Monitors the effective learning rate normalized by the top Fisher eigenvalue using a budget-rescaled smoothing kernel for label-free early stopping.
H7gWOcdqWj.evidence: Theoretical scale-invariance proof and experiments across seven regimes (including ResNet-50 on ImageNet, MAE pretraining, BERT fine-tuning, and 40% label noise) with five seeds.
H7gWOcdqWj.claimed_gains: CFS adds ~5% memory on models up to 340M parameters and matches or beats validation-based early stopping in five of seven settings.
H7gWOcdqWj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the principled derivation of budget-rescaled smoothing and the breadth of architectures and regimes tested.
H7gWOcdqWj.main_concern: Reviewers criticize dense, hard-to-read writing with undefined terms, missing comparisons to other label-free stopping baselines, and per-task tuning of 35–48 parameter combinations.

xwnYE6MomD.one_liner: Learns task-specific Bregman divergences via bi-level optimization for concept erasure in flow-matching text-to-image models.
xwnYE6MomD.problem: Flow-matching concept erasure methods use fixed Euclidean velocity-matching losses, which poorly balance removing target concepts against preserving unrelated generations.
xwnYE6MomD.method: BEM notes that all Bregman divergences are valid flow-matching losses and uses bi-level optimization to learn a parameterized potential function defining the Bregman divergence so that fine-tuning erases target concepts on unseen prompts while retaining benign generation.
xwnYE6MomD.key_idea: Replaces fixed Euclidean velocity-matching loss with a Bregman divergence learned via bi-level optimization to balance concept erasure and retention.
xwnYE6MomD.evidence: Evaluated on nudity, bloody gore, real identities, and copyrighted characters under GEM's protocol on FLUX/SD3.5.
xwnYE6MomD.claimed_gains: Cuts bloody-gore unsafe rate from 53.9% to 14.4% and nudity FID from 8.64 to 6.64 versus GEM, though retention degrades on some concepts (e.g., Einstein 72.7% vs. 93.3%).
xwnYE6MomD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree learning the Bregman divergence for flow-matching erasure is theoretically grounded and cleanly controlled against GEM.
xwnYE6MomD.main_concern: Reviewers highlight severe computational cost (~50x slower than GEM, up to 438 min), inconsistent concept retention, and missing ablations on the potential network and bi-level components.

562QHhdCeL.one_liner: Learns preference-drift-robust Pareto policy sets via drift-aware trust regions, hierarchical perturbations, and contrastive alignment.
562QHhdCeL.problem: Observation and dynamics uncertainty in multi-objective RL causes preference drift, misaligning requested preferences from realized trade-offs.
562QHhdCeL.method: DROPS constructs a drift-aware trust region per preference, applies hierarchical adversarial perturbations to bound degradation, and uses contrastive drift alignment over trajectory embeddings to preserve preference-to-policy correspondence across the Pareto set.
562QHhdCeL.key_idea: Combines drift-aware trust regions, hierarchical adversarial perturbations, and contrastive trajectory-embedding alignment to preserve preference-to-policy mapping under uncertainty.
562QHhdCeL.evidence: Evaluated on five continuous robotic-control tasks and one discrete benchmark with component ablations.
562QHhdCeL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree identifying preference drift (misalignment of preference-to-outcome correspondence) is a meaningful MORL problem with rich empirical results.
562QHhdCeL.main_concern: Reviewers question the rationale for contrastive pairing via policy KL divergence, note missing theoretical guarantees, and criticize modeling partial observability with stationary MDP policies.

SRgVeYveTJ.one_liner: Preconditions deep predictive coding activity inference with a batch-shared Gauss-Newton recurrence and cached output-space correction.
SRgVeYveTJ.problem: Inner activity inference in deep predictive coding networks suffers from chain-wide low-curvature modes, requiring gradient budgets that grow with depth.
SRgVeYveTJ.method: Cached Boundary Transport (CBT) linearizes predictions at the feedforward state to form a batch-shared Gauss-Newton preconditioner inverted via one backward and one forward layer recurrence plus a cached output-space correction, followed by short gradient-descent refinement and an energy-checked fallback.
SRgVeYveTJ.key_idea: Inverts a linearized batch-shared Gauss-Newton preconditioner via single-pass backward/forward layer recurrences to resolve chain-wide modes in constant depth cost.
SRgVeYveTJ.evidence: Evaluated on residual predictive coding networks from 16 to 256 layers on MNIST and CIFAR-10.
SRgVeYveTJ.claimed_gains: Keeps inference cost nearly constant in gradient evaluations from 16 to 256 layers while a 28-fold larger first-order budget leaves 256-layer test accuracy unchanged.
SRgVeYveTJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree diagnosing chain-wide low-curvature modes and applying curvature preconditioning to accelerate deep PC inference is an interesting direction.
SRgVeYveTJ.main_concern: Reviewers note small-scale benchmarks (MNIST, 40.75% CIFAR-10) where deeper networks underperform shallower ones, missing component ablations, and dense exposition.

qLwm8hAflc.one_liner: Aligns event features to RGB semantics before RGB-dominant asymmetric fusion with a spatial retrieval prior for object detection.
qLwm8hAflc.problem: Differences in density, semantics, and reliability between RGB and Event streams cause modality bias during RGB-Event object detection fusion.
qLwm8hAflc.method: SACFusion operates in two stages: Stage I aggregates temporal/polarity event structures and adapts event features to the pretrained RGB semantic space via local alignment and semantic preservation; Stage II performs RGB-dominant asymmetric fusion weighted by a spatially varying Event Retrieval Prior.
qLwm8hAflc.key_idea: Separates event-to-RGB semantic alignment (Stage I) from RGB-queried asymmetric fusion weighted by a learned Event Retrieval Prior (Stage II).
qLwm8hAflc.evidence: Evaluated on DSEC-Det and PEOD autonomous driving benchmarks with ablations.
qLwm8hAflc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree decomposing compatibility before complementarity and using RGB-dominant asymmetric retrieval are plausible and yield strong DSEC-Det/PEOD gains.
qLwm8hAflc.main_concern: Reviewers point out that ablations bundle SLSA and CP together, lack a budget-matched one-stage baseline for the extra 30k Stage I iterations, and lack direct validation of the retrieval prior.

2AdSgH2P7a.one_liner: Plans budgeted evidence validation and repair over versioned dependency DAGs for reusable scientific agent workflows.
2AdSgH2P7a.problem: Scientific agents must re-validate or repair claim-supporting evidence within a compute budget when assumptions, measurements, or protocols change.
2AdSgH2P7a.method: CBR-VERIFY models claim revision as budgeted claim completion over version-bound obligations and executable predicates, using bounded seed enumeration and closure selection ranked by covering density to jointly allocate compute across shared-cost archive validation and conditional repair.
2AdSgH2P7a.key_idea: Formulates scientific claim revision as budgeted closure selection over versioned dependency DAGs, ranking shared-cost validation and repair actions by covering density.
2AdSgH2P7a.evidence: Evaluated across 12 paired GPT tasks, frozen-task replications, structural sharing sweeps, and real simulation-adapter executions.
2AdSgH2P7a.claimed_gains: Improves observed utility by 9.52 percentage points over Plan-Verify (7.85% fewer tokens, 12.13% more credits), gains 15.48 points over greedy while saving 4.35 credits/task, and saves ~17% simulation-tool cost.
2AdSgH2P7a.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree budgeted scheduling over shared-cost evidence dependencies addresses a practical maintenance problem in scientific workflows.
2AdSgH2P7a.main_concern: Reviewers note pair expansion adds only 0.40 points over singleton selection, the system relies on manually pre-authored static DAGs/predicates, and task scale (5 claims) is small.

jK6q6YzNIg.one_liner: Bridges a large video backbone to a lightweight action DiT via a spatio-temporal object-and-detail compression interface.
jK6q6YzNIg.problem: Implicit world-action models expose deep high-dimensional video features directly to the action expert, inflating action-denoising compute.
jK6q6YzNIg.method: STaC-WAM decouples a large predictive video backbone from a lightweight 6-layer Action DiT using a Spatio-Temporal Action-Conditioning (STaC) bridge that compresses multi-layer video representations into compact object-centric and fine-detail conditioning features.
jK6q6YzNIg.key_idea: Compresses multi-layer predictive video features into compact object-centric and detail conditioning tokens via a STaC bridge for a lightweight action DiT.
jK6q6YzNIg.evidence: Evaluated on LIBERO, RoboTwin, and five real-robot tasks with latency measurements and component ablations.
jK6q6YzNIg.claimed_gains: Reduces inference latency from 192.83 ms to 91.68 ms (~2.1x speedup) while improving LIBERO success from 97.60% to 98.85%.
jK6q6YzNIg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree decoupling video and action capacities achieves a strong latency-success trade-off across simulation and real-robot benchmarks.
jK6q6YzNIg.main_concern: Reviewers point out missing matched-supervision MLP compression controls (MLP + TSA) to isolate Slot Attention's benefit and missing comparisons to Faster-WAM/Light-WAM.

HiXe1jYbU2.one_liner: Shows arithmetic transformers learn most-significant digits first via magnitude estimation and uses curriculum learning to shift them to digit-wise computation.
HiXe1jYbU2.problem: It is unclear whether transformers solve symbolic arithmetic via digit-wise algorithms or statistical shortcuts, and how training structure shapes their internal strategy.
HiXe1jYbU2.method: The authors analyze how an encoder transformer learns addition and solve the exact learning dynamics of a linear model on the same task to show why a continuous magnitude representation is acquired first. They then apply curriculum learning to force canonical least-to-most-significant digit acquisition and inspect resulting strategies via attention patterns, activation patching, and carry-chain tests.
HiXe1jYbU2.key_idea: Uses an analytically solved linear model to explain most-significant-digit-first magnitude estimation and applies a canonical-order curriculum to induce digit-wise computation in transformers.
HiXe1jYbU2.evidence: Combines exact linear-model learning-dynamics theory with encoder transformer addition experiments, activation patching, carry-chain tests, and generalization to structurally similar tasks.
HiXe1jYbU2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the combination of analytically tractable theory with mechanistic curriculum-intervention experiments.
HiXe1jYbU2.main_concern: Reviewers question the broader significance beyond toy arithmetic and note a gap between the linear model's magnitude representation and the transformer's actual learned mechanism, alongside dense presentation.

Bxo1CinK6t.one_liner: Regularizes individualized rs-fMRI brain effective connectivity using a subject-specific neighbor reference graph and quality-control-aware edge refinement.
Bxo1CinK6t.problem: Individualized brain effective connectivity estimation from short, noisy rs-fMRI data is unstable, while global population priors erase pairwise inter-subject differences.
Bxo1CinK6t.method: PR-EC builds a multimodal inter-subject similarity graph to aggregate effective connectivity estimates from each target subject's most relevant training neighbors into a personalized population reference. A quality-control-aware refinement module then adaptively modulates how strongly the population reference regularizes each edge.
Bxo1CinK6t.key_idea: Aggregates neighbor effective connectivity via a multimodal inter-subject similarity graph and modulates edge-wise regularization using quality-control-aware refinement.
Bxo1CinK6t.evidence: Includes theoretical bias-variance tradeoff analysis and disease classification plus cross-cohort reproducibility experiments on three rs-fMRI datasets (including ABIDE-I and ABIDE-II).
Bxo1CinK6t.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that balancing individualized estimation with neighbor-specific population guidance in a leakage-aware design is well motivated.
Bxo1CinK6t.main_concern: Reviewers highlight that effective connectivity is never validated against ground-truth directed networks (only classification is tested) and that classification gains are marginal, single-seed, and lack significance tests.

1zF9zPNiru.one_liner: Separates forward financial model selection from superiority claims using Prediction-Portfolio-Deployability evaluation and paired simultaneous inference.
1zF9zPNiru.problem: Financial forecasting benchmarks rely on isolated metric wins that ignore portfolio construction, deployment conditions, and multiple-comparison uncertainty.
1zF9zPNiru.method: PPD-SOTA decouples forward model selection from superiority testing by evaluating models through Prediction, Portfolio, and Deployability criteria over rolling windows with trading costs. To test superiority claims across a comparator set, it applies practical margins and paired simultaneous statistical inference.
1zF9zPNiru.key_idea: Decouples forward deployment selection across Prediction, Portfolio, and Deployability criteria from comparator-set superiority claims verified via paired simultaneous inference with practical margins.
1zF9zPNiru.evidence: Evaluated on a unified benchmark of seven recent stock-forecasting models under varying deployment conditions, alongside ablations and a theoretical proposition.
1zF9zPNiru.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating forward deployment selection from superiority claims and incorporating trading execution conditions addresses a realistic evaluation gap.
1zF9zPNiru.main_concern: Reviewers note that the simultaneous-interval statistical construction is underspecified, simplified ablations perform similarly to full PPD, and deployment modeling lacks a practitioner case study.

zqJkXM0xmu.one_liner: Mitigates grounding drift in multimodal deep research agents using trajectory SFT and source-linked rubric-guided GRPO.
zqJkXM0xmu.problem: Long-horizon multimodal deep research agents suffer from Grounding Drift, where previously acquired visual observations, claim-source bindings, or constraints are omitted or corrupted during synthesis.
zqJkXM0xmu.method: Cog-Research constructs a 500-task Plan-and-Act dataset with source-linked, task-specific rubrics derived from research traces, workspace artifacts, and human reports. It post-trains Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct via trajectory SFT followed by rubric-guided GRPO rewarding evidence-informed criterion coverage and report quality.
zqJkXM0xmu.key_idea: Converts intermediate multimodal research traces and artifacts into source-linked rubrics that supply process and outcome rewards for GRPO post-training.
zqJkXM0xmu.evidence: Built on Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct and evaluated on MMDeepResearch-Bench, DeepResearch-Bench II, and MiroEval-Multimodal, plus an inter-annotator error-attribution study.
zqJkXM0xmu.claimed_gains: Improves the Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct base agent by 4.85, 3.54, and 4.91 points on MMDeepResearch-Bench, DeepResearch-Bench II, and MiroEval-Multimodal, respectively, and reduces primary Grounding Drift incidence from 30.7% to 17.1% on MMDeepResearch-Bench.
zqJkXM0xmu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the clear operationalization of Grounding Drift as a trajectory-level failure mode and the end-to-end diagnosis-to-post-training loop.
zqJkXM0xmu.main_concern: Reviewers warn that lexical and URL-presence rubric evaluators can be satisfied without true semantic claim-source entailment (e.g., under entity-source swaps), and note limited novelty and regressions in presentation and instruction following.

zrAGERhIvv.one_liner: Trains an online RL policy directly on a shared one-step Flow Transformer world-model backbone using next-latent prediction and rollout training.
zrAGERhIvv.problem: Diffusion-based online RL agents treat world models as slow black-box simulators and train separate policy networks without reusing world-model representations.
zrAGERhIvv.method: DRIFT trains an online RL agent from scratch whose policy learns entirely in imagination on the same compact continuous-latent Flow Transformer backbone as its world model. It adds a reconstruction-free next-latent prediction loss for control representations, trains the world model on its own rollouts to stabilize reward prediction, and uses shortcut flow matching for one-step imagination.
zrAGERhIvv.key_idea: Shares a one-step shortcut Flow Transformer backbone between imagination and control by adding a next-latent prediction objective and training on self-generated rollouts.
zrAGERhIvv.evidence: Evaluated online from scratch on Craftium, Crafter, and Atari 100k against diffusion, flow, and discrete latent-dynamics agents (such as DIAMOND and STORM) with component ablations.
zrAGERhIvv.claimed_gains: Uses 33x fewer FLOPs per imagined transition than prior diffusion-based agents while outperforming diffusion and flow baselines on Craftium and Crafter.
zrAGERhIvv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the efficient one-step imagination, useful diagnostics showing denoising features alone are poor for control, and ablations supporting next-latent and self-rollout training.
zrAGERhIvv.main_concern: Reviewers note that the shared-backbone claim is never directly tested against a separate-policy encoder over the same world model, and question novelty over DreamerV3 and existing components.

sfTjORT74p.one_liner: Expands phrase queries into multi-instance grounding slots and uses a frozen grounding head as an annotation-free RL verifier for video captioning.
sfTjORT74p.problem: Grounded video captioning pipelines flow one way without feeding grounding evidence back to the captioner, and single-trajectory grounding heads fail to verify plural phrases.
sfTjORT74p.method: The authors add a Multi-Instance Adapter that expands each phrase query into multiple persistent evidence slots for structured multi-instance localization. They then run annotation-free visual self-alignment via KL-regularized policy optimization using instance-presence and temporal-consistency rewards from a frozen copy of the grounding head.
sfTjORT74p.key_idea: Upgrades phrase grounding with multi-instance persistent evidence slots and reuses a frozen grounding head to provide instance-presence and temporal-consistency RL rewards during training.
sfTjORT74p.evidence: Evaluated on iGround, VidSTG, and ActivityNet-Entities against GROVE and other baselines, with ablations over slot count, matching, and orthogonality.
sfTjORT74p.claimed_gains: On iGround, the Multi-Instance Adapter raises AP50 from 40.0 to 51.7 over GROVE, and the full self-aligned model reaches 53.3 AP50 and 88.0 CIDEr.
sfTjORT74p.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the Multi-Instance Adapter delivers a substantial, well-ablated grounding improvement, especially on non-singular phrases.
sfTjORT74p.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the closed-loop verification only operates as a training reward (not at inference) and question whether objectness and box-overlap rewards actually verify counts, actions, or relations.

KgptZnvKUY.one_liner: Performs flow matching on multilevel discrete wavelet coefficients using a channel-token transformer and learnable orthonormal wavelets.
KgptZnvKUY.problem: Time-series generative models struggle to jointly reproduce multi-scale temporal structure and cross-channel dependencies in multivariate signals.
KgptZnvKUY.method: The authors apply flow matching in the multilevel discrete wavelet domain per channel, separating coarse trends from fine details across decomposition levels. A channel-token transformer parameterizes the velocity field so attention operates directly across channels, paired with learnable orthonormal wavelets parameterized via paraunitary lattice factorization.
KgptZnvKUY.key_idea: Learn a channel-token transformer velocity field via flow matching over per-channel multilevel discrete wavelet coefficients with optional paraunitary learnable orthonormal filters.
KgptZnvKUY.evidence: Compared against five generative baselines (four diffusion, one flow-matching) across seven multivariate time-series datasets and multiple sequence lengths, with time-domain and wavelet ablations.
KgptZnvKUY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the wavelet flow-matching architecture is simple, intuitive, and achieves strong empirical results across datasets at sequence length 24.
KgptZnvKUY.main_concern: Novelty over prior transformed-domain time-series diffusion methods is limited, and because DWT is orthonormal, the paper lacks deeper insight into why wavelet-domain flow matching helps.

mwWGvcZwZX.one_liner: Anchors flow matching on a Koopman-autoencoder forecast with tunable source variance to emulate forced chaotic dynamical systems.
mwWGvcZwZX.problem: Deterministic neural operators suffer spectral bias and drift in long chaotic rollouts, while standard Gaussian-source generative emulators require many solver steps to rebuild global structure.
mwWGvcZwZX.method: KoopFM pairs a forcing-aware Koopman-autoencoder base predictor with base-anchored flow matching whose source distribution is centered on the deterministic forecast rather than isotropic Gaussian noise. Tuning the source variance sigma prevents degeneracy and controls transport path length and correction range.
mwWGvcZwZX.key_idea: Replace the Gaussian flow-matching source with a noise distribution centered on a Koopman-autoencoder forecast, using source variance to govern residual transport distance.
mwWGvcZwZX.evidence: Evaluated on long autoregressive rollouts across three chaotic dynamical systems (including Kolmogorov flow and Rayleigh-Benard convection noted in reviews) under varying and out-of-distribution forcing.
mwWGvcZwZX.claimed_gains: Whenever the one-step conditional is narrow, inference requires as few as two NFEs without distillation.
mwWGvcZwZX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that anchoring flow matching on a deterministic forecast is intuitive, reduces NFEs effectively, and is backed by thorough rollout and forcing ablations.
mwWGvcZwZX.main_concern: Forecast-centered residual generative modeling closely overlaps with existing predictor-corrector and residual diffusion/flow methods, and the efficiency mechanism is not cleanly isolated from conditioning changes.

ZwyLuQBVDc.one_liner: Localizes a parameter subspace to suppress designated visual-to-knowledge associations in multimodal reasoning models while preserving text access.
ZwyLuQBVDc.problem: Existing multimodal unlearning methods erase entire concepts or allow forgotten visual-keyed information to leak through intermediate reasoning traces or be replaced by hallucinated identities.
ZwyLuQBVDc.method: Visual-Keyed Counterfactual Rebinding (VKCR) formulates cross-modal association unlearning to block target retrieval only under a designated visual context while retaining the same knowledge in permitted contexts. It localizes parameter edits to a compact association-conditioned subspace and suppresses target support across task outputs and reasoning.
ZwyLuQBVDc.key_idea: Isolate an association-conditioned parameter subspace to suppress designated visual-to-knowledge access across answers and reasoning traces while preserving text-only knowledge access.
ZwyLuQBVDc.evidence: Evaluated on multimodal unlearning benchmarks (CLEAR-R and MLLMU-R with LLaVA-1.5-7B mentioned in reviews) with text-access, on-key/off-key, and perturbation controls.
ZwyLuQBVDc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distinguishing knowledge erasure from visual-association suppression and separating leakage from hallucinated reassociation is a useful framing.
ZwyLuQBVDc.main_concern: Evidence of true relation-level removal is incomplete, lacking stronger adversarial or relearning probes, paired relation-selectivity tests, and baselines combining existing modality-selective and reasoning-trace unlearning.

QqTpTgiGDz.one_liner: Pretrains a 3.88M-parameter weather-conditioned foundation model with separate observation/weather streams and solar-geometry embeddings for zero-shot PV forecasting.
QqTpTgiGDz.problem: Existing photovoltaic power forecasters are site-specific and generalize poorly to new plants, while general time-series foundation models underperform on short-horizon high-resolution PV forecasting.
QqTpTgiGDz.method: PVFM is a 3.88M-parameter foundation model that separates historical PV observations and future weather covariates into dedicated streams augmented with solar-geometry and static identity embeddings. Pretrained on 59.2M global PV observations, it is evaluated zero-shot across horizons and optionally extended via multimodal fine-tuning with satellite imagery.
QqTpTgiGDz.key_idea: Separates historical PV and future weather covariate streams with solar-geometry embeddings, pretrained globally on 59.2M observations and optionally adapted with a satellite-imagery adapter.
QqTpTgiGDz.evidence: Pretrained on 59.2M observations across 845 global sites and evaluated on five zero-shot forecasting tasks at 1-hour and 15-minute resolutions plus ramp-event and satellite fine-tuning settings.
QqTpTgiGDz.claimed_gains: Across five zero-shot tasks, PVFM reduces MAE by 10.2–24.3% and CRPS by 10.0–29.5% over full-shot models and existing TSFMs, while satellite-image fine-tuning further cuts ultra-short-term RMSE by 9.1%.
QqTpTgiGDz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the large 845-site heterogeneous PV corpus, practical forecasting problem, and strong zero-shot comparisons against target-site full-shot baselines.
QqTpTgiGDz.main_concern: Reviewers warn of possible future-weather covariate leakage (since error stays nearly flat from 6h to 168h ahead), reliance on external NWP forecasts, and lack of a no-imagery control for satellite fine-tuning.

aVA0N6FwE3.one_liner: Couples affine continuous flows with absorbing discrete flow matching and anchor-distance regularization for unordered parametric CAD sketch generation.
aVA0N6FwE3.problem: Parametric 2D CAD sketch generators struggle to jointly preserve unordered primitive-set symmetry, unquantized geometric precision, and fast sampling.
aVA0N6FwE3.method: ParaSketchFM uses a permutation-equivariant Transformer to pair affine continuous geometric flows with absorbing categorical flow matching over type-indexed superposition slots, stabilized by type-probability gating and a one-sided cross-primitive anchor regularizer. A lightweight LoRA branch over the frozen backbone enables parallel partial-sketch completion.
aVA0N6FwE3.key_idea: Combines affine continuous geometric flows with absorbing discrete type flows in a permutation-equivariant Transformer, using type-probability gating and one-sided anchor regularization to prevent early mask contraction.
aVA0N6FwE3.evidence: Evaluated on SketchGraphs for unconditional generation, partial sketch completion, early-stage expansion, and FreeCAD solid extrusion against SketchDNN and continuous/discrete baselines.
aVA0N6FwE3.claimed_gains: On SketchGraphs, ParaSketchFM reaches 5.22 unconditional FID and 99.59% raw entity constructibility at 19.2x higher sampling throughput than SketchDNN, with 38.9% of unconditional sketches yielding valid FreeCAD extruded solids.
aVA0N6FwE3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper provides clear controlled comparisons of continuous, discrete, and joint CAD generation under a shared protocol with strong FID and constructibility gains.
aVA0N6FwE3.main_concern: Reviewers view the novelty over SketchDNN and prior continuous-discrete flow matching as incremental and question whether the anchor regularizer merely compensates for the chosen gating scheme.

LknY00DhzL.one_liner: Learns nonlinear latent corrections from short repeated self-reconstruction trajectories of a frozen autoencoder without test-time optimization.
LknY00DhzL.problem: Repeatedly applying a frozen autoencoder degrades reconstructions, while per-sample test-time latent optimization is computationally expensive.
LknY00DhzL.method: SRD-RR feeds short self-reconstruction trajectories from a frozen autoencoder into a learned corrector that predicts nonlinear latent refinements decoded by the unchanged decoder, plus an x-free variant trained on SRD pseudo-targets. The authors also define an MSE recovery ratio relative to an empirical decoder-optimized reference.
LknY00DhzL.key_idea: Extracts sample-specific refinement signals from short iterated re-encoding trajectories of a frozen autoencoder to predict nonlinear latent corrections in a single forward pass.
LknY00DhzL.evidence: Evaluated across six datasets, six higher-compression AE settings (6x–24x) including ImageNet100 and CIFAR-10, and 14 settings including pretrained RAE and KL-VAE against linear and trajectory-free controls.
LknY00DhzL.claimed_gains: Across six datasets, SRD-RR with two transitions improves PSNR by 2.01 dB on average and recovers 45.3% of the empirical MSE gap (40.7% for the x-free variant), recovering 52.2% on ImageNet100 and 19.0% on CIFAR-10 at 24x compression.
LknY00DhzL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question of extracting refinement signals from frozen autoencoder chains interesting, with thorough variants, ablations, and low inference cost.
LknY00DhzL.main_concern: Reviewers note that SRD-RR underperforms a simple image-space baseline (M4) on all six datasets, lacks clear positioning against classical van Cittert deconvolution and decoder inversion, and has undefined notations.

mZ5FPU21Em.one_liner: Places view selection, query-conditioned segmentation, and 3D render inspection under closed-loop VLM control for part-level Gaussian referring segmentation.
mZ5FPU21Em.problem: Two-stage referring segmentation methods on 3D Gaussian scenes select from fixed pre-generated object candidates, omitting fine-grained parts needed as targets or cues.
mZ5FPU21Em.method: SplatScout uses a VLM in a closed perception loop to actively choose views, direct query-conditioned segmentation, and inspect rendered 3D Gaussian results to iteratively refine predictions. The authors also introduce PartRef-ScanNet++, a benchmark of 261 verified queries across 12 ScanNet++ scenes with mesh-derived ground truth.
mZ5FPU21Em.key_idea: Replaces fixed precomputed candidate tables with a VLM-controlled closed loop that selects views, prompts part-level segmentation, and inspects 3D Gaussian renders iteratively.
mZ5FPU21Em.evidence: Evaluated on the new PartRef-ScanNet++ benchmark (261 queries, 12 scenes), four existing referring benchmarks, ablations on iterative refinement, and multiple VLM backbones.
mZ5FPU21Em.claimed_gains: On PartRef-ScanNet++, SplatScout achieves 0.538 mIoU (raising mIoU from 0.313 as stated in the TL;DR), outperforming existing methods on PartRef-ScanNet++ and four existing referring benchmarks.
mZ5FPU21Em.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that query-dependent part-level 3D grounding is a meaningful problem, PartRef-ScanNet++ is a useful benchmark, and SplatScout delivers strong grounding gains.
mZ5FPU21Em.main_concern: Reviewers criticize inaccurate positioning against existing dynamic-perception methods (TAB and OpenGround) and note that gains from query-conditioned SAM3 prompting are not separated from closed-loop VLM iteration.

scjqbURi3R.one_liner: Uses a persistent evidence graph to match equivalent visual-tool states across orders while preserving provenance for call-specific RL credit assignment.
scjqbURi3R.problem: Group-based RL for visual-tool agents assigns uniform trajectory-level credit or fails to match equivalent intermediate evidence when acquisition orders differ or identical values come from different regions.
scjqbURi3R.method: ProVIC maintains a persistent evidence graph that tracks both observation content and provenance across visual-tool calls so equivalent prior evidence can be matched regardless of acquisition order. It then uses matched final-answer rewards to compute call-specific advantages for each tool segment.
scjqbURi3R.key_idea: Matches intermediate visual-tool states via an order-invariant, provenance-preserving persistent evidence graph to compute call-specific RL advantages from final-answer rewards.
scjqbURi3R.evidence: Evaluated with Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct across five visual reasoning benchmarks and five paired training seeds against matched RL baselines.
scjqbURi3R.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that ProVIC identifies a genuine mismatch in visual-tool RL credit assignment and designs a well-motivated provenance-aware matching rule with consistent gains on the tested model.
scjqbURi3R.main_concern: Reviewers flag that experiments use only a single 8B model (Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct) with a structured-provenance executor and do not report how often calls match locally versus falling back to trajectory-level GRPO.

dPWRB9Gmof.one_liner: Systematically evaluates 10 model-pool pruning strategies across 39 LLMs, 27 benchmarks, and six router families to study routing quality-cost trade-offs.
dPWRB9Gmof.problem: LLM routing research focuses primarily on router algorithms while neglecting how the composition of the underlying candidate model pool governs quality-cost trade-offs.
dPWRB9Gmof.method: The authors evaluate 10 model-pool pruning strategies across 39 models, 27 benchmark tasks, and six router families, measuring both utility retention and budget coverage after retraining routers on pruned pools. They compare pool-composition effects against router choice and test cross-task transfer of pruned pools.
dPWRB9Gmof.key_idea: Audits LLM routing by pruning candidate model pools with 10 strategies and retraining routers to separate pool-composition effects from router-choice effects across quality and budget metrics.
dPWRB9Gmof.evidence: Empirical study spanning 10 pruning strategies, 27 benchmark tasks, 39 distinct LLMs, and six router families, including unseen-task transfer experiments.
dPWRB9Gmof.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical focus on model-pool construction, broad coverage of models and routers, and separation of utility retention from budget coverage.
dPWRB9Gmof.main_concern: Reviewers challenge the claimed 11–18x importance ratio of pool choice over router choice as an artifact of including poor pruning configurations while excluding random routers, and note overlap with prior findings.

v9HvWPqhbp.one_liner: Introduces CrossFly, a 15K-trajectory indoor-outdoor UAV simulation benchmark and Interaction Readiness Rate metric linking aerial navigation to manipulation.
v9HvWPqhbp.problem: Existing aerial navigation benchmarks restrict evaluation to single environments and initialize manipulation near targets, leaving cross-domain navigation-to-interaction transitions unmeasured.
v9HvWPqhbp.method: CrossFly provides 15K long-horizon trajectories across over 20 reconstructed scenes spanning Indoor, Outdoor, and Indoor-Outdoor transitions in a unified simulator, alongside a CrossFly-Agent baseline. It defines Interaction Readiness Rate (IRR) to evaluate whether terminal UAV poses satisfy distance and yaw conditions for downstream manipulation.
v9HvWPqhbp.key_idea: Benchmarks cross-domain indoor-outdoor UAV navigation toward manipulation readiness via a 15K-trajectory simulator and a policy-agnostic terminal pose metric (IRR).
v9HvWPqhbp.evidence: Contains 15K trajectories across >20 reconstructed scenes evaluated with five aerial VLA agents, CrossFly-Agent, and a downstream manipulation case study.
v9HvWPqhbp.claimed_gains: In Indoor-Outdoor settings on unseen scenes, the highest navigation success rate among evaluated agents reaches 9.7%.
v9HvWPqhbp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that bridging long-horizon indoor-outdoor aerial navigation with downstream manipulation readiness fills a meaningful evaluation gap.
v9HvWPqhbp.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the IRR metric as incomplete (omitting elevation angle, visibility, and embodiment constraints) and lacking quantitative validation of its predictive power for actual manipulation success.

r0UAb9KaIL.one_liner: Linearizes the downstream forward pass between a specific source and recipient token to decode query-conditioned concept transport in diffusion language models.
r0UAb9KaIL.problem: Existing vocabulary lenses decode intermediate states directly or apply globally averaged downstream maps, obscuring what a specific source token contributes to a specific recipient in a given forward pass.
r0UAb9KaIL.method: The Contextual Cross-Jacobian (CCJ) lens linearizes the remaining computation from one source position to one recipient position in the current forward pass, transports the source state through this local Jacobian map, and decodes via the model's unembedding. The authors evaluate concept localization, denoising trajectories, and label-free activation binding swaps.
r0UAb9KaIL.key_idea: Computes execution-specific source-to-recipient local Jacobians to transport and unembed intermediate states rather than using globally averaged lens maps.
r0UAb9KaIL.evidence: Evaluated on Dream and LLaDA diffusion language models plus a matched autoregressive model using target-blind multihop recovery, denoising-step tracking, and activation-only two-way binding swaps across 100 disjoint splits.
r0UAb9KaIL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distinguishing route-specific from globally averaged transport is conceptually valuable and appreciate the careful disjoint splits, bootstrap intervals, and causal controls.
r0UAb9KaIL.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over J/R-lenses, low absolute target-blind recovery (P@10 <= 14.5%), missing baselines designed for route-specific readout, and presentation issues.

ZK8VdGhlft.one_liner: Coordinates six objective-specialized editing agents via shared editorial state, visual verification, and beam search to turn hour-scale videos into montages.
ZK8VdGhlft.problem: Existing agentic video editing systems organize decisions by tool or stage, leaving dependencies among narrative alignment, musical pacing, and visual quality implicit.
ZK8VdGhlft.method: CutMaster uses a request-independent material analyst to build reusable video memory and five request-conditioned agents sharing an editorial state to align music slots, story anchors, and visually verified clip candidates via beam search and bounded replanning. The authors also introduce MontageX-Bench with 40 tasks across four intents and three domains.
ZK8VdGhlft.key_idea: Factorizes hour-scale montage editing across six objective-specialized agents coordinated through a shared editorial state with visual verification, beam-search composition, and bounded replanning.
ZK8VdGhlft.evidence: Evaluated on the 40-task MontageX-Bench against five baselines using automated narrative, pacing, and visual-quality metrics plus a human evaluation study.
ZK8VdGhlft.claimed_gains: On MontageX-Bench, CutMaster achieves a Quality score of 81.40 compared with 75.55 for the strongest of five baselines.
ZK8VdGhlft.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that hour-scale music-conditioned video montage editing is a challenging, practical task and that CutMaster's six-role workflow produces strong benchmark and human-study results.
ZK8VdGhlft.main_concern: Reviewers flag uncontrolled baseline comparisons (differing model backbones, compute budgets, and rendering policies), incremental novelty over CutClaw, and incomplete component ablations.

pgXNS4eMwy.one_liner: Decomposes skill rollouts into factor-specific state changes and optimizes an LLM-preference-conditioned mutual-information objective for unsupervised skill discovery.
pgXNS4eMwy.problem: Unsupervised skill discovery methods maximize distinguishability or diversity, often producing easily separated behaviors that lack behavioral significance for downstream tasks.
pgXNS4eMwy.method: Preference-Conditioned Skill Discovery (PCSD) decomposes skill executions into factor-specific behavioral changes and uses pretrained LLM preferences learned per factor to weight skill significance. It optimizes a preference-conditioned mutual-information objective with a variational interpretation to prioritize consequential skills.
pgXNS4eMwy.key_idea: Weights factorized state-change skill discovery with per-factor LLM preference models inside a preference-conditioned mutual-information objective.
pgXNS4eMwy.evidence: Supported by a variational derivation of the preference-conditioned MI objective and downstream task evaluations across multiple RL environments against unsupervised skill discovery baselines.
pgXNS4eMwy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that incorporating LLM preferences into unsupervised skill discovery is a sensible direction with clear empirical gains over the tested baselines and a helpful MI derivation.
pgXNS4eMwy.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the unfair comparison against non-LLM baselines while omitting closely related LLM/preference-guided skill discovery methods (HaSD, LGSD, CDP), limiting demonstrated novelty.

ak3T1NDptl.one_liner: Uses error-geometry-driven sparse gating over specialized modules to combine immediate reactive motor corrections with slow synaptic consolidation.
ak3T1NDptl.problem: How biological and artificial sensorimotor controllers simultaneously achieve rapid online error correction and slower long-term adaptation remains unclear.
ak3T1NDptl.method: Mixture-of-Microzones (MoM) sparsely recruits specialized modules based on sensory-error direction and magnitude to perform local state-conditioned coordinate transformations from sensory-error space to motor space. The same geometric gate applies immediate corrections directly to controller outputs while directing slower learning updates to consolidate responses.
ak3T1NDptl.key_idea: Shares an error-geometry sparse gate across specialized coordinate-transform modules to drive both immediate direct motor corrections and targeted slow synaptic updates.
ak3T1NDptl.evidence: Evaluated on sensorimotor adaptation tasks with component ablations, comparisons to controller-adapter baselines, biological neuron tuning comparisons, and a learned-optimization generalization test.
ak3T1NDptl.claimed_gains: In sensorimotor adaptation, MoM reduces adaptation time by approximately fourfold relative to ablated variants.
ak3T1NDptl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that MoM is an intuitive, clearly presented cerebellar-inspired architecture combining fast correction and slow adaptation with strong behavioral error-reduction results.
ak3T1NDptl.main_concern: Reviewers question whether MoM actually speeds up lasting learning rather than just fast direct correction (noting slower internalization in Table 2) and ask for stronger positioning against prior cerebellar models.

VYQEYhFfMj.one_liner: Replaces additive Transformer residual updates with a gated rank-1 delta rule that reads, compares, and overwrites state along learned directions.
VYQEYhFfMj.problem: Standard additive Transformer residual updates lack a direct primitive to read, compare, and selectively overwrite existing residual-stream content.
VYQEYhFfMj.method: Deep Delta Learning (DDL) applies the delta rule across network depth: each layer reads the residual state along a learned direction, compares it against a learned target, and writes a gated rank-1 correction along that direction. It supports both standard vector states and expanded multi-channel value states while keeping attention and MLP widths unchanged.
VYQEYhFfMj.key_idea: Updates Transformer residual streams via a gated rank-1 read-compare-overwrite delta rule along learned directions, interpolating smoothly between identity and exact overwrite.
VYQEYhFfMj.evidence: Pretrained decoder-only models at roughly GPT-2 small and medium scales on FineWeb-Edu, comparing scalar and expanded DDL variants against an additive residual baseline.
VYQEYhFfMj.claimed_gains: At GPT-2 small and medium scales on FineWeb-Edu, the best expanded DDL variants increase average one-shot accuracy by 0.91 and 1.18 points over the additive baseline while lowering validation loss.
VYQEYhFfMj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that DDL is a clean, simple, well-defined residual update mechanism with consistent validation-loss reductions across both tested model scales.
VYQEYhFfMj.main_concern: All three reviewers emphasize the lack of controlled baselines isolating the delta erase-write rule from learned gating (e.g., Highway/ReZero) or write-only updates, plus single-seed training and slower compute-matched speed.

oHxqXXdQh1.one_liner: Extracts a low-dimensional functional core from safety-tuning weight updates to diagnose downstream alignment erosion and guide minimal safety-preserving corrections.
oHxqXXdQh1.problem: The parameter-space geometry of safety tuning and how subsequent downstream fine-tuning erodes learned safety remain poorly understood.
oHxqXXdQh1.method: The authors analyze safety-tuning parameter updates to identify a behaviorally compressible functional core despite broad spectral energy, tracking how downstream fine-tuning accumulates opposing in-core displacement. They then use a safety-memory loss restricted to this core subspace to apply minimal corrective adjustments to downstream updates.
oHxqXXdQh1.key_idea: Identifies a low-dimensional functional core of safety-tuning weight updates and constrains corrective safety-memory updates to that subspace during downstream fine-tuning.
oHxqXXdQh1.evidence: Supported by spectral decomposition, signed behavioral interventions, and downstream fine-tuning mitigation experiments (including on Dolly) primarily on a GPT-2-based model adapting attention projections.
oHxqXXdQh1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper investigates an important alignment problem with clear organization, connecting parameter-space geometry directly to behavioral safety interventions.
oHxqXXdQh1.main_concern: Reviewers question generality because main dense-update experiments rely on a single GPT-2-based model adapting only attention projections and lack a comparison to ordinary task fine-tuning updates.

PHzJd1tMEr.one_liner: Builds behavior graphs from agent skill documents augmented with ML predicates to mine sparse-weighted Horn rules for malicious skill detection.
PHzJd1tMEr.problem: Existing malicious agent-skill detectors do not learn interpretable detection rules from data, limiting both detection coverage and traceability.
PHzJd1tMEr.method: Skill Behavioral Rules (SBRs) extract a behavior graph from each skill document, augment it with ML predicates scoring text maliciousness, and mine Horn rules combining structural patterns with these predicates. Sparse logistic regression learns rule weights so each detection decomposes into matched rules and supporting graph evidence.
PHzJd1tMEr.key_idea: Mines Horn rules over skill behavior graphs augmented with ML text-maliciousness predicates and scores them with sparse logistic regression for traceable detection.
PHzJd1tMEr.evidence: Evaluated on 1,329 MalSkillBench test skills (excluding prompt-injection) against nine baseline configurations and tested cross-source on the ASM dataset.
PHzJd1tMEr.claimed_gains: On 1,329 MalSkillBench test skills, SBRs achieve 87.17% F1 and a 5.88% false positive rate, outperforming nine baseline configurations.
PHzJd1tMEr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that detecting malicious agent skills is important and praise SBR's structural interpretability, where scores decompose directly into matched behavioral rules and graph evidence.
PHzJd1tMEr.main_concern: Reviewers flag that script bodies are omitted from graph extraction (limiting code-injection coverage) and that MalSkillBench compares trained SBR against untrained off-the-shelf baselines while LLM baselines win on ASM.

cUpJd5MbpK.one_liner: Replaces greedy merging with top-down greedy splitting plus local breakpoint fine-tuning to achieve linear-time min-epsilon segmented regression.
cUpJd5MbpK.problem: Exact dynamic programming for min-epsilon segmented regression scales quadratically with dataset size, while recent greedy merge-and-fine-tune heuristics still run in log-linear time.
cUpJd5MbpK.method: The authors propose a top-down greedy splitting algorithm paired with local segment breakpoint fine-tuning to fit a k-segment piecewise-linear function minimizing residual sum of squares in linear time with respect to dataset size.
cUpJd5MbpK.key_idea: Uses top-down greedy segment splitting followed by local breakpoint fine-tuning to reduce segmented regression runtime from log-linear to linear in dataset size.
cUpJd5MbpK.evidence: Supported by complexity analysis and runtime/quality experiments on synthetic data and one real-world dataset compared against dynamic programming and the greedy merge-and-fine-tune baseline.
cUpJd5MbpK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the algorithm is simple, clearly written, linear in dataset size for fixed dimension and segment count, and empirically faster and more accurate than the merging heuristic.
cUpJd5MbpK.main_concern: All three reviewers view methodological novelty as limited—simply swapping merging for greedy splitting with an existing fine-tuning step—with no approximation guarantee and narrow empirical evaluation.

EyOzNleJZi.one_liner: Calibrates cross-round client update trajectories by region and uses FFT frequency evidence to softly reweight persistent poisoning in federated load forecasting.
EyOzNleJZi.problem: Persistent poisoning attacks in federated load forecasting accumulate small malicious updates across rounds that are masked by regional non-IID variation and missed by single-round defenses.
EyOzNleJZi.method: The authors introduce two persistent attacks (Hist-Residual and Profile-LIE) and FedRASR, a five-stage server-side defense that extracts compact update features, builds region-calibrated residual trajectories, computes FFT-based frequency scores, estimates client risk, and softly reweights updates.
EyOzNleJZi.key_idea: Constructs region-calibrated cross-round update residual trajectories and scores their FFT frequency signatures to estimate client risk and softly downweight poisoned updates.
EyOzNleJZi.evidence: Evaluated on four regional smart-meter collections with 1,200 clients across five seeds under Hist-Residual, Profile-LIE, and clean training with component ablations.
EyOzNleJZi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that persistent poisoning under regional non-IID heterogeneity in federated load forecasting is a meaningful problem and that regional residual calibration is a sensible idea.
EyOzNleJZi.main_concern: All three reviewers warn that both evaluated attacks use an odd/even-round alternating schedule tailored to FFT detection, while zero-filling ~80% of missing rounds confounds client participation with malicious frequency patterns.

ibW2ISqSsQ.one_liner: Maintains situational, trajectory, and failure-aware memory with applicability-based decision routing to adapt past experience in interactive LLM agents.
ibW2ISqSsQ.problem: Continual interactive agents fail to update world knowledge from interaction feedback and struggle to tell when retrieved historical trajectories actually apply to evolving states.
ibW2ISqSsQ.method: CWME stores Situational Knowledge, Action Trajectory Experience, and Failure-Aware Knowledge, adapting retrieved trajectory structures to current interactions rather than replaying them verbatim. An Experience-Guided Decision Router separates retrieval relevance from current-state applicability to choose direct reuse, lightweight verification, or fresh reasoning, updating memory from outcomes.
ibW2ISqSsQ.key_idea: Separates retrieval relevance from current-state applicability to route between trajectory adaptation, verification, and fresh reasoning while updating three structured experience memories from interaction outcomes.
ibW2ISqSsQ.evidence: Evaluated on two text-based interactive agent tasks with baseline comparisons and component ablations.
ibW2ISqSsQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem of distinguishing retrieval relevance from current-state applicability is practical and clearly formulated, with solid performance on the evaluated tasks.
ibW2ISqSsQ.main_concern: Reviewers criticize calling an editable LLM memory a 'world model' without learned transition prediction, note evaluation is restricted to discrete text environments, and question novelty over existing experience-memory agents.

BHbsr7Pc7T.one_liner: Projects centered multi-agent debate responses onto task-adaptive semantic probes to separate adversarial conflict direction from benign evidence-driven disagreement.
BHbsr7Pc7T.problem: Anomaly-based safeguards for multi-agent debate mistakenly isolate benign agents whose responses diverge due to heterogeneous private evidence rather than adversarial manipulation.
BHbsr7Pc7T.method: PDVC builds task-adaptive semantic probes from public task context and independent first-round responses, projects centered agent responses onto these probes to form discussion-relative conflict representations, and trains an agent-wise role readout to intervene in debate topology.
BHbsr7Pc7T.key_idea: Projects centered debate responses onto first-round task-adaptive semantic probes so low-rank adversarial conflict directions separate from benign evidence-driven disagreement.
BHbsr7Pc7T.evidence: Evaluated across four multi-hop reasoning benchmarks, diverse attack topologies (including majority-malicious settings), multiple LLM backbones, and multiple sentence encoders.
BHbsr7Pc7T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distinguishing benign private-evidence disagreement from adversarial deviation in multi-agent debate is a well-motivated problem backed by broad experimental coverage.
BHbsr7Pc7T.main_concern: Reviewers flag missing variance/seeds and inconsistent numbers across tables, lack of a simple first-round embedding classifier baseline, and no controlled sweep over evidence heterogeneity.

GDI9NHxRRX.one_liner: Benchmarks whether vision-language models adapt safety-critical object selections to stated jurisdictions across ten multi-convention object families.
GDI9NHxRRX.problem: Embodied vision-language models are evaluated on object recognition without testing whether they adapt when identical visual cues carry different safety meanings across jurisdictions.
GDI9NHxRRX.method: EMBRACE curates ten safety-relevant object families across healthcare, manufacturing, and retail where visual conventions vary by jurisdiction, using controlled image sets with jurisdiction prompts and label-shuffling tests. It also tests abstention when the locally correct object is absent.
GDI9NHxRRX.key_idea: Tests jurisdiction-conditioned visual grounding and abstention via label-shuffling perturbations across safety-critical object families whose color/visual conventions differ by country.
GDI9NHxRRX.evidence: Evaluated four vision-language models on 89 edited benchmark images spanning ten safety-relevant object families.
GDI9NHxRRX.claimed_gains: Shuffling jurisdiction labels within each object family preserves 64–82% of the four evaluated VLMs' original performance.
GDI9NHxRRX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jurisdiction-dependent safety semantics for visual cues is an underexplored, deployment-relevant failure mode for embodied VLMs.
GDI9NHxRRX.main_concern: Reviewers highlight the small scale and artificiality of 89 text-obscured edited images and note that the 64–82% shuffled-label retention metric is confounded by uneven convention distributions.

4axu6xjJUQ.one_liner: Measures nearest-neighbor overlap and ICA magnitude differences between paired texts to link embedding-space structure retention with MTEB benchmark performance.
4axu6xjJUQ.problem: Text embedding evaluation focuses on aggregate benchmark scores without explaining how high-performing models geometrically organize their embedding spaces beyond cosine similarity.
4axu6xjJUQ.method: The authors probe embedding spaces using nearest-neighbor overlap and independent component analysis (ICA) magnitude differences between paired text instances, comparing against target-shuffling and cosine-similarity controls across English and multilingual settings.
4axu6xjJUQ.key_idea: Quantifies local nearest-neighbor retention and ICA component magnitude alignment between paired embeddings to correlate geometric structure with downstream task scores.
4axu6xjJUQ.evidence: Evaluated 25 text embedding models (8M to 8B parameters) across five MTEB tasks spanning retrieval, bitext mining, pair classification, and summarization in English and multilingual settings.
4axu6xjJUQ.claimed_gains: Nearest-neighbor overlap and ICA magnitude differences between paired texts correlate with task performance up to 0.97.
4axu6xjJUQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the broad empirical scope across 25 embedding models, multiple MTEB task categories, and thoughtful controls like target shuffling and cosine baselines.
4axu6xjJUQ.main_concern: Reviewers note that the probes require paired data without showing an evaluation advantage over direct retrieval metrics, lack causal or mechanistic explanation for observed correlations, and suffer from disorganized paper structure.

iulhIv5sLI.one_liner: Ranks Verilog training examples by spectral-entropy reduction over specification-weighted AST structural spans between base and adapted models.
iulhIv5sLI.problem: Sequence-level loss or gradient data-selection methods do not measure whether an RTL Verilog example strengthens a model's representations of specification-relevant hardware structures.
iulhIv5sLI.method: Veri-eRank parses Verilog programs into AST-derived structural spans (declarations, assignments, event controls, control flow), weights spans by specification relevance, and measures spectral-entropy reduction from a base model to a reference-adapted model across resampled structural views.
iulhIv5sLI.key_idea: Selects RTL training examples that yield stable spectral-entropy reductions in specification-weighted AST span representations after reference adaptation.
iulhIv5sLI.evidence: Evaluated on six model-benchmark pairs over five seeds at a 20% data budget with ablations on instruction weighting, span resampling, and variance regularization.
iulhIv5sLI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that incorporating AST-derived RTL structure and instruction-conditioned weighting into spectral data selection is well-motivated and yields consistent gains at a 20% budget.
iulhIv5sLI.main_concern: Reviewers point out that running a full-dataset epoch of reference adaptation undermines the claimed data-efficiency savings, a random 20% training baseline is missing, and the 20% budget appears tuned on test benchmarks.

kcBJuzYd5g.one_liner: Uses an LLM and tabular foundation model to build iterative residual-state teacher representations distilled into a lightweight XGBoost student.
kcBJuzYd5g.problem: Trained tabular models exhibit systematic regional error patterns that are hard to fix by relearning residuals directly from raw features without incurring heavy inference costs.
kcBJuzYd5g.method: RECAST partitions out-of-fold XGBoost errors into three residual states; an LLM selects semantic feature subsets and focus conditions for in-context examples while a tabular foundation model estimates residual-state representations for a teacher predicting residual corrections. Out-of-fold teacher predictions are blended with true labels to distill a single inference-only XGBoost student on original features.
kcBJuzYd5g.key_idea: Distills iterative LLM- and tabular-foundation-model-estimated residual-state teacher corrections into a standalone XGBoost student that uses only raw features at inference.
kcBJuzYd5g.evidence: Evaluated across 50 tabular datasets from OpenML, TabArena, and TALENT against nine competing models and an external-validation-tuned XGBoost control.
kcBJuzYd5g.claimed_gains: Across 50 datasets, RECAST ranks second among ten models with an overall average rank of 4.14 and beats base XGBoost in mean test performance on every dataset.
kcBJuzYd5g.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the clean nested cross-fitting protocol and the practical goal of removing foundation models at inference time via student distillation.
kcBJuzYd5g.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the modest ~2% average gain over base XGBoost stems from selecting the best of 25 students on an external validation set unseen by base XGBoost, alongside high training cost and weaker mean NRMSE/AUROC than TabM.

HC6RlhcCNI.one_liner: Adaptively splits layers per client in Stacked-Activation Split Federated Learning with warm-up and weight-shrinking stabilization.
HC6RlhcCNI.problem: Client resource and data heterogeneity in Split Federated Learning degrade latency and cause cross-layer update inconsistencies when clients use different split points.
HC6RlhcCNI.method: PyramidSFL dynamically selects each client's cut layer based on its compute and communication profile within Stacked-Activation SFL, and stabilizes optimization using an early warm-up phase and a layer-wise weight-shrinking mechanism.
HC6RlhcCNI.key_idea: Assign per-client adaptive cut layers by resource profile while counteracting unequal server-layer update frequencies through warm-up and layer-wise weight shrinking.
HC6RlhcCNI.evidence: Evaluated on real-world benchmarks against FL and SFL baselines using simulated client profiles on NVIDIA A40/A100 GPUs, accompanied by fixed-cut convergence analysis.
HC6RlhcCNI.claimed_gains: Improves global model accuracy by up to 15.53% under the same wall-clock budget and reduces convergence latency by up to 72.86% over FL and SFL baselines.
HC6RlhcCNI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that identifying and addressing the conflict between client-specific dynamic splitting and cross-layer optimization stability is practical and yields strong accuracy-latency gains.
HC6RlhcCNI.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over prior adaptive-splitting and weight-shrinking methods, missing adaptive-splitting baselines, modeled rather than real-device latency, and convergence theory limited to fixed cuts.
